api/DBTools.Core.Failure.FailureReport.h.title: Class FailureReport | DB Tools
api/DBTools.Core.Failure.FailureReport.h.summary: Class FailureReport Namespace DBTools.Core.Failure Assembly DBTools.Core.dll Shows each failure once. A handler that shows a failure banner records it with the exception; an outer handler that receives the same exception only logs it. The banner system keeps every request it accepts (see NotificationBannerService), so a request counts as shown when it is made. public static class FailureReport Inheritance object FailureReport Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The outermost SafeExecutor run of an asynchronous flow opens a report scope; nested runs use its records. A run that rethrows to its caller hands its record on to the window error boundary, which takes it once. A later run ignores and removes a record that another run handed on, so a failure its caller cached and throws again is shown again. Tool code that shows its own banner and rethrows records the failure for its next handler. Methods ShowBanner(IWindowErrorBanner, Exception, string, string) Shows a failure banner and records it, for tool code that rethrows the failure afterwards. public static void ShowBanner(IWindowErrorBanner notifier, Exception failure, string title, string message) Parameters notifier IWindowErrorBanner failure Exception title string message string TakeShown(Exception) For a last handler that would show its own banner: returns true, and takes the record, when an earlier handler already showed this failure. public static bool TakeShown(Exception failure) Parameters failure Exception Returns bool

On the owner dispatcher's thread, owner resolution and presentation finish before return. Their exceptions propagate to the caller. Other threads queue delivery and return immediately. Delivery failures are logged without propagating to the caller. Dispatcher selection can throw on any thread. A zero owner HWND, missing anchor position, retired host or host reset suppresses presentation and returns an inert handle. A returned handle therefore does not confirm presentation. Disposing the handle before delivery cancels presentation. Rows use these default deadlines: success 3 s, info 5 s, warning 8 s, error 10 s. Prompts have no automatic deadline. Rows with actions use their kind's deadline too; a successful action can close one early when CloseOnSuccess is true (the default). A running action defers expiry, requested dismissal and last-handle release until it finishes. A request with the same key as an open row updates that row. Without a key, a request updates an open row only when kind, title, message and action presence match. An update restarts its deadline when the kind has one; an exact repeat shows a count. api/DBTools.Core.Revit.Execution.CallGat.summary: Interface IRevitCallGate Namespace DBTools.Core.Revit.Execution.CallGate Assembly DBTools.Core.dll Unified entry point for executing Revit API callbacks either inline (modal) or queued (modeless). public interface IRevitCallGate Remarks Null work delegates and rejected delegate shapes throw from the call itself. Failures after argument validation, including cancellation, mode or context refusal, callback failure, and erased awaitable-result rejection, are delivered through the returned task. Cancellation completes the task as Canceled. An OperationCanceledException thrown by a gate check or work delegate is rethrown; cancellation observed by the queued host surfaces as a TaskCanceledException. Properties InGate True when currently executing within a call-gate callback on the Revit UI thread. bool InGate { get; } Property Value bool RunsInline True when every accepted callback runs synchronously inside the calling API turn. bool RunsInline { get; } Property Value bool Remarks This is a fixed property of the gate. It grants no Revit API authority and does not describe the current InGate state. Methods RunAsync(Action<UIApplication>, CancellationToken, RevitCallGateMode) Executes the work delegate on the Revit UI thread. Null work and async-state-machine Action delegates throw from the call before execution. Task RunAsync(Action<UIApplication> work, CancellationToken ct = default, RevitCallGateMode mode = RevitCallGateMode.Auto) Parameters work Action<UIApplication> ct CancellationToken mode RevitCallGateMode Returns Task Remarks Queued work that has not started when the owning call-gate task retires is dropped, and its task never completes, even if its cancellation token is canceled later. Callers must not await or block on such a task during shutdown. Failed-startup cleanup cancels pending work instead. RunAsync<T>(Func<UIApplication, T>, CancellationToken, RevitCallGateMode) Executes the work delegate on the Revit UI thread and returns a result. Task<T> RunAsync<T>(Func<UIApplication, T> work, CancellationToken ct = default, RevitCallGateMode mode = RevitCallGateMode.Auto) Parameters work Func<UIApplication, T> ct CancellationToken mode RevitCallGateMode Returns Task<T> Type Parameters T Remarks Task and ValueTask result shapes and reference-typed multicast result delegates throw from the call before execution. An erased Task or boxed ValueTask result (for example, a Task returned as object or an interface) is rejected only after the work runs. Its side effects remain, and any started Task continues running. Other awaitable types (for example, ConfigureAwait results and custom awaiters) are not detected. Queued work that has not started when the owning call-gate task retires is dropped, and its task never completes, even if its cancellation token is canceled later. Callers must not await or block on such a task during shutdown. Failed-startup cleanup cancels pending work instead.

api/DBTools.Core.Revit.Execution.CallGat.summary: Class RevitCallGateTask Namespace DBTools.Core.Revit.Execution.CallGate Assembly DBTools.Core.dll Owns one ExternalEvent and its FIFO work queue for one App service root. public sealed class RevitCallGateTask : IRevitCallGateTask, IExternalEventHandler, IDisposable, IAsyncDisposable Inheritance object RevitCallGateTask Implements IRevitCallGateTask IExternalEventHandler IDisposable IAsyncDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Each native Execute runs the work that was queued when it started, in order, until the DBTools.Core.Revit.Execution.CallGate.RevitCallGateTask.s_drainBudget is used. Work queued during the turn, or left by the budget, waits for the next raise, which is posted to the dispatcher and so runs after Execute returns. Revit discards what a callback leaves open only when the callback returns. A call ends the turn when it leaves a transaction open in any document, or when it creates a transaction group, which every production group owner reports through DBTools.Core.Revit.Execution.CallGate.RevitCallGateTurnBoundary. No later call of the turn then runs inside state that an earlier call left open. Every raise is posted, also from the dispatcher thread, so a caller never waits on native Raise. Turn timing is logged at Debug level, throttled by DBTools.Core.Revit.Execution.CallGate.RevitCallGateTurnStatistics. Retirement drops queued delegates and registrations without completing their tasks. Such tasks never finish: a worker synchronously waiting on one would remain blocked. Callers must use asynchronous lifetimes and must not wait for retired work during shutdown. Failed-startup cleanup uses CancelPending instead, so callers in the live process observe cancellation. api/DBTools.Core.Revit.SharedParameters..summary: Class SharedParameterFamilyMigration Namespace DBTools.Core.Revit.SharedParameters Assembly DBTools.Core.dll Replaces, in the loaded families of a project, each shared family parameter that has the name of a target and another GUID with the target, reloads each changed family into the project and keeps every value. public sealed class SharedParameterFamilyMigration Inheritance object SharedParameterFamilyMigration Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A loaded family keeps its own definition of a shared parameter. Its formulas, dimension labels and annotation labels refer to the parameter by GUID, so a project that replaces its own parameter leaves them on the old GUID. Deleting that parameter from the project also removes it from the labels of loaded families. Callers therefore run this migration before Migrate(Document, ParameterElement, ExternalDefinition, IReadOnlyCollection<Category>, SharedParameterUseHandling) or any delete of the old parameter. Plan(Document, IReadOnlyList<SharedParameterFamilyTarget>) changes nothing. When the project has a parameter with the name of a target and another GUID, it opens every editable loadable family (Autodesk.Revit.DB.Document.EditFamily(Autodesk.Revit.DB.Family)) and closes it unsaved. It opens editable nested families recursively. It does not open a non-editable nested family; it checks its symbols and instances for the GUID. A carrier parameter can proceed when those elements do not show the GUID. A direct-use path refuses when any non-editable nested family could hide a label, formula or other use. A family parameter with the name and another GUID becomes a change. A use that is not a family parameter is refused: a label that shows the parameter directly (added through Edit Label in a tag or title block family) or a nested family that defines it. Revit 2027 names each such label with its detail group and formatting. Revit 2026 refuses every direct shared-parameter element because it cannot read labels. It describes an annotation-family element as an unread label, and does not call a model-family element an annotation label. Other refusals: a nested shared family, another data type, a type parameter in a category that the target binds as an instance parameter, an element whose old and new values differ, and an in-place or non-editable top-level family that defines the parameter or may define it. Revit does not open such a family; when its elements show the parameter and a project binding could explain that, the plan rebinds the project parameter without the family's category in a transaction that always rolls back and reads the elements again. Migrate(Document, SharedParameterFamilyPlan) runs in one transaction group. For each family it records the old values of its types or elements, opens the family, replaces the parameter through a temporary family parameter (FamilyManager.ReplaceParameter(FamilyParameter, string, ForgeTypeId, bool), then the target definition) with the same group and instance or type kind, and checks in the family that every formula, value, dimension label, associated element parameter and, in Revit 2027, label follows. It also checks for a remaining family parameter, nested-family symbol or instance, or readable label that uses the old GUID. Project view-filter rules are handled by FindFilterRules(Document, ParameterElement) when the project parameter is deleted. An unused Autodesk.Revit.DB.SharedParameterElement may remain after replacement. In Revit 2026 it refuses an annotation family when that element remains because the family may use the GUID in a label that DB Tools cannot read. It reloads the family over the loaded one, writes each recorded value that the reload did not keep and reads every value back. Any refusal or failure rolls the group back; the project keeps its families and values. Family files on disk do not change. A family loaded again from such a file brings the old GUID back. api/DBTools.Core.Revit.SharedParameters..summary: Class SharedParameterMigration Namespace DBTools.Core.Revit.SharedParameters Assembly DBTools.Core.dll Replaces a project parameter with a shared parameter of another GUID, binds an unbound shared parameter, or rebinds a shared parameter as an instance parameter of more categories, and carries over every value. public sealed class SharedParameterMigration Inheritance object SharedParameterMigration Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Both operations change the project only when they can carry over every value. Before any change they plan one write per value: an instance-bound parameter keeps each element value; a type-bound parameter copies each type value to every instance of that type. A type value without an instance cannot be carried, so the call refuses. Migrate(Document, ParameterElement, ExternalDefinition, IReadOnlyCollection<Category>, SharedParameterUseHandling) also requires the source and target specs to match (ForgeTypeId.NameEquals). One transaction group then changes the binding, writes the values and reads each one back. Revit refuses a changed value on a member of a group placed more than once when the parameter does not vary between group instances, so such writes run with the variance on, the original variance comes back after them, and every value is read back again; a parameter that Revit does not let vary is refused. If any write or read-back fails, or any step throws, the group rolls back and the project keeps the original parameter, binding and values. A refusal or a rollback after failed writes throws SharedParameterMigrationException with every value that could not be carried; each is also logged. Migrate(Document, ParameterElement, ExternalDefinition, IReadOnlyCollection<Category>, SharedParameterUseHandling) deletes the source parameter. A loaded family that defines the source GUID keeps it in its own definition, and its labels and formulas then refer to a parameter the project no longer has; run SharedParameterFamilyMigration first. The target may already exist without a binding, because loaded families define it; the migration then binds it. Each source-bound element keeps the value that is not empty. The migration also records target-only values on elements in categories added to the binding, and restores them if binding changes them. Two different values refuse before any change. Bind(Document, SharedParameterElement, IReadOnlyCollection<Category>, ForgeTypeId) handles a shared parameter that already exists in the project but has no binding. It records values that loaded families expose in the categories to bind, binds the parameter as an instance parameter, restores values that binding changes, and reads them back. A placed family type parameter refuses when the repair needs an instance binding. An unplaced family type parameter stays on its type. CheckBind(Document, SharedParameterElement, IReadOnlyCollection<Category>, ForgeTypeId) runs the same plan without a lasting change. Every operation reads bindings through SharedParameterBindingLookup, so a dead key in Revit's binding map refuses it with SafeExecutionRefusedException before any change. A check that changes the project in a transaction that always rolls back (the group variance check, and the family ownership check of SharedParameterFamilyMigration) requires Revit to report the rollback. When Revit does not, or the rollback throws, the check throws SharedParameterRollbackException, a failure that is not a refusal. api/DBTools.Core.Revit.Transactions.ITra.title: Interface ITransactionRunner | DB Tools
api/DBTools.Core.Revit.Transactions.ITra.summary: Interface ITransactionRunner Namespace DBTools.Core.Revit.Transactions Assembly DBTools.Core.dll Runs synchronous work in a Revit transaction, or in a subtransaction when the target document already has an open transaction. public interface ITransactionRunner Remarks A rejected delegate shape throws InvalidOperationException from the call itself. Every other failure arrives through the returned task. The work runs synchronously inside one Revit API callback of the call gate. The token is checked before the transaction starts and before and after the work runs. Cancellation alone rolls back an open transaction and cancels the task without faulting it. An erased Task or boxed ValueTask result, for example a task returned as object, is rejected after the work runs, and the transaction rolls back. A start status other than Autodesk.Revit.DB.TransactionStatus.Started, or a commit status other than Autodesk.Revit.DB.TransactionStatus.Committed, raises TransactionFailureException. TransactionName and Status identify the transaction. For a transaction commit, Warnings lists the suppressed warnings, and BlockingFailures, BlockingFailureDefinitionIds and BlockingFailureDefinitionGuids describe the errors that blocked it. The GUIDs follow the IDs in order; Core does not classify them. An InvalidOperationException refuses a missing active document, a target document that differs from a modifiable active document, and a call that the gate cannot run in its context. A work or Revit exception propagates unchanged after cleanup. When the rollback or the disposal also fails, an AggregateException holds the first failure followed by the cleanup failures. A disposal failure after a commit propagates, and the commit stays. api/DBTools.Core.Revit.Transactions.Tran.summary: Class TransactionFailurePreprocessor Namespace DBTools.Core.Revit.Transactions Assembly DBTools.Core.dll Preprocessor that suppresses Revit warnings and prevents Revit's failure UI from surfacing. Warnings are deleted. Errors/fatal failures cause the transaction to roll back (no Revit dialogs) so DBTools can surface the error. public sealed class TransactionFailurePreprocessor : IFailuresPreprocessor, IDisposable Inheritance object TransactionFailurePreprocessor Implements IFailuresPreprocessor IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Revit holds a stable RevitCallbackRelay, not this object. Dispose() drops this object from the relay, so failure handling options that Revit keeps after the transaction cannot keep a Dev Mode generation alive. The failure records stay readable after Dispose(). Production code declares the preprocessor before its transaction (using var failures = new TransactionFailurePreprocessor();, then using var tx, then AttachTo(Transaction)), so the transaction is disposed, and rolled back if needed, before the preprocessor is released. Properties AccessorFaults public List<Exception> AccessorFaults { get; } Property Value List<Exception> BlockingFailureCount public int BlockingFailureCount { get; } Property Value int BlockingFailureDefinitionIds public List<FailureDefinitionId> BlockingFailureDefinitionIds { get; } Property Value List<FailureDefinitionId> BlockingFailureMessages public List<string> BlockingFailureMessages { get; } Property Value List<string> FailureRecords Every failure message read during commit, with its definition, failing elements and resolution. public List<TransactionFailureRecord> FailureRecords { get; } Property Value List<TransactionFailureRecord> LastResult public FailureProcessingResult LastResult { get; } Property Value FailureProcessingResult SuppressedWarningCount public int SuppressedWarningCount { get; } Property Value int SuppressedWarningMessages public List<string> SuppressedWarningMessages { get; } Property Value List<string> Methods AttachTo(Transaction) Attaches this preprocessor to an active transaction, once. public void AttachTo(Transaction tx) Parameters tx Transaction AttachToTransaction(Transaction) Creates a preprocessor and attaches it to an active transaction. Dispose it after the transaction is disposed. public static TransactionFailurePreprocessor AttachToTransaction(Transaction tx) Parameters tx Transaction Returns TransactionFailurePreprocessor Dispose() Drops this preprocessor from the relay that Revit holds. Call it after the transaction is disposed. public void Dispose() PreprocessFailures(FailuresAccessor) This method is called when there have been failures found at the end of a transaction and Revit is about to start processing them. public FailureProcessingResult PreprocessFailures(FailuresAccessor a) Parameters a FailuresAccessor Returns FailureProcessingResult Notifies end of transaction code about further actions required. Return values are interpreted as follows: Continue - the failure processing will continue. Failures will be shown to the user, even if they were addressed by this method. ProceedWithCommit - end of transaction checks and failure processing will restart from the beginning. If some failures were resolved here, they will be removed and not delivered to the user. ProceedWithCommit cannot be returned if transaction is being rolled back. ProceedWithRollBack - the failure processing will continue. Failures will be shown to the user, but user will have no option to resolve or ignore them - only cancel option will be available. If intent is to roll back transaction without showing failures to the user, it can be achieved by setting failure handling option to remove failures before returning ProceedWithRollBack. Other return values are not allowed.

api/DBTools.Core.Revit.Transactions.Tran.summary: Interface IAtomicTransactionGroup Namespace DBTools.Core.Revit.Transactions.TransactionGroup Assembly DBTools.Core.dll Runs work inside one transaction group within a single Revit API callback, so the group becomes exactly one Revit Undo entry. Revit rolls back a group that is still open when the callback that started it returns, so a group must never span call-gate calls. public interface IAtomicTransactionGroup Methods RunAsync<T>(string, Func<CancellationToken, Task<T>>, Func<T, bool>, CancellationToken) Begins the group on the active document, runs work, then assimilates the group when keep accepts the result and rolls it back otherwise. An exception, or cancellation seen at any point before finalization, rolls the group back and propagates. The work must complete within the callback: its call-gate calls run inline. A document with an open transaction is refused before any work. Unless Revit confirms the rollback, the call throws TransactionGroupOutcomeUnknownException. api/DBTools.Core.Revit.Transactions.Tran.summary: Interface ITransactionGroupService Namespace DBTools.Core.Revit.Transactions.TransactionGroup Assembly DBTools.Core.dll Groups the active document's transactions into one Revit undo entry through separate begin and finalize calls. public interface ITransactionGroupService Remarks Revit rolls back an open group when the API callback that started it returns. An owned group must therefore begin and finalize through inline call-gate execution within that same callback, as in a modal command. Queued modeless work uses RunAsync<T>(string, Func<CancellationToken, Task<T>>, Func<T, bool>, CancellationToken), whose outcome contract covers an unconfirmed rollback. On a document that is already modifiable, BeginAsync(string, CancellationToken) creates no owned group but sets IsActive, and finalization only resets that state. Failures arrive through the returned task, and cancellation cancels it. When cleanup also fails, an AggregateException holds the first failure followed by the cleanup failures. Properties IsActive Gets whether a group session is active, including the session without an owned group on a modifiable document. Finalization with a supported value resets it, also when finalization fails. bool IsActive { get; } Property Value bool Methods BeginAsync(string, CancellationToken) Begins a group session on the active document. Task BeginAsync(string name, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters name string ct CancellationToken Returns Task Remarks The task faults with InvalidOperationException when there is no active document or a session is already active, and with TransactionFailureException when an owned group does not reach Autodesk.Revit.DB.TransactionStatus.Started. FinalizeAsync(TransactionGroupFinalization, CancellationToken) Assimilates or rolls back the owned group, then resets the session. Task FinalizeAsync(TransactionGroupFinalization finalization, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters finalization TransactionGroupFinalization ct CancellationToken Returns Task Remarks An unsupported finalization value faults the task with ArgumentOutOfRangeException and leaves the session and its group unchanged. A supported value does nothing when no session is active. Commit expects Autodesk.Revit.DB.TransactionStatus.Committed and Rollback expects Autodesk.Revit.DB.TransactionStatus.RolledBack. Another status raises TransactionFailureException, unless a Revit exception from the assimilation or rollback is already the failure. IsGroupHealthyAsync(CancellationToken) Returns true without scheduling Revit work when no owned group exists. Otherwise returns whether the group status is Autodesk.Revit.DB.TransactionStatus.Started; false alone does not show that the group was rolled back. api/DBTools.Core.SafeExecution.Domain.IS.title: Interface ISafeExecutor | DB Tools
api/DBTools.Core.SafeExecution.Domain.IS.summary: Interface ISafeExecutor Namespace DBTools.Core.SafeExecution.Domain Assembly DBTools.Core.dll public interface ISafeExecutor Methods RunAsync(Func<Task>, ILogger, IBannerNotifier?, SafeExecutionOptions, CancellationToken) Runs action inside the safe-execution boundary, reports its outcome, and rethrows every outcome except success. Task RunAsync(Func<Task> action, ILogger logger, IBannerNotifier? notifier, SafeExecutionOptions opts, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters action Func<Task> logger ILogger notifier IBannerNotifier opts SafeExecutionOptions ct CancellationToken Returns Task Remarks The returned task completes normally only for Succeeded. A Refused, Canceled or Failed outcome is reported first and then rethrown. The rethrown exception is the instance that the action threw, with its original stack trace, unless a reporting stage failed and the outcome became an AggregateException. Reporting follows opts and needs a notifier for banners. An exception that an inner run already showed (FailureReport) is logged again, without a second banner or failure surface. A SafeExecutionRefusedException is Refused. It shows a warning banner, or writes a warning log entry when there is no notifier or banners are suppressed. It writes no exception diagnostics and uses no failure surface. Every OperationCanceledException is Canceled, also one that does not come from ct. It writes a warning log entry and shows no failure banner and no failure surface. A canceled ct stops the action before it starts. Any other exception is Failed. It is logged, shown in an error banner, and passed to the failure surface, as opts allows. The banner text is the exception message, or The operation failed. for a blank message. A success banner that throws makes the outcome Failed with that exception. A reporting failure makes an AggregateException with the operation's exception first and the reporting failure second. The stages run in this order: refusal reporting (the outcome is then Failed and takes the failure path), failure notification, failure surface. When more than one stage fails, each later aggregate holds the earlier one as its first inner exception. The outermost run hands its failure record to the caller's handler, such as the window error boundary. Exceptions ArgumentNullException action, logger or opts is null. The returned task faults with this exception; nothing is reported. RunWithoutThrowingAsync(Func<Task>, ILogger, IBannerNotifier?, SafeExecutionOptions, CancellationToken) Runs action with the reporting of RunAsync(Func<Task>, ILogger, IBannerNotifier?, SafeExecutionOptions, CancellationToken) and returns the outcome instead of rethrowing it. Task<SafeExecutionResult> RunWithoutThrowingAsync(Func<Task> action, ILogger logger, IBannerNotifier? notifier, SafeExecutionOptions opts, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters action Func<Task> logger ILogger notifier IBannerNotifier opts SafeExecutionOptions ct CancellationToken Returns Task<SafeExecutionResult> The outcome. Exception is null for success; otherwise it holds the exception that RunAsync(Func<Task>, ILogger, IBannerNotifier?, SafeExecutionOptions, CancellationToken) would rethrow. Exceptions ArgumentNullException action, logger or opts is null. The returned task faults with this exception; argument validation is not a handled outcome.

api/DBTools.Core.Settings.Persistence.IS.summary: Interface ISettingsProvider Namespace DBTools.Core.Settings.Persistence Assembly DBTools.Core.dll Reads layered settings and atomically commits per-year sections. public interface ISettingsProvider Methods CommitAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite>, CancellationToken) Replaces the supplied per-year sections with one atomic file swap. Task CommitAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite> writes, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters writes IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite> ct CancellationToken Returns Task Remarks Rejects an empty batch, null entries and repeated sections. Acquires a cross-process lock and rereads the file before replacing sections. Lock acquisition throws IOException after 10 seconds. A failed commit leaves the settings file unchanged. Get<TSettings>(SettingsSection<TSettings>) Synchronously rereads defaults and per-year settings without caching. TSettings Get<TSettings>(SettingsSection<TSettings> section) where TSettings : class, new() Parameters section SettingsSection<TSettings> Returns TSettings Type Parameters TSettings Remarks Missing files, sections and optional values use defaults. A value of the wrong JSON kind at an object or collection position reads as empty. An object, array or null at a string property reads as an empty string. A later file's null or scalar preserves an earlier object or array. Malformed JSON and missing JsonRequired members throw, including members of objects that read as empty. Values that cannot convert to a boolean or number throw, including null, objects and arrays. Other I/O errors propagate. RecoverAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite>, CancellationToken) Preserves the existing per-year file as raw bytes and atomically publishes the supplied defaults. Task<string?> RecoverAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite> writes, CancellationToken ct = default) Parameters writes IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite> ct CancellationToken Returns Task<string> Remarks Rejects invalid batches and serializes before changing files. Holds the same lock as CommitAsync through preservation and publication. An absent source needs no preservation copy. A valid JSON object keeps unwritten top-level values with their original JSON text. Invalid documents are replaced in full. Returns the completed preservation path, or null for an absent source. Completed sibling recovery copies remain after success, failure or cancellation. Before publication, failure or cancellation leaves the active file unchanged. Application defaults are outside this operation.

Required = 1 Awaited publication. Callback exceptions propagate; a skip (false) makes the publisher throw InvalidOperationException.

api/DBTools.ElevationTags.Settings.html.summary: Namespace DBTools.ElevationTags.Settings Classes ElevationTagsSettings Persisted settings for elevation-tag alignment workflows. PatternContext PreviewContext Draws the selected spot elevation type as Align places it. The preview shows one spot whose leader runs down to the element point and one whose leader runs up to it. The family symbol, shoulders, leaders and elevation text use paper-inch layout and the type's visual properties. SettingsPackContext Settings pack context for elevation tag configuration. Coordinates pattern, type, and preview contexts for the settings UI. SpotElevationPreviewLayout Places a spot type preview in paper inches. It shows one leader that runs down to the element point and one that runs up. X grows along the shoulder and canvas Y grows downward. SpotElevationPreviewScene A laid-out preview: two spots of one type whose leaders run down and up to one element point. ShowsSymbol is false when the type has no symbol drawing or uses in-line text. SpotElevationPreviewTag One spot in the preview. The symbol center is LeaderEnd; the shoulder runs from there to ShoulderEnd, where the leader turns to the element point. Label and BaseLabel span the capitals, from their top to the baseline; BaseLabel is the label without offsets. SpotElevationPreviewTag.SymbolPlacement The symbol's leader-end origin and its canvas-space extent. SpotElevationSymbolDrawing A Revit-free spot symbol drawing in paper inches. api/DBTools.Presentation.Dialogs.Behavio.summary: Class ButtonCommandCloseBehavior Namespace DBTools.Presentation.Dialogs.Behaviors.ButtonCommandClose Assembly DBTools.Presentation.dll Runs an attached command and optionally closes the hosting window through its session. public static class ButtonCommandCloseBehavior Inheritance object ButtonCommandCloseBehavior Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks For a raw modal view use DialogResult="True" (Save) or DialogResult="False" (Cancel), with this behavior's optional Command and CommandParameter properties. A result implies close. The attached command executes before the session's close gate runs. Use the attached Command, rather than Button.Command, so WPF does not execute a second command after closing. ExecuteAndClose retains result-free closing for existing views. Accepted clicks remain unhandled so parent Click handlers can observe them. api/DBTools.Presentation.Logging.LoggerW.summary: Class MarqueeText Namespace DBTools.Presentation.Logging.LoggerWindow.Controls Assembly DBTools.Presentation.dll Shows one line of text. Text that does not fit is still by default and shortened in the middle, keeping its start and as much of its last word (after the last space or dot) as fits: Joist…AutoUpdateTask. While IsActive is true, such text runs as a ticker instead: it holds at its start, scrolls left at a slow, steady speed, followed by a second copy after a gap, and repeats. Deactivation stops the ticker and returns the text to its start. When AnimationsEnabled is false, the text never scrolls. public sealed class MarqueeText : FrameworkElement, IAnimatable, ISupportInitialize, IFrameworkInputElement, IInputElement, IQueryAmbient api/DBTools.Presentation.Logging.LoggerW.title: Namespace DBTools.Presentation.Logging.LoggerWindow.Controls | DB Tools
api/DBTools.Presentation.Logging.LoggerW.summary: Namespace DBTools.Presentation.Logging.LoggerWindow.Controls Classes MarqueeText Shows one line of text. Text that does not fit is still by default and shortened in the middle, keeping its start and as much of its last word (after the last space or dot) as fits: Joist…AutoUpdateTask. While IsActive is true, such text runs as a ticker instead: it holds at its start, scrolls left at a slow, steady speed, followed by a second copy after a gap, and repeats. Deactivation stops the ticker and returns the text to its start. When AnimationsEnabled is false, the text never scrolls.

api/DBTools.Presentation.RevitCallback.R.summary: Class RevitCallbackRelay Namespace DBTools.Presentation.RevitCallback Assembly DBTools.Presentation.dll A callback object for Revit whose type belongs to the never-reloaded tier. Revit keeps some callbacks after the call that received them; for example, it keeps native copies of failure handling options, with their failures preprocessor, until it next pumps. A reloadable callback held that way keeps its Dev Mode generation alive while a reload proves the generation unreachable. api/DBTools.Presentation.ToolWindows.ITo.summary: Interface IToolWindowSession Namespace DBTools.Presentation.ToolWindows Assembly DBTools.Presentation.dll Owns a raw-XAML view and its stable window shell. public interface IToolWindowSession Remarks Register payload event handlers and cleanup through the session. Retire synchronously on the shell's UI thread before unloading a payload generation. Window and View are unavailable after retirement. Host-owned creation, lifecycle, root layout and dispatcher callbacks temporarily clear contextual reflection and restore the caller's scope on return. Raw templates resolve through the stable schema. The close gate, subscribed handlers and AddCleanup callbacks re-enter the creation context with ExecutionContext flow suppressed. Retirement releases that context on every exit. Flow suppression prevents captures. Clearing contextual reflection controls synchronous resolution. A command must suppress flow throughout its payload reflection scope, including tool-triggered layout outside shell overrides. WPF can measure an invalidated subtree directly. This work can see the command context but cannot capture it while flow is suppressed. Async callback continuations do not inherit that context. Name resolution after an await must explicitly re-enter it under suppression for synchronous work. Binding accessors, edit cancellation, collection notifications and custom shell initializers execute in the host's neutral reflection context. They must not depend on ambient name resolution. Properties Closed Completes after an accepted user close, once every AddCleanup callback has run. Task Closed { get; } Property Value Task Remarks Forced retirement leaves this task pending, and it never completes. Callers must not await or block on it during shutdown or reload. Register retirement-time work through AddCleanup, never through a continuation of this task. IsRetired bool IsRetired { get; } Property Value bool Outcome Open until retirement starts. Retire records Closed for an accepted user close or Retired for a forced retirement, including native window destruction, once and before any AddCleanup callback runs. IReadOnlyList<Exception> Retire() Returns IReadOnlyList<Exception> Remarks Writers are quiesced before behavior release, LIFO cleanup and edit cancellation. Final discovery and severing include disconnected containers and owned popup roots. UI Automation may retain the stable tree; its bindings, resources, inputs and values must no longer retain the payload. Shared stable definitions are not mutated. Forced retirement suppresses payload close notifications. Accepted user close preserves pending form edits and Explicit bindings through Closed and cleanup. Neither path pumps. Register payload event unsubscriptions and other owned work through AddCleanup. api/DBTools.RecordSet.Features.Operation.summary: Interface ISafeFileSystemOperations Namespace DBTools.RecordSet.Features.Operations Assembly DBTools.RecordSet.dll public interface ISafeFileSystemOperations Methods AcquireLock(RecordSetSafeOperationContext) void AcquireLock(RecordSetSafeOperationContext context) Parameters context RecordSetSafeOperationContext CopyPath(SafeCopyPathRequest, RecordSetSafeOperationContext) Copies a file, or each file under a directory at the same relative path, to a destination in the target root. void CopyPath(SafeCopyPathRequest request, RecordSetSafeOperationContext context) Parameters request SafeCopyPathRequest The source and destination paths, the file filter and the verification option. context RecordSetSafeOperationContext The target root, long-path mode, log and cancellation token of the run. Remarks A file that ShouldCopyFile rejects is skipped with a log line and is not a failure. Each accepted file overwrites its destination and gets the source creation, last-access and last-write times. With VerifyAfterCopy, the SHA-256 hash of each accepted destination file must equal that of its source. A normal return means that every accepted file was copied and verified as requested, not that every source file was copied. The resolved destination is checked against the target root before each write. The check and the write are separate operations, so a concurrent path replacement can race them. Cancellation is observed between operations; a running file copy or hash read is not interrupted, so a late cancellation can return normally. A copy, timestamp, callback or verification failure, or a cancellation, can leave destination files changed, and execution does not restore them. An exception from ShouldCopyFile or Log propagates unchanged. Exceptions ArgumentNullException request, context or the context runtime is null. InvalidOperationException The destination, or a file destination under it, resolves outside the target root. OperationCanceledException The context cancellation token was canceled before an operation started. IOException The source does not exist, a read or write failed, or verification found a missing or different destination file. UnauthorizedAccessException The process cannot read the source or write the destination. Remarks A file that ShouldCopyFile rejects is skipped with a log line and is not a failure. Each accepted file overwrites its destination and gets the source creation, last-access and last-write times. With VerifyAfterCopy, the SHA-256 hash of each accepted destination file must equal that of its source. A normal return means that every accepted file was copied and verified as requested, not that every source file was copied. The resolved destination is checked against the target root before each write. The check and the write are separate operations, so a concurrent path replacement can race them. Cancellation is observed between operations; a running file copy or hash read is not interrupted, so a late cancellation can return normally. A copy, timestamp, callback or verification failure, or a cancellation, can leave destination files changed, and execution does not restore them. An exception from ShouldCopyFile or Log propagates unchanged. Exceptions ArgumentNullException request, context or the context runtime is null. InvalidOperationException The destination, or a file destination under it, resolves outside the target root. OperationCanceledException The context cancellation token was canceled before an operation started. IOException The source does not exist, a read or write failed, or verification found a missing or different destination file. UnauthorizedAccessException The process cannot read the source or write the destination. Plan Plan { get; } Property Value Plan Version 0 when cleared; increments on initialize and on each accepted update. int Version { get; } Property Value int Methods Clear() void Clear() Initialize(Plan) Admits a detached copy without modifying the caller's plan. void Initialize(Plan plan) Parameters plan Plan TryGetPlan(out Plan?) Returns a detached snapshot when a plan is initialized. bool TryGetPlan(out Plan? plan) Parameters plan Plan Returns bool Update(Action<Plan>) Updates a private candidate. Only an accepted change replaces state and advances its version. void Update(Action<Plan> mutator) Parameters mutator Action<Plan> Remarks mutator changes a detached copy of the accepted plan. A candidate with unchanged content is a no-op: the version stays and no event is raised. An exception from mutator and a rejected admission keep the accepted plan and version. An accepted candidate advances the version once and then raises PlanChanged. An exception from a PlanChanged subscriber propagates after that commit; the committed plan and version stay. Exceptions InvalidOperationException The store has no initialized plan. SpecFailureException Admission rejected the changed candidate. The failure code is PlanValidationFailed, and the detail lists each rule failure. Events PlanChanged Raised after initialize, accepted update, and clear. Published plans are detached from stored state. Clear publishes a null plan with version 0. event EventHandler<PlanChangedEventArgs> PlanChanged Event Type EventHandler<PlanChangedEventArgs>

A probe rotation out of range (DBTools.SGT.Domain.SpecFailures.SpecFailureCodes.AnalyzerRotationRange) stops the candidate search and returns a failed OrientationResult that contains the range diagnostic. Other expected per-family incompatibilities (calibrated faces not found, rejected rotation, justification or offset writes) arrive as DBTools.SGT.Domain.SpecFailures.SpecFailureException; cancellation, rollback failures and invariant defects propagate unchanged.

TemplateApplyResult BatchApply(long targetTemplateId, TemplateComparison comparison, IReadOnlyList<SettingSelection> selections, IReadOnlyList<PendingCategoryOverride> pendingOverrides) Parameters targetTemplateId long comparison TemplateComparison selections IReadOnlyList<SettingSelection> pendingOverrides IReadOnlyList<PendingCategoryOverride> Returns TemplateApplyResult The attempted, succeeded and failed counts, with one conflict for each setting whose apply failed with an expected apply failure (that setting's subtransaction rolled back); no conflicts when every setting was applied. api/index.html.title: API reference | DB Tools
api/index.html.summary: API reference This section is generated from the XML documentation comments in the source code. It lists the public types and members of the DB Tools assemblies. Generating the reference Run the documentation build from the repository root: bash .github/scripts/build-docs.sh full-api Use the SDK pinned by global.json. The script restores DocFX 2.78.5 from wiki/.config/dotnet-tools.json. It builds the Release product and Sandbox for Revit 2026 to supply build tasks, dependency assemblies and generated WPF source. The build runs on Linux with Windows targeting enabled. It does not start Revit. The script restores each non-test project in src/ with the metadata properties from wiki/docfx.json. DocFX's automatic restore is disabled because version 2.78.5 does not pass these properties to dotnet restore: Property Value Purpose Configuration Release Match the prerequisite builds and DocFX's default configuration. RevitYear 2026 Select the Revit API packages and year-specific restore assets. EnableWindowsTargeting true Resolve Windows and WPF reference packs on Linux. Set for every project by Directory.Build.props. DesignTimeBuild false Include Revit source excluded by XAML designer builds. DBT_IsDesignerBuild false Use normal project paths and source inclusion. _DBT_MergeDesigner true Retain public package references for DocFX's unmerged project symbols. _DBT_MergeDesigner controls package visibility separately from source inclusion. The product build merges public dependencies into their owning assemblies. DocFX reads project source, so its compilation needs those dependencies as package references. Keep the restore properties in the script aligned with the metadata properties in wiki/docfx.json. DocFX reads the projects in src/, excludes test projects, writes metadata to wiki/api/, and builds the site into wiki/_site/. Compilation errors fail the build. The conceptual script mode uses docfx-conceptual.json and builds the articles without API metadata or product builds. The reference covers the namespaces of DBTools.Core, DBTools.App, DBTools.Presentation and the tool assemblies (DBTools.GM, DBTools.SGT and others). Members without an XML comment appear without a description. Writing documentation comments Document each public type and member with /// comments. Give a <summary> for every member, a <param> for every parameter, <returns> for non-void methods and <exception> for exceptions that callers handle: /// <summary> /// Runs an action inside a Revit transaction. /// </summary> /// <param name="action">The action to run in the transaction.</param> /// <returns><see langword="true"/> if the transaction committed; otherwise <see langword="false"/>.</returns> /// <exception cref="InvalidOperationException">No document is active.</exception> public bool Execute(Action action) Use <remarks> only for constraints that a caller must know.

developer-guide/architecture/assembly-lo.title: Assembly Loading Contract | DB Tools
developer-guide/architecture/assembly-lo.summary: Assembly Loading Contract The product is a tree of ordinary files: one entry assembly, three top-level libraries and one assembly per tool. The installed add-in loads in Revit's default AssemblyLoadContext. Revit-hosted tests and Dev Mode load the product into a context that the dbtools-daemon creates. In every host, App loads each tool assembly by explicit path into the context that holds DBTools.dll, and Revit calls each command by its assembly path and class name. Installed layout Each supported year has one directory of ordinary files. This is the product tree that the installer, Revit-hosted test staging, Sandbox and Dev Mode use: <year>/ ├── DBTools.addin ├── DBTools.dll ├── DBTools.Core.dll ├── DBTools.Presentation.dll ├── DBTools.HandyControl.dll └── Tools/ ├── DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel.dll ├── DBTools.DialogSuppression.dll ├── DBTools.ElevationTags.dll ├── DBTools.ERFT.dll ├── DBTools.FoundationTags.dll ├── DBTools.FramingJoins.dll ├── DBTools.GM.dll ├── DBTools.JoistGirderWeight.dll ├── DBTools.OrganizeFoundationTypes.dll ├── DBTools.RecordSet.dll ├── DBTools.SGT.dll ├── DBTools.Settings.dll ├── DBTools.TDV.dll └── DBTools.VTC.dll DBTools.addin names DBTools.dll and the class DBTools.App.Addin.AddinEntry. DBTools.dll contains the entry point and host infrastructure and no tool code. WPF needs the physical location of Presentation and HandyControl, so they stay at the top level. Merged libraries Every third-party runtime library is merged into one owner assembly; no third-party DLL is staged. build/Merging/AssemblyMerges.props declares the merges: App owns ricaun.Revit.UI.0.9.0. Core owns the manifest and YAML parser, MVVM, functional, dependency injection, logging, options and primitives libraries, and Serilog.Extensions.Logging. SGT owns LibTessDotNet privately. The double-precision assembly is not merged. Presentation owns the Helix and SharpDX closure, Serilog, and the public dependency injection and logging abstractions. SGT and ERFT declare CSharpFunctionalExtensions directly. Desktop builds share its public types through Core. Portable dependencies retain their NuGet identities. Serilog is in Presentation, which is never reloaded, because its thread-static state must not enter a collectible load context (dotnet/runtime#134928). A declaration's Include is the assembly name. The optional PackageId names a NuGet package whose name differs; ricaun uses PackageId="ricaun.Revit.UI" because its assembly name contains a version. MSBuild passes each merge its inputs as items: the resolved runtime asset of a package, or the output of a project. The merge copies its evaluated reference files into a temporary reference directory. ILRepack searches only that directory and resolves framework identities only from those files, so other package or compiler-output files and the runtimes installed on the build host cannot change the result. MSBuild Inputs and Outputs, including the owner's project.assets.json, decide when a merge reruns. The task deletes its temporary files afterwards. App host references The pinned ricaun.Revit.UI.0.9.0 assembly references Revit 27.0.4, also when App is compiled for Revit 2026. The App merge therefore binds these host references to the exact identities of the selected year during the final Cecil normalization: RevitAPI;RevitAPIUI;AdWindows;UIFramework Only App does this. MergeReferenceGuard then resolves every TypeRef, MemberRef and attribute type name with Cecil against the selected year's evaluated references. It rejects a missing type or member, a referenced version higher than the evaluated one, and any reference to an assembly that a merge removed. The Nice3point UIFramework reference is part of the Revit reference metadata used for this check; it is not shipped. Entry and idle acknowledgement AddinEntry has a public parameterless constructor for Revit. OnStartup first calls AddinIdle.TryAcknowledge. If DBTOOLS_DAEMON_REVIT_ROLE is set to any nonempty value and the entry assembly is in exactly AssemblyLoadContext.Default, it sets the AppContext data DBToolsDaemon.IdleAddin:DBTools to the entry assembly's file location and returns Succeeded before any runtime, ribbon, logging or tool work. OnShutdown returns Succeeded immediately for that instance. Otherwise startup enters AppStartupBoundary, a non-inlined method, which starts the App lifecycle inside ToolWindowCallbackScope. Startup, shutdown and ribbon failures that cannot reach the normal log are written to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\DBTools.Fallback.log with BCL APIs only. Tool resolution ToolAssemblyResolver.LoadAssembly(rootAssembly, assemblyName) loads a manifest-declared assembly. The name must be a simple assembly name: it does not end with .dll in any case and contains no /, \, , or :. Other names throw ArgumentException before any file lookup. If the name equals the root assembly's name, the root is returned. Otherwise the resolver: requires a file-backed root assembly; resolves <root directory>/Tools/<assemblyName>.dll and requires the file; reads the file's assembly name and requires the declared simple name; returns an assembly of that name already loaded in the root's context, if its full identity and location match the file; a different identity or location is an error; otherwise loads the file with that context's LoadFromAssemblyPath. The resolver does not search other contexts, install an AppDomain resolver or create a load context. The ribbon registers each command by its assembly location, full class name and availability type name. Availability is implemented by the command's own assembly. Command and availability callbacks enter ToolWindowCallbackScope, which suppresses ExecutionContext flow and sets contextual reflection to the command's load context. Hosted tests and Dev Mode The daemon creates ProductLoadContext for hosted tests and DevModeLoadContext for Dev Mode. App loads each declared tool from Tools/ into that context; Dev Mode does not probe other subfolders. Presentation and HandyControl stay loaded for the life of the process. App, Core and the tool assemblies can be reloaded, as the host decides. DevModeCollectibleUnloadTests composes such a generation on Linux and requires it to unload; see Testing Tools. Sandbox Sandbox runs one new process in the default context for each candidate year. Its entry point uses only BCL types: it validates the candidate, loads the top-level product files and the Tools/ assemblies from their paths, and then starts WPF through a non-inlined method. The process exits after validation, so no candidate assembly remains loaded for the next year. See Sandbox Validator. Distribution hashes Distribution validation checks the exact relative file set, PE identities, source-derived versions, first-party reference identities, file lengths and SHA-256 hashes. The hashes identify the staged candidate. Nothing checks them when an assembly loads. See Build Pipeline, Architecture Overview and Installation.

developer-guide/architecture/build-pipel.title: Build Pipeline | DB Tools
developer-guide/architecture/build-pipel.summary: Build Pipeline build.sh (Linux, WSL) and build.ps1 (Windows, PowerShell 7) are the build entry points. Both run dotnet build build/Build.proj -t:<Target> with the pinned SDK. They map public Restore to the build graph's restore target because MSBuild reserves the target name Restore for its own package restore. Use either wrapper to run DBTools' restore step. A plain dotnet build build/Build.proj -t:Restore does not run that step. The default target is BuildAll, which builds, validates and publishes the complete distribution for Revit 2026 and 2027. BuildAll compiles no test projects. Synopsis ./build.sh [Target] [parameters] pwsh -NoProfile -File build.ps1 [Target] [parameters] Both entries print build/Usage.txt for --help. Option names ignore dashes and case. Option Short form Description --Configuration <Release\|Debug> -d, --debug Build configuration; -d selects Debug. Default: Release --Years <years> -y, --year Revit years, for example 2026 or "2026 2027". Default: every supported year --SkipClean <true\|false> --clean Skip Clean before Restore. --clean sets SkipClean to false. Default: true --Verbose [true\|false] -v, --verbose; -q, --quiet Show the child builds on the terminal; -q sets false. Default: false --DryRun [true\|false] Clean lists the directories and deletes none; BuildBundle writes no bundle. The target's dependencies still run. Default: false --CandidateDistributionPath <dir> --candidate-dist Package an existing promoted tree --Revit2026Dir <dir>, --Revit2027Dir <dir> Installed Revit, used only for validation --TestProjects <a,b> Projects for the selected-test targets An unknown option exits with status 2 before any SDK work, with Unknown build parameter '<option>'. The target is the first positional argument. build.sh rejects the NUKE options --target, --root, --solution, --continue, --nologo, --verbosity, --plan, --profile, --skip and --host with a message that starts ERROR: '<option>' is a NUKE option, and this build does not use NUKE. build.sh exits with status 3 in a Windows shell (Git Bash, Cygwin) and names build.ps1. Build.proj validates the option values in its Initialize step: a boolean other than true or false fails before any target runs. Targets Target Result BuildAll Complete 2026/2027 build, validation and promotion to .artifacts/dist/Release BuildApp [-y <year>] App, Core, Presentation, HandyControl and the tool assemblies ValidatePrePush BuildApp plus manifest type validation BuildTests [-y <year>] Every test project and the hosted product inputs; all years by default BuildSelectedLocalTests, BuildSelectedPureTests, BuildSelectedDesignAutomationTests The projects named by --TestProjects in one test lane AssembleDistributionCandidate [-y <year>] A candidate year tree for checks that consume one; it is not published StagePortableAcceptanceInput Stage the candidate and Revit references for portable validation ValidateDistributionCandidate Portable validation and Dev Mode preflight of the candidate PackageSandboxValidationInput A content-addressed zip of the candidate and Sandbox for Windows validation PromoteToDist Replace the published distribution with the validated candidate BuildBundle Package the promoted tree into .artifacts/bundle/DBTools.bundle, one year tree per Revit year, under the Version.props product version Restore [-y <year>] Restore the production and validation graphs for the selected years through either wrapper ValidateManifestTypes, VerifyArtifacts, BuildSandbox, BuildValidationRunner, Clean, Info Individual steps BuildAll, StagePortableAcceptanceInput, ValidateDistributionCandidate, PackageSandboxValidationInput, PromoteToDist and BuildBundle build the complete distribution. These targets require the Release configuration and the complete supported year set, which is the default; a -y that omits a supported year fails. ValidateDistributionCandidate and PromoteToDist also require a clean Git worktree. BuildBundle with --candidate-dist PATH packages an existing promoted tree without building. --clean runs Clean first, which deletes build output (see Directory layout); without it, an incremental BuildAll reuses the existing artifacts. No target switches to another SDK or output root. BuildAll depends on PromoteToDist, so it runs, in order: Restore, BuildValidationRunner (the Dev Mode policy runner), BuildApp for each year with ValidateProductVersions, VerifyArtifacts, StageDistributionCandidate, WriteCandidateMetadata, StagePortableAcceptanceInput, ValidateDistributionCandidate, ValidateManifestTypes and PromoteToDist. Examples ./build.sh BuildAll ./build.sh BuildAll --clean ./build.sh BuildApp --Configuration Debug --Years 2026 ./build.sh Restore --Years 2026,2027 ./build.sh BuildTests ./build.sh BuildSelectedLocalTests --TestProjects DBTools.App.Local.Tests -y 2026 pwsh -NoProfile -File build.ps1 BuildAll pwsh -NoProfile -File build.ps1 Restore -y 2026,2027 Individual projects also build with plain dotnet build. Their MSBuild graph computes content versions and stages runtime prerequisites, but does not validate or publish a distribution. Build the installer On Windows, install Inno Setup 6.7.1 or a later 6.x, for all users or for the current user, then run: ./build.ps1 BuildBundle pwsh -NoProfile -File .github/scripts/compile-installer.ps1 BuildBundle writes the bundle and installer-defines.json. The compile script reads those files. It finds ISCC.exe and its version through the Inno Setup 6_is1 uninstall entry (HKLM, then HKCU) and refuses a version outside 6.7.1 to 6.x. It writes DBTools-Setup-<version>.exe under .artifacts/release-assets/. Implementation Each entry maps its options to MSBuild properties, acquires the pinned SDK, initializes the HandyControl submodule when needed, and runs Build.proj. Both entries produce the same dotnet build command line. No Build.proj target runs bash or Python, so BuildAll and BuildTests behave the same on Windows. Test execution is done by test.sh. Build.proj owns the target graph and starts each child dotnet build with its own binary log. The C# code of each target is a BuildPipelineStep in build/Tasks (DBTools.Build.Tasks, net8.0, loaded by the SDK's MSBuild on .NET 10). It owns option validation, Revit reference checks and distribution steps. The task assembly is written to .artifacts/build-tasks/<Configuration>/ and recompiles only when its inputs change. Compilation on every operating system uses the centrally pinned Nice3point Revit API metadata packages with runtime assets excluded. An installed Revit is never a build prerequisite. --Revit2026Dir and --Revit2027Dir name an installation, native or mounted under WSL, for validation only. The staged Revit API files are reference metadata, not an executable runtime. APS Design Automation builds the separate Revit 2026 net8.0 Sentinel test project with its own API provider. Product output build/MSBuild/ProductOutput.proj and ProductOutput.targets stage the product tree for each year in .artifacts/bin/Release/<year>/net10.0-windows/. StageProductOutputTask keeps the Tools/ directory and validates each declared owner image. Intermediate runtime inputs can be year-keyed under .artifacts/bin/Release/<year>-runtime-input/. Local test staging copies the year tree recursively into the test output and removes stale top-level tool images. BuildBundle writes installer-defines.json with the product file list and supported years. The year list comes from RevitYearContract.SupportedYears. compile-installer.ps1 passes both values to ISCC. The installer checks each selected year against the product file list and filters unselected components from the generated PackageContents.xml. Assembly merges build/Merging/AssemblyMerges.props declares one owner for each merged library; AssemblyMerge.targets runs the merge. Every merged library is private to its owner and absent from the year tree, including Tools/. Each owner is merged once per build; MSBuild Inputs and Outputs skip the merge when nothing changed. The merger writes a deterministic MVID and PDB, and version validation requires each stable assembly (Presentation, HandyControl) to have the same version and SHA-256 in every year. Owner Merged libraries DBTools.dll (App) ricaun.Revit.UI DBTools.Core DBTools.Manifest, YamlDotNet, CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, CSharpFunctionalExtensions, Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection, .Logging, .Options, .Primitives, Serilog.Extensions.Logging DBTools.SGT LibTessDotNet (private types; no double-precision assembly) DBTools.Presentation HelixToolkit and SharpDX assemblies, Cyotek.Drawing.BitmapFont, CommunityToolkit.Diagnostics, Serilog, Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions, Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions Serilog is in Presentation, which is never reloaded, because its thread-static state must not enter a collectible load context (dotnet/runtime#134928). The merge details are in Assembly Loading Contract. Content versions WPF resolves compiled resource URIs by assembly name and version, and Dev Mode identifies Presentation and HandyControl by full identity and SHA-256 hash. A content version therefore changes exactly when an assembly image can change. build/MSBuild/ContentVersion.targets computes it inside each ordinary compilation from these inputs: source, XAML and resource bytes, with the metadata that names, types and exposes each resource (Link, LogicalName, ManifestResourceName, Access, culture and generator metadata); resolved references: a package by its immutable coordinates, a project or local reference by its bytes, resolved before WPF markup compilation; source generators and the properties visible to them; the emitted assembly attributes, rendered as the SDK generates them, and the framework attribute; the signing key, Win32 manifest and resources, and the effective PathMap; the compiler options that change emitted code or metadata; for a merge owner, the merged project images and the merger code and binaries; for HandyControl, its vendor URI rewrite rules and the rewrite task's source (DBT_ContentVersionRule and DBT_ContentVersionInput). The content hash keys the rewrite, and a missing rewritten file reruns it. These are not inputs: build scripts and targets, .editorconfig and other analyzer configuration, diagnostic-only analyzers and warning options. Editing them changes no version. No Git commit or tree enters assembly attributes, content inputs or debug metadata. The computation runs inside the project's own compilation: it starts no second MSBuild evaluation and loads no other project. Because the inputs are hashed, resetting a source timestamp cannot hide changed bytes. A referenced content version is part of the referencing image, so consumers change version with it. An implementation-only change behind an unchanged version does not propagate through compiler references. The input list is written one entry per line to: .artifacts/obj/content-version/<Configuration>/<year|shared>-<flavor>/<project>/<framework>/inputs.txt The SHA-256 of the list is the input hash. Its first six bytes give the four-part assembly version: 4.<u16(bytes 0..1) % 65535>.<u16(bytes 2..3) % 65535>.<u16(bytes 4..5) % 65535> AssemblyInformationalVersion is <version>+inputs.<hash>. Compare two input lists to see why a version changed. Identical inputs keep the same identity and output timestamps. Content versions apply to Presentation, HandyControl, Core, App and projects that set DBT_IsToolAssembly=true. Other product metadata uses the release version from Version.props. Checked-in files are named relative to the repository root and artifacts relative to a relocatable root, so a fresh clone gives the same versions. Repository source and intermediate PDB documents use the path prefix /_/dbtools/; transformed vendor documents use /_/dbtools/vendor-build/. SourceLink revision stamping is off. A WPF temporary project hashes its parent's input list, so local-type identities in BAML carry the final version. The staged year trees carry the version evidence: each first-party image has its content version and input hash, the version must derive from that hash, and a stable image must be byte-identical in every year. The staging step reads them before it validates the compiled resource URIs. Candidate validation and promotion Distribution validation walks each year tree recursively. It requires the exact relative file set with Tools/ as the only directory, and checks PE identities, source-derived versions, first-party reference identities, framework references, and the length and SHA-256 of every file. It also checks the add-in entry, commands, availability types, manifests, resources and ownership. A missing, extra, misnamed, misplaced or stale file fails the candidate. Manifest validation scans every manifest.yml under src/ and resolves module, command, explicit availability and design-time ViewModel type names against the compiled images of each year. Every declared owner must resolve to Tools/<owner>.dll. BuildAll and ValidatePrePush run it. Portable candidate validation requires each explicit availability type to implement IExternalCommandAvailability and rejects a redundant type equal to the command. ValidateDistributionCandidate prints one Dev Mode preflight line per year: Revit <year> Dev Mode preflight: <n> failures, <m> warnings; outcome=<x> Every collectible-boundary warning counts as a failure: each warning code is on the Dev Mode contract's avoid list and is a warning only because static analysis cannot prove that it breaks retirement. Promotion requires a clean Git worktree (tracked and untracked files) with a resolved HEAD. Three records describe a distribution: The build metadata (build.json) records the years, frameworks, the distribution fingerprint, the Git commit and tree IDs, the source versions, the hash of each product file and the Protocol package pin. The portable acceptance receipt, written by ValidateDistributionCandidate, records for each year the validated files, the Revit reference descriptors and the Dev Mode preflight result. Its AvailabilityTargetTypes and matching owner array record only explicit availability classes. Both arrays can be empty when commands use inferred availability. The promotion receipt, .artifacts/dist/Release/promotion-receipt.json, embeds the acceptance receipt with the source snapshot and the distribution fingerprint. It contains no temporary staging paths; consumers validate it against the published tree. Promotion validates the staged candidate, its fingerprint, the exact year trees and the receipt. It then deletes the published .artifacts/build.json, replaces .artifacts/dist/Release with the validated tree, copies the tool contract to .artifacts/acceptance/tool-contracts.json, and writes build.json last. Read the distribution only after the build command exits successfully. When promotion prepares the new tree, each declared file whose SHA-256 equals the file at the same path in the current .artifacts/dist/Release becomes a hard link to that file; new and changed files are copied. An unchanged file therefore stays the same file across promotions, and a virus scanner that has scanned it (Windows Defender on a Dev Mode host) does not scan it again. If the platform refuses a link (different file system, no hard-link support, permission error), promotion logs the reason once at low importance and copies that file and all remaining files. No step writes into a published file. Point Dev Mode at .artifacts/dist/Release/<year> directly; a copy is a set of new files that the scanner scans again. Tool contract build/Distribution/tool-contracts.json holds the DBTools texts that the live Tools check of dbtools-daemon compares with the running product: window titles, interaction kinds, prerequisite refusal names, and banner, control and status texts. Its tools object is keyed by command type name without the Command suffix (Gm for GmCommand). Each entry has interaction, title (null for a command without a window), source_files and named texts. PromoteToDist publishes it as .artifacts/acceptance/tool-contracts.json, so a distribution archive carries it beside build.json: the CI dbtools-complete artifact and the release assets include it. Clean keeps .artifacts/acceptance/. UpdateCombinedFoundationTags names the gate of the Combined Foundation Tags commands: warning_key, the warning that disables them, and blocked_message, its message. While the warning is inactive and a required shared parameter fails, Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags show a modal repair alert instead of running. Both entries name it: repair_alert_title (the window title), repair_alert_message (the header, which prerequisite_message repeats), and the UI Automation names of its buttons, repair_alert_cancel_button and repair_alert_repair_button. Cancel changes nothing and ends the command as Cancelled with no banner; the alert has turned the warning on, so a later gated command in the same session is refused by the warning. Change a source text that an entry names and this file in the same commit. ToolContractsTests in testing/DBTools.Build.Tests fails when a source_files path does not exist, or when a text equals no whole string value of its tool's source files: ./test.sh test --tool BUILD --fixture ToolContractsTests The string values are C# string literals, XAML attribute values and text with XML references resolved, and YAML scalar values; a longer string such as General Settings does not match General. Three forms also match: each line of a multi-line C# literal, because a refusal message reaches the log one line at a time; a ribbon displayText with its lines joined by spaces, which is the command's execution name; and a C# interpolated string or a XAML StringFormat whose holes each take a whole string value from the same files. One value is not product text. Gm.workspace_status_pattern is a regular expression that the check applies to the GM status text; the test requires that it compiles. Revit-hosted test inputs Staging for Revit-hosted tests builds one complete product tree for the selected year and includes it with relative paths unchanged, including the 14 tool assemblies in Tools/. Test assemblies, NUnit and adapter files, and companions are separate inputs. The input cache checks relative path, identity, length and hash before the daemon request is written. Test restore roots are per year: each year of the local scope restores separately, and Design Automation tests share the 2026 root. The Pure root restores every Pure project against $(DBT_PureRevitYear) owners through static graph restore. NuGet keys package specifications by project path, so one root never mixes owner variants. See Test Pipeline. Pinned SDK build/DotNet/sdk.sh selects the SDK version from global.json. If no installed dotnet has that SDK, it uses the private root ~/.dotnet/pinned-sdk-<version>. A system dotnet with the pinned SDK is used as is. A build needs only the SDK. A net8.0 test host (the APS Design Automation Sentinel) also needs the .NET 8 runtime. sdk.sh pins that runtime version, because global.json cannot, and installs it only when such a host runs: test.sh requests it, or run bash build/DotNet/sdk.sh --test-host-runtime. On a system dotnet without the .NET 8 runtime, a net8.0 test host uses the private root. A package in the private root is valid only when its marker file, .dbt-complete-<package>-<version>, names its archive. To install a package, sdk.sh: checks the archive against the SHA-512 in Microsoft's release metadata; extracts it into a staging directory beside the root; renames the version directories into place; writes the marker. A version directory without a valid marker is replaced from the verified archive; one that already matches stays. The lock <root>.lock serializes installs across builds and worktrees, and a build that waited for the lock checks the markers again before it installs anything. The Linux installer requires Python 3.10 or later. build.ps1 uses the same root, SHA-512 check, marker and lock for the SDK without Python. It downloads the release metadata's dotnet-sdk-win-<arch>.zip and replaces a root without a valid marker as a whole. It installs no test-host runtime. Build servers DBT_BUILD_SERVERS sets the server mode for every wrapper invocation (build.sh, test.sh, the lane helpers and their child builds). DBT_MSBUILD_MAX_CPU_COUNT sets the graph build parallelism (default 2); the wrappers validate it and Build.proj passes it to its child builds. build.sh runs Build.proj itself without the MSBuild server; each child dotnet build uses the selected mode. 1 (default): the invocation owns one compiler server and one MSBuild server. Its scope ID, dbtools-scope-<owner pid>-<run id>, is the compiler pipe name, and <scope id>-msbuild is the MSBuild handshake salt. On every trapped exit, each server gets a shutdown request with a 30 s timeout; then every process the invocation still owns is terminated, the compiler by its exact -pipename: argument and MSBuild nodes by the exact salt in their environment. No process is matched by name. A starting invocation stops dbtools-scope servers whose owner process no longer exists; servers of a live owner are never touched. The servers make a clean build faster and raise its peak memory use. 0: no compiler server and no MSBuild server (UseSharedCompilation=false). Use this on hosts that admit builds by free memory. build.ps1 always uses mode 0, because the ownership checks read Linux /proc. Node reuse is off in both modes. Outside a wrapper, Directory.Build.props keeps the compiler server off. UseSharedCompilation is not a content-version input. build/Testing/check-build-server-lifecycle.sh <second-checkout> runs the server lifecycle with the real SDK: a normal exit, a failed build, SIGTERM, SIGKILL followed by the next build's sweep, and a concurrent owner in another checkout. Run it manually. Temporary folder Each wrapper invocation (build.sh, each test.sh test build and the daemon test lane) runs in its own temporary folder, /tmp/dbt-<owner pid>-XXXXXX, in both server modes. Every dotnet build leaves empty folders in the temporary directory, and a killed .NET process leaves its dotnet-diagnostic-*-socket and clr-debug-pipe-* files there; the folder takes them. TMPDIR names the folder. When cygpath exists (Git Bash), TMP and TEMP name it in Windows form, so native dotnet.exe uses it too. The folder is in /tmp whatever TMPDIR the caller sets. Its path has at most 23 characters, so the runtime's socket paths in it stay under the Unix limit of 107 bytes. The compiler pipe stays in /tmp, where the SDK puts it. NUGET_SCRATCH, unless set, names NuGet's default lock folder in the caller's temporary directory, so concurrent restores still share their locks. The test.sh test-input cache also stays in the caller's TMPDIR. On exit the scope removes the folder after its exit callback. A folder that cannot be removed, also on a second try one second later, is reported and fails a command that succeeded. The invocation holds a flock on <folder>/.lock through a file descriptor that every process it starts inherits. The lock stays held while any of those processes lives, also after the wrapper is killed and its dotnet build goes on writing to the folder. A starting invocation removes a folder only when its owner process no longer exists and its lock is free. A folder whose lock is held, or cannot be checked because .lock or flock is missing, stays. The folder of a live owner is never touched. build.ps1 sets TMP, TEMP and TMPDIR to a folder of its own and NUGET_SCRATCH as above, and removes the folder in the same way when the build ends. It then restores the four variables, also when its setup fails, so & .\build.ps1 leaves the PowerShell session as it was. On Windows the folder is dbtools-build-<build id> in the temporary directory. Each run removes the folders that killed runs left: those that the current user owns, that are plain folders (not links or junctions), whose name has exactly that form and whose process no longer exists. A folder whose owner cannot be read stays. Elsewhere the folder is /tmp/dbt-<pid>-XXXXXX without a lock, so a killed run's folder stays. Logs Each run writes to .artifacts/build/<YYYYMMDD-HHmmssfff>-<pid>/, named by build.sh or build.ps1 (by Build.proj for a plain dotnet build).
