Shared parameter migration GroupPlacementQuery.IsInGroupPlacedMoreThanOnce(document, elementId) walks the element's group and every enclosing group. It checks GroupType.Groups.Size for all placed instances of each type, including nested instances. It returns false for an ungrouped element or a chain of group types placed once. SharedParameterMigration uses this check before grouped value writes. GroupPlacementQuery.CreateRunQuery(document) creates a query for a run whose group placements do not change. It caches each element's membership, ancestor reads and each group type's placement count. Discard the query when the run ends. Foundation Tags creates one query per run, then restricts only changed parameters that do not vary between group instances. SharedParameterMigration.Migrate(document, source, target, requiredCategories, useHandling) replaces the project parameter source with the shared parameter target that has another GUID, for example a parameter that a project received from an older shared parameter file. target is an ExternalDefinition from the open shared parameter file; the file stays open until Migrate returns, and the project must not bind the target GUID. Loaded families may define it already; Migrate then binds that parameter. The caller supplies its own definitions and categories and selects useHandling explicitly. RemoveWithParameter deletes dependent schedule fields and filter rules with the source. CarryToTarget snapshots and restores supported schedule and filter uses. Migrate changes the project only when it can carry over every value. Before any change it: Refuses a global parameter, and refuses unless the source spec NameEquals the target spec. The message names both specs, for example 'Associated Pier Elevation' exists as Area; expected Length; nothing changed. Refuses when a rebar container overrides the source; the override cannot be carried to the target. Plans one write per value, read by storage type (String, Double, Integer, ElementId); unset values are skipped. An instance-bound source keeps each element value. A type-bound source copies each type value to every instance of that type in the bound categories; it refuses when a type has a value and no instance. When the target already exists, it also records target-only values on elements in categories added to the target binding. When loaded families define the target already, the binding makes source and target one parameter. Each element keeps the value that is not empty: an old value is written to the target, a target-only value is restored if binding changes it, and an element that has one value for the source and another for the target refuses. Compares the source definition with the target: name, visibility, hide-when-no-value, and, through an element that has the parameter, description and user-modifiable. The target is canonical; each difference is reported and logged. One transaction group then contains these operations: Delete the source. Bind the target as an instance parameter of the source categories and requiredCategories, in the source parameter group. Set its variance between group instances to the source's and verify it. Restore the recorded schedule fields and view filter trees when useHandling is CarryToTarget. Write every planned value to its element, then read each one back. Revit refuses a changed value on a member of a group placed more than once (directly or through a nested group) when the parameter does not vary between group instances ("Changes to groups are allowed only in group edit mode"), and the API has no group edit mode. When the source does not vary and a planned write changes such a value, step 1 also turns the variance on. A third transaction turns it off after the writes; Revit reports every element whose value it aligned with another instance of its group, and any such element, or any value read back afterwards that differs, rolls the group back. A source that does not vary holds one value per group member, so its values come back unchanged. Revit does not let every spec vary: in Revit 2026 and 2027 Text, Area, Material and URL can vary, and Integer, Number, Length and Yes/No cannot. For a spec that cannot vary, such a value is refused in the plan, before any change, and the message lists the grouped elements. A target-only value that a loaded family exposes on a member of a group placed more than once is the same in every placement, because Revit refuses another value while the parameter does not vary. The binding keeps it, so it needs no write and does not refuse, for any spec. Revit reports whether a parameter can vary only when variance is set. For Migrate and copied type values in Rebind, the plan trial-binds when the original binding does not vary and a candidate write is on a repeated group member. It checks whether the parameter can vary only if binding changes the value and a write is needed. The trial runs in a transaction (or a subtransaction inside an open transaction) that always rolls back. CheckMigrate and CheckRebind therefore find this refusal too. The trial binds the parameter in the same transaction, so its rollback leaves no dead binding key (see below). Hosted tests cover one group type with several instances, a group type with a standalone instance and copies nested in other groups, nested groups, a detail group, type values copied to grouped instances, Text and Length target-only values on repeated groups, a Length value in a group placed once, a Length refusal for source values, an aligned value that rolls back, and a failure while the variance is on that restores the values and the variance. The API cannot create attached detail groups or design options, so those are not tested. If any write or read-back fails (read-only, rejected by Revit, a Revit exception, a grouped value that Revit aligned), or any step throws, the group rolls back and the project keeps the source with its binding and values. A write that Revit blocks for any other reason takes the same path. A refusal, or a rollback after failed writes, throws SharedParameterMigrationException; its Failures list each value that could not be carried over as a SharedParameterValueFailure with the element ID and reason, and each is logged as a warning. Any other failure propagates its own exception after the rollback. A caller with more repair steps runs Migrate inside its own transaction group, which then rolls the migration back with the rest. CarryToTarget records every field in each affected main and embedded schedule. It also records field order, formatting, display settings, sort and group entries, filters and percentage references. It blocks a combined field and a schedule with a calculated field; Revit counts a percentage field as a calculated field. After it replaces the parameter, it restores the target field at the source index and remaps the field IDs in every reference. It writes a display type (totals or minimum and maximum values) only when the restored field shows another one, because Revit rejects any such write on a field that cannot show it, and it refuses when the restored field cannot show the recorded display type. It reads the schedule back and compares the complete record. It also records each affected filter's categories, logical tree, inversion flags and typed rules. It rebuilds each tree with the target parameter ID, checks that every rule applies to the filter categories and compares the result with the record. An unknown rule or evaluator blocks the move. Any difference beyond the source-to-target parameter and field-ID substitutions throws inside the group and rolls the move back. CheckMigrate runs the same carry checks without a lasting change. Foundation Tags passes RemoveWithParameter and keeps its confirmation prompt. Rebind(document, parameter, requiredCategories) uses the same plan and transaction group to bind a shared parameter as an instance parameter of its categories and requiredCategories, for a type-bound parameter or one that lacks a category. Its plan includes values already exposed by loaded families in added categories. The check trial-binds with the same categories. Revit's BindingMap.ReInsert resets the variance between group instances and aligns grouped values, so Rebind records every value first, restores the variance, writes the values back and reads them back, with the same group handling as Migrate. It keeps the GUID and parameter group, copies each type value of a type-bound project parameter to every instance of that type, refuses when a valued project type has no instance or a rebar container overrides the parameter, and returns SharedParameterRebindReport. It also refuses before a change when a placed family defines the target GUID only as a type parameter in a category that the rebind adds; in a category that an instance binding already has, the family type value stays on its type. Element.get_Parameter(Guid) also returns an empty parameter with that GUID on each instance of such a family, and on the type of an instance parameter; only the parameter that holds the value is in Element.Parameters, so the plan decides whether a type defines the GUID from that set. An unplaced family type parameter stays on its type because the instance binding does not change it. CheckMigrate(document, source, target, requiredCategories, useHandling) and CheckRebind(document, parameter, requiredCategories) run the same checks and plan without a change, and throw the same refusals, so a caller can find every refusal before it changes the project. CheckMigrate plans values in the same additional categories as Migrate. For planned writes on repeated group members, each check trial-binds in a transaction that always rolls back. It checks variance only if binding changes a value and a write is needed. CheckRebind uses the same rule for copied type values and values in added categories, with the same categories as Rebind. Such a check transaction must report RolledBack; when Revit reports another status or the rollback throws, the check throws SharedParameterRollbackException. It is not an InvalidOperationException, so a caller that shows refusals as messages lets it propagate as a failure, and a caller's own transaction group rolls back. Shared parameter use scan and repair SharedParameterUseScan.Find(project, query) reports project bindings, stored values, schedule and filter uses, and matching uses in loaded families. A query with ScanFamilies = false opens no family and cannot plan a repair. A full scan opens every editable loadable family. FamiliesScanned is true only when it opens all of them. The report records other GUIDs, use locations, blockers and the state that the repair compares at apply time. A category ID in a binding, schedule or filter that the project cannot resolve, or cannot bind, is a blocking use with its reason. SharedParameterFamilyScan owns the open, visitor and close loop used by both the family migration and use scan. Some FamilyManager reads need a current type: when a family has none selected, the scan selects its first type, and when the family has no type it adds a temporary one. The scan closes each family without saving, so neither change reaches the project. A family with no type cannot be replaced (FamilyManager.ReplaceParameter needs a type), so the plan refuses it per family and the use scan shows that as a blocking use. A non-editable nested family whose types or instances expose an old GUID is always a blocking use. One that shows no such GUID may still hide a use that the scan cannot open; that possible use blocks only an old GUID that no family parameter of the host carries, as in the family plan's direct-use path. For a carried GUID, SharedParameterFamilyMigration.Migrate refuses after the reload when a hidden use keeps the old GUID. A family template can bring such nested families (the Generic Model template loads level and section head families). SharedParameterRepairEligibility.Evaluate(report, selection) opens phase 2 only when every family parameter is ticked, no hand-fix or blocking use of an old GUID remains, and every schedule or filter use can move with the project binding. Uses of the company GUID itself are listed only and do not block, except a company-GUID project binding that is itself blocked. Phase 1 can move selected family parameters while the old project binding remains. A selected family cannot have a hand-fix or blocking use; Plan then throws ArgumentException that lists each such use with its reason. SharedParameterRepair.Plan refuses phase 1 when a schedule field or filter rule uses a selected old GUID, unless the same plan moves that GUID's project binding, because the move would leave that field or rule on a GUID that the moved families no longer fill. A project binding that stays does not count: its categories need not be the families'. When the selection asks to move the binding and phase 2 is not open, Plan throws ArgumentException that lists the binding blockers. SharedParameterFamilyPlan.Refusals holds SharedParameterFamilyRefusal values with the family ID, family name, use kind, labels and original exception. SharedParameterFamilyMigration.Migrate still throws the combined refusal exceptions. SharedParameterRepair.Plan requires a full scan. Apply checks the target GUID and name, scans again and compares the reviewed state. A difference throws SharedParameterMigrationException before a change. Both phases run in one transaction group: family parameters move first, then the binding, values, schedule fields and filter trees. A failure or cancellation between phases rolls the group back. Bind(document, parameter, requiredCategories, parameterGroup) binds an existing unbound shared parameter as an instance parameter. It records values exposed by loaded families in those categories, restores each value that binding changes and reads every value back. CheckBind runs the same plan without a lasting change. Both methods refuse before a change when a value cannot be kept or a placed family defines the target GUID only as a type parameter. A family type parameter with no placed instance stays on its type because the instance binding does not change it. HoldsAnyValue(document, parameter) is true when an element or type in the bound categories has a value, or a rebar container overrides the parameter. It does not inspect an unbound parameter. Removing a binding removes its project-bound element values, but a loaded family can still define the same shared GUID and expose family values. Bind records those exposed values before it creates an instance binding. SharedParameterBindingLookup.Contains, Get and Find look up a binding in Document.ParameterBindings. After a lookup of a binding, a rollback that undoes a change to its variance between group instances leaves a dead key in the binding map, unless the rolled-back changes inserted or reinserted the binding. Every later Contains or get_Item in that document then throws InvalidObjectException until the model is reopened. The kind of rollback (a transaction or a transaction group) and the bound categories do not matter. Core binds the parameter in the transaction or transaction group that changes its variance, so its own rollbacks restore the map; another add-in's rollback, or an Undo of the variance setting, can leave the dead key. The lookups catch only that exception from the lookup and throw SafeExecutionRefusedException with InvalidStateMessage: Revit's parameter bindings for this model are in an invalid state; save, close and reopen the model, then try again. They do not retry. Migrate, Rebind, Bind, CheckMigrate, CheckRebind, CheckBind and HoldsAnyValue read bindings through them and refuse with that message. A hosted test leaves the dead key in a document that it creates and closes. Deleting a parameter removes each schedule field that uses it and the field's sorting, grouping, filter entries and formatting. It removes a combined field whole. GetDependentElements does not list those schedules. FindScheduleFields(document, parameter) lists each field that a delete removes as a SharedParameterScheduleField, with its schedule ID and name, heading, combined-field status and embedded-schedule status. With RemoveWithParameter, Migrate deletes the source and Revit removes its schedule fields and filter rules. A caller can show those uses before it deletes the source. With CarryToTarget, Core records and restores the complete schedule definitions and supported filter trees. Combined fields, calculated-field schedules (including percentage fields), unknown filter rules and unknown evaluators block this operation. Deleting a parameter also removes every rule set (ElementParameterFilter) that has a rule on it. Revit keeps each filter's categories, other rule sets and AND/OR structure. A filter with no rules left applies to every element in its categories. FindFilterRules(document, parameter) lists every rule in each affected filter as a SharedParameterFilterRule: the filter ID and name, rule parameter name and plain-language rule. It includes category rules and adds an a rule entry when Revit does not expose a rule. It does not show a filter's tree or inverted flag. CarryToTarget uses typed snapshots of both properties when it rebuilds a filter. A successful Migrate returns SharedParameterMigrationReport: the kept value count, the number of copied type values, and the definition differences. Combined Foundation Tags uses CheckMigrate, CheckRebind, CheckBind, FindScheduleFields, FindFilterRules, Migrate, Rebind, Bind, HoldsAnyValue and the family migration below in Install/Repair. Install/Repair plans family and project changes before confirmation. It cannot inspect final project values that family migration creates. If a later project migration finds a value it cannot keep, it refuses inside the outer transaction group and rolls the repair back. That refusal may appear after confirmation. Shared parameters in loaded families A loaded family keeps its own definition of a shared parameter, and its formulas, dimension labels and annotation labels refer to the parameter by GUID. Revit registers each shared parameter of a loaded family in the project as a SharedParameterElement. When the project deletes that element (as Migrate and a delete of a duplicate do), Revit also removes the parameter from the labels of the loaded families that use it, so a tag shows no value. A caller therefore replaces the parameter in the families first, and deletes the old GUID only when nothing in a family uses it. SharedParameterFamilyMigration does that for any set of definitions. Its input is one SharedParameterFamilyTarget per definition: the ExternalDefinition from the open shared parameter file and the categories that the project binds, or will bind, it to as an instance parameter. A family matches a target by name, ignoring case. FindFamilyNames(document, name, targetGuid) opens no family. It returns the loaded families whose types, or placed elements for an instance parameter, show a shared parameter with the name and another GUID where no project binding of that parameter to the family's category explains it. A label that uses the parameter directly shows on nothing, so this misses it. A parameter shows on a type or element only when it is in Element.Parameters (see Rebind above). Plan(document, targets) changes nothing. When the project has a shared parameter with a target name and another GUID, it opens every editable loadable family with Document.EditFamily, inspects it and closes it unsaved; otherwise it opens none. It also opens editable nested families recursively. For a non-editable nested family, it checks parameters on its symbols and placed instances without opening it. In a carrier path, it refuses if those elements expose the old GUID. A non-editable nested family can still hide a label or formula, which the plan cannot see. Revit removes a shared parameter element that nothing in a family uses when it loads the family and keeps one that a nested family or a label still uses, so Migrate opens each reloaded family and refuses, rolling every family back, when the old GUID remains. In a direct-use path, it refuses if any non-editable nested family could hide a label, formula or other use, even when its symbols and instances do not expose the GUID. A family parameter with the name and another GUID becomes a SharedParameterFamilyChange. Plan.Refusals holds SharedParameterFamilyRefusal records with the family ID, name, use kind, labels and original exception. Migrate throws their exceptions before any change. Every other use refuses, with the family named: a shared parameter element with the name that no family parameter carries (a label that uses it directly, added through Edit Label in a tag or title block family, or a nested family; Revit removes a shared parameter element that nothing in the family uses when the family is loaded); a loaded editable nested family that contains a shared parameter element with the old GUID, even when it has no instance in the host family; a family nested as a shared family in another loaded family; another data type; a type parameter in a category of InstanceCategoryIds (the family's type parameter would hide the instance values of its elements); an element or type whose value for the old GUID differs from its value for the target; a carrier whose target value is on the other scope (a type value of any type of an instance carrier's family, placed or not, or an instance value of a type carrier's type, from a binding with the other scope); an in-place or non-editable top-level family that defines the parameter or may define it; and a family that Revit does not open. Revit does not open an in-place or non-editable top-level family, so its elements decide: a parameter that shows where no project binding explains it refuses; where a binding could explain it, the plan rebinds the project parameter without the family's category in a transaction that always rolls back (a rolled-back rebind leaves the binding map intact) and reads the elements again, and a family that still shows the parameter, or a check that cannot run, refuses; a rollback that does not complete throws SharedParameterRollbackException. In Revit 2027 builds (REVIT2027_OR_GREATER), SharedParameterLabels reads each annotation label and the refusal lists one SharedParameterLabelUse line per label that shows the parameter: the label ID, its detail group, the position of the parameter in the label, and its prefix, suffix, sample text, spaces before, line break before and the label's non-breaking-spaces setting; when no label shows the parameter, no nested family shows it, and no non-editable nested family remains uninspected, the element is unused and does not refuse. If a non-editable nested family remains uninspected, the refusal names it and says that DB Tools cannot prove the parameter is unused because Revit does not let DB Tools edit it. In Revit 2026, DB Tools cannot read annotation labels and therefore refuses every direct shared-parameter element. An annotation-family refusal says the labels could not be read; a model-family refusal names the direct use without calling it an annotation label. Every refusal tells the user to reload the edited family into the project. No supported Revit lets an add-in change a label: the Revit 2027 reference assembly does not make AnnotationLabel.SetParameterFormatting or AnnotationLabel.Create public. Migrate(document, plan) throws the plan's refusals before any change. Otherwise one transaction group holds every family. For each family it records, for each type (type parameter) or placed element (instance parameter), the value to keep: the old parameter's, or the target's when the old one is empty. Project target-only values in categories added to a binding are handled by SharedParameterMigration.Migrate, not by this family migration. It opens the family, replaces the family parameter with a temporary family parameter and then with the target (FamilyManager.ReplaceParameter, which cannot replace a shared parameter with another shared parameter directly), with the same group and instance or type kind, and checks in the family document that the group, kind, reporting setting, formula, every type value of every parameter, the formula of every other parameter, each dimension labeled with it, each associated element parameter and, in Revit 2027, each label kept their state with the target in place of the old GUID. Plan has already inspected loaded nested families recursively. After replacement, Migrate re-scans nested families and refuses if a family parameter, nested-family type or instance, or readable label still uses the old GUID. Project view-filter rules are listed by FindFilterRules; when the project parameter is deleted, Revit removes every rule of each rule set that uses it and keeps the filter's other rule sets and its AND/OR logic. In Revit 2026 it refuses an annotation-family replacement if the old shared-parameter element remains, because a label may use it; the refusal tells the user to edit the labels and reload the family. An unused SharedParameterElement may remain after replacement. It reloads the family (IFamilyLoadOptions overwrites the family and its type values; a nested shared family stays as the project has it); a Revit warning is dismissed and a Revit error rolls the load back and refuses. It opens the reloaded family and refuses if the old GUID is still there (a hidden use, see Plan). It then writes each recorded value that the reload did not keep, clears a value that was empty, regenerates the project (Revit shows an instance value written after a family reload only then) and reads every value back. A changed value on a read-only parameter (a formula) or on a member of a group placed more than once refuses. Any refusal or failure rolls the group back. It returns one SharedParameterFamilyReport per replaced parameter with the kept type and element value counts. When the project binds the target, Revit shows the project binding's parameter group for that parameter in every loaded family that defines it, so the family editor shows that group after the migration. Family files on disk do not change; a family loaded again from such a file brings the old GUID back. Plan opens each family, so it takes longer in a project with many families; it logs the count and the time. Hosted tests in Tests/Integration/Revit/Revit/SharedParameters/ cover text, integer, length and material values on two categories, type values, a failure after values are written, an incompatible spec, definition differences, and the main, combined and embedded schedule fields that FindScheduleFields lists. Elements in design options and elements owned by another user in a workshared model are not tested; a write that Revit blocks there takes the rollback path above. Safe execution ISafeExecutor Every tool entry point runs inside ISafeExecutor. public interface ISafeExecutor { Task RunAsync(Func<Task> action, ILogger logger, IBannerNotifier? notifier, SafeExecutionOptions opts, CancellationToken ct = default); Task<SafeExecutionResult> RunWithoutThrowingAsync(Func<Task> action, ILogger logger, IBannerNotifier? notifier, SafeExecutionOptions opts, CancellationToken ct = default); } SafeExecutor: gives each execution a GUID correlation ID and logs the elapsed milliseconds. A start or completion log write that fails goes through ContainedDiagnostic and does not change the outcome; checks the token immediately before it invokes the action inside the protected boundary, so pre-canceled work returns a canceled result without running; logs full exception details, including inner exceptions and XAML parse context. ExceptionDiagnosticsLogger owns the formatting of exception, cancellation, XAML and notifier-failure logs; shows success and error banners through IBannerNotifier and logs notifier failures. The error banner shows the exception message, or The operation failed. for a blank message; shows each failure once (Failure/FailureReport). When it shows a failure or refusal banner, it records that with the exception. The banner system keeps every request it accepts (see Notification banners), so the record means the banner will be seen. An outer layer that receives a recorded exception (or a wrapper or aggregate whose causes are all recorded) logs it and shows no banner and no failure surface. Records belong to the report scope that the outermost run of an asynchronous flow opens (an AsyncLocal). The outermost RunAsync, which rethrows, hands its record on to the window error boundary, which takes it once. A later run ignores and removes a record that another run handed on, so a failure that its caller cached and throws again in a later run is shown again. A cached failure that reaches the boundary without a run is still taken as shown once. Code that shows its own failure banner and rethrows calls FailureReport.ShowBanner; a last handler calls FailureReport.TakeShown; calls ISafeExecutionFailureSurface on fatal errors. App composition adapts the logger window's show action to this interface (SafeExecutionFailureSurface), so Logging does not depend on SafeExecution; reports, then rethrows, refusals, cancellations and failures from RunAsync(...). The rethrown exception keeps its instance and stack trace, unless a reporting failure wraps it in an AggregateException with the operation's exception first. RunWithoutThrowingAsync(...) returns the same outcome as a SafeExecutionResult, for event and UI callers that log and notify, then stop propagation. A null argument faults the task of either method. The XML documentation of ISafeExecutor gives the full contract. An expected refusal throws SafeExecutionRefusedException; the result status is SafeExecutionStatus.Refused and SafeExecutionRefusalReporter reports it once: the first layer with a notifier shows the warning banner, and outer layers only log it. Tool { get; } } A manifest without a module must declare a panel and at least one ribbon command, and cannot declare settings or settings packs. A manifest with a module must declare at least one responsibility: tool.ribbonTools, tool.settings, tool.settingsPacks or a registered lifecycle hook. App checks that after RegisterHooks(...), against the temporary registry, before it merges the module's registrations into the root container. Type resolution and availability ToolTypeResolver resolves a manifest type only from the assemblies the caller supplies; it never scans all loaded assemblies. Command types resolve against the manifest's tool assembly. Availability types resolve against the tool assembly, Core and the App runtime assembly, so startup cannot bind to a stale or unrelated assembly. Generic availability predicates (active document, active view, selection) are in Tools/Availability. A tool-specific predicate stays with the tool feature that owns the rule. ToolCommand implements IExternalCommandAvailability through IsCommandAvailableCore and RequiresActiveDocument. When a manifest omits availabilityType, ToolRegistration.FromManifest(...) infers the command type if it implements that interface. An explicit separate availability type uses the existing resolver and validation route. An explicit type equal to the command type is rejected with tool and command context. The direct registration constructor retains nullable availability metadata. CommandAvailabilityValidator.Validate(...) reuses the executing instance when its exact type and the registered availability type equal the command type. Contextual edits have no executing command instance, so the validator constructs the declared availability type once. It also constructs separate availability classes once. Null availability metadata skips the check. Both paths create the Revit category set and use the same refusal messages. ToolModule public abstract class ToolModule { public virtual void RegisterSettings(IServiceCollection services, ToolManifest manifest) { } public virtual void RegisterServices(IServiceCollection services, ToolManifest manifest) { } public virtual void RegisterSettingsPacks(IServiceCollection services, ToolManifest manifest) { } public virtual void RegisterHooks(ToolRegistry registry, ToolManifest manifest) { } } public class MyToolModule : ToolModule { public override void RegisterServices(IServiceCollection services, ToolManifest manifest) { services.AddSingleton<IMyService, MyService>(); services.AddSingleton<IViewActivationTask, MyViewActivatedTask>(); } public override void RegisterHooks(ToolRegistry registry, ToolManifest manifest) { registry.RegisterLifecycleHook<MyContextualRibbonInjector>(); } } ToolRegistry The registry of tool registrations and lifecycle hooks. Command execution reads registration metadata through CommandPreflight; HookCatalog resolves the lifecycle hooks in registration order. public sealed class ToolRegistry { public ReadOnlyCollection<ToolRegistration> Tools { get; } public IReadOnlyList<Type> LifecycleHookTypes { get; } public bool HasHookRegistrations { get; } public void RegisterTool(ToolRegistration registration); public ToolRegistration ResolveCommandRegistration(Type commandType); public void RegisterLifecycleHook<T>() where T : class, IHookLifecycle; public void MergeFrom(ToolRegistry source); } RegisterLifecycleHook<T>() rejects a type that is already registered. MergeFrom checks every incoming tool and lifecycle hook against the target before it changes the target, then appends the source registrations after the target's. The registry has no view-activation entry: Core's AddDbtHookRuntimeServices registers the one ViewActivationHook service. App owns assembly loading and the validation of command and availability types. With the concrete types resolved, ToolRegistration.FromManifest(...) builds the registration and the registry accepts it. ToolRegistration and ToolRibbonSpec public sealed class ToolRegistration { public Type CommandType { get; } public Type? AvailabilityType { get; } public AppRunScopeProfile ExecutionProfile { get; } // manifest RunProfile; default InlineUi public ToolRibbonSpec Ribbon { get; } public static ToolRegistration FromManifest(Type commandType, ToolManifest manifest, RibbonToolManifest tool, Type? availabilityType = null); } ToolRibbonSpec is the Revit-free ribbon metadata that App ribbon composition consumes. FromManifest(...) is the only place that holds both the tool manifest and the ribbon manifest. It selects the internal ToolRibbonSpec.CreatePushButton(...) or CreateGroupedControl(...) factory and keeps the manifest display text and group metadata. A push control cannot carry group fields; a grouped control requires a non-push control kind and a non-blank group identity. Hooks Supported hook types: ViewActivationHook: the Core dispatcher for view-activated work. AddDbtHookRuntimeServices registers it; IViewActivationTask services supply its work. IHookLifecycle: module-owned lifecycle work, such as contextual ribbon setup or dialog-showing event subscriptions, registered through ToolRegistry.RegisterLifecycleHook<T>(). internal sealed class HookHost { internal Task AttachAsync(UIControlledApplication application, CancellationToken ct); internal Task RollbackAttachAsync(CancellationToken ct); internal void Detach(); } IHookLifecycle defines asynchronous initialization, asynchronous rollback after an attach failure and synchronous shutdown at the application boundary. Shutdown has no cancellation token or task; HookShutdownAction holds a plain Action. HookCatalog resolves the required ViewActivationHook service and the registered lifecycle implementations, in registration order, from DI. A missing service fails attachment. HookHost adds its own ViewActivated subscription as the last HookAttachAction, queues subscription and the unsubscription after an attach failure through the call gate, and publishes the attached state only after the whole attach succeeds. HookLifecycleCoordinator keeps the attach actions that initialized successfully, rolls them back in reverse order after a later attach failure and runs their shutdown actions in reverse initialization order. Normal detach clears that ownership only after every action succeeds; after a failure the complete, idempotent action set stays available for retry. Each lifecycle implementation cleans up its own resources when its initialization fails after it acquired them. ViewActivationHookDispatcher owns the safe-executor dispatch policy for this high-frequency event. ViewActivationHook keeps a runtime-failure gate per task and per document. The gate keys on DocumentSessionKey (title, path and instance hash): a reopened model starts clean, and after Save As or the first save of a new model the task can run once more under the new key. Dialog Suppression records ownership immediately after its adapter subscribes and calls its unsubscribe path if later initialization fails. Contextual ribbon: Initialization cleanup runs in the queued initialization context. It attempts the selection detach, every contextual UI removal and the edit-event disposal, and keeps both the initialization and the cleanup failures. Each registration keeps its tab, panel and button, and whether the injection created the panel or only the button. Cleanup removes a panel only when it owns it; a reused panel loses only the created button. A foreign button with the same ID, and its handler, are kept. The injection registry removes only registrations that cleaned up successfully, keeps failed ones for retry and throws one aggregate after it attempts them all. Injection and button-state sweeps attempt every target, keep the original causes with their tab, panel and button, and throw one aggregate after the sweep. The selection controller keeps the exact detach action captured at subscription, so shutdown needs no new UIApplication. The selection refresh completion callback runs only after all injection, toggle or cleanup changes succeed. OnEvaluateAndToggleCompleted is an extension point of ContextualRibbonInjector; the Extreme Roof Framing Tool (ERFT) overrides it. Sources: src/DBTools.Core/Tools/Hooks/{Lifecycle,Host,ContextualRibbon}/, src/Tools/Services/DialogSuppression/Features/DialogSuppressionHook.cs. UI components Color picker ColorPickerViewModel synchronizes RGB, HSV and hex before raising ColorChanged. A component edit inside the callback synchronizes state and notifies PreviewBrush and HueBrush again. A notification guard suppresses nested ColorChanged events. Callback exceptions propagate. Invalid hex text remains visible without changing the color state or raising the event. Windows Presentation (DBTools.Presentation.Windows) owns the stable window surface: WPF Window inheritance, owner-handle support through IWindowOwnerHandleTarget and the IThemeOptOut contract. public class ModalWindow : Window, IWindowOwnerHandleTarget, IThemeOptOut { public IWindowOwnerHandleProvider? OwnerHandleProvider { get; set; } public bool UseDefaultTheme { get; set; } } public class ModelessWindow : Window, IWindowOwnerHandleTarget, IThemeOptOut { /* same members */ } ToolWindowHost constructs the stable shell. Core's ToolWindowFactory installs the owner, theme, icon, error boundary and progress lifecycle before the raw view loads; for a modeless window the session's shell initializer selects the modeless owner policy. Retiring the session releases all of it. Settings, Alert, Logger and notification banners are raw views hosted by ToolWindowSession. ToolWindowFactory registers modal Settings and Alert sessions and modeless Logger sessions in the window registry. The banner host registry retires its modeless sessions when banners close or reset. Sandbox previews load the same raw resources with manifest-declared design-time view models. ToolWindowRegistry.RetireAll retires child sessions first, then each session's registered cleanups, then closes the shell. App shutdown calls it before other runtime owners reset. Window error boundary DBTools.Core.UI.Windows.ErrorBoundary holds the window error workflow. WindowStaticRuntime.Configure(...) is the one composition point where App startup supplies the banner notifier. The runtime receives IWindowErrorLogSurface and IWindowErrorBanner, so boundaries can surface the logger window and show handled-error banners without depending on the concrete shells. WindowErrorBoundaryRegistry owns one exception subscription per dispatcher. It routes each failure to the most recently activated attached window, then through activation history, then the attached list, skipping windows that have closed. WindowErrorBoundary classifies the original exception and every nested branch, including every aggregate branch. A branch is a DB Tools failure when its throwing method or a frame on its stack belongs to an assembly named exactly DBTools or starting with DBTools. (ordinal). Vendor code qualifies only as DBTools.HandyControl (the renamed HandyControl build) or DBTools.Presentation (which merges Helix). A raw HandyControl or HelixToolkit* assembly belongs to another add-in and never qualifies. A framework or Revit API failure raised from DB Tools code is therefore handled; another add-in's vendor failure is not. A bare DB Tools OperationCanceledException whose token was canceled is marked handled with a Warning log only: no banner and no handled-failure signal. The boundary presents and publishes the original outer exception, with its wrappers and causes, and returns the handled decision to the registry. An exception tree with no DB Tools branch stays unhandled and gets no notification. A window seen as closed keeps a weak tombstone and cannot be attached again. A closed WPF window that was never attached or seen is outside this registry; classifying it would need reflection or a new HWND. A lifecycle owner can subscribe through WindowErrorBoundaryRegistry to the handled-failure signal of its window. The subscription requires the attached per-window host and throws if it is missing. The notification carries the original failure and any presentation failure. Detaching clears the window's observers. WindowErrorPresenter owns the banner and logger-window show policy. A failure whose record a run or tool handed on (see FailureReport) is only logged, and the record is taken. A SafeExecutionRefusedException shows its reason in a warning banner, without the logger window and never as Unhandled UI exception. Any other failure shows an error banner and the logger window. WindowStaticRuntime configures and resets Core UI for App and Sandbox. It serializes the whole lifecycle and reports ready only after diagnostics, window error boundaries and progress overlays are all configured. It rejects duplicate or partial existing configuration before it changes anything. A failed configuration rolls back only what that attempt installed, in reverse order, so it can be retried; cleanup failures are kept with the primary failure. Configure opens the dispatcher operation registry last, just before it reports ready. Reset retires that registry first, then resets error boundaries, progress overlays and diagnostics. It attempts every step, clears readiness even when a step fails and reports cleanup failures in one aggregate. The progress-overlay capability owns its host registry and visual attachment, so this reset disposes every registered host. App shutdown calls Reset after runtime host teardown. The Sandbox calls it when its window-runtime registration is disposed. The progress capability exposes only a getter for the attached overlay-visibility state, so tool XAML can collapse airspace content. WindowRuntimeCapabilities.CreateSandbox(writeLog, defaultOwnerMode) builds the Sandbox logger factory, logger, error-log surface, notification surface and a no-op progress capability inside the Core that owns the window interfaces. App startup configures its own notification, logging and progress capabilities with WindowOwnerMode.DefaultOwner. Sandbox installs WindowOwnerMode.Unowned. This required policy controls default-owner binding; explicit per-window owner providers retain their existing behavior. Sources: src/DBTools.Core/UI/Windows/Runtime/{WindowRuntimeCapabilities,WindowStaticRuntime}.cs, src/DBTools.Core/UI/Dispatching/DispatcherOperationRegistry.cs, src/DBTools.App/Shutdown/AppShutdownWorkflow.cs, src/DBTools.Sandbox/Runtime/WindowStaticRuntimeConfigurator.cs, src/DBTools.Sandbox/Composition/AppRuntime.cs. Alerts public interface IAlertService { AlertResult Show(AlertRequest request); } public static class AlertServiceExtensions { public static bool Confirm(this IAlertService alerts, string message, IWindowOwnerHandleProvider ownerHandleProvider, string title = "DB Tools"); public static T? SelectSingle<T>(this IAlertService alerts, AlertSelectionRequest<T> request) where T : class; public static IReadOnlyList<T> SelectMultiple<T>(this IAlertService alerts, AlertSelectionRequest<T> request) where T : class; } AlertServiceFactory, IAlertService and AlertServiceExtensions are public. Show is the only presentation call, so a substitute implements Show alone. AlertServiceExtensions owns the confirmation request (buttons yes and no) and, through the internal AlertSelectionPolicy, the selection requests (buttons ok and cancel) and their typed results. An empty selection returns null or an empty list without calling Show. The internal AlertService, AlertBodyBuilder, AlertWindowPresenter and AlertWindowViewModel own presentation, body composition, modal display and shell state. Confirm takes an IWindowOwnerHandleProvider; other alerts take owner and size policy in AlertWindowOptions. Implement IAlertBody for custom alert content. Core's container bodies (composite, banner table and message selection) return their immediate children through the internal IAlertBodyChildren; AlertWindowPresenter walks them root first, and each IAlertBodyTemplateProvider that owns a body adds its templates once. AlertCompositeBodySpec rejects an undefined CompositeBodyLayout. Alerts open with WindowStartupLocation.CenterScreen, which WPF centers on the work area of the owner's monitor in device pixels. An alert therefore opens on its owner's monitor (Revit or the DB Tools window that raised it) at any display scaling. WPF does not clamp the position, so an alert larger than the work area extends past it. Structural preview DBTools.Presentation.StructuralPreview.IStructuralPreview3D owns structural preview navigation and rendering. ERFT and the Super Girt Tool (SGT) pass immutable scene and emphasis snapshots and consume stable pointer events. Core compiles against Presentation; the Helix and SharpDX assets are private to Presentation. Each tool registers the viewport's synchronous disposal as a session cleanup. ToolWindowRegistry.RetireAll releases the viewport handlers, timers, camera, material and device state and payload subscriptions before it closes the shell. See Structural Preview. Extension points Call gates: implement IRevitCallGate for another execution mode. Hooks: register IHookLifecycle implementations, or IViewActivationTask services for view-activated work. Settings packs: register packs through AddDbtSettingsPackDefinition<TOptions, TContext>. Alert bodies: implement IAlertBody. Related pages Architecture Overview DBTools.App

developer-guide/projects/presentation.ht.title: DBTools.Presentation | DB Tools
developer-guide/projects/presentation.ht.summary: DBTools.Presentation DBTools.Presentation.dll is the WPF assembly that stays loaded for the life of the Revit process. It is staged at the root of each product year, beside DBTools.dll, DBTools.Core.dll and DBTools.HandyControl.dll. Item Value Project src/DBTools.Presentation/DBTools.Presentation.csproj Assembly DBTools.Presentation.dll Target framework net10.0-windows (Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027) References WPF, DBTools.HandyControl; Helix, Serilog and the logging and DI abstractions are merged in Contents Presentation holds only types that must live for the whole process: theme dictionaries, resource keys, styles, converters and pack resources; controls whose code-behind is limited to binding, dependency-property, routed-event, input and lifecycle mechanics; the ModalWindow and ModelessWindow base types with their owner-handle contracts, and the tool window shells ToolWindowModalShell and ToolWindowModelessShell; tool-specific behaviors, converters and controls under Tools/<TOOL>/; the structural 3D viewport (see Structural Preview). Production source is under src/DBTools.Presentation, with namespaces DBTools.Presentation.* that follow the folder tree. Compiled tool settings views live under Tools/<TOOL>/ in DBTools.Presentation.Tools.<TOOL>: the views of DialogSuppression, ElevationTags, FoundationTags and JoistGirderWeight. They bind to their tool contexts by property path, so Presentation does not depend on the tool assemblies. The project lists each Page and EmbeddedResource item; default Compile inclusion owns the code-behind. See Theme System for the two supported settings view forms. Presentation does not reference DBTools.dll, Core, tool types, view models, commands, services or the Revit API. App, Core and the tools may reference Presentation. ColorPickerPopup exposes and binds dependency properties by property path, and popup dismissal updates the stable IsPopupOpen property. ProgressOverlayControl binds to the command that the host supplies. Tool windows Tool views are raw embedded XAML. ToolWindowHost creates a modal or modeless shell, parses the view inside ToolWindowReflectionScope and sets the tool's view model. Core's ToolWindowFactory runs WindowInitializer on the shell first, which installs owner, theme, progress and error handling, and then registers the session. Hosts call session.ShowDialog() or session.Show() and get named controls with session.Require<T>(name). When a session closes or is retired, Presentation tears down bindings, automation roots, resources and callbacks. See Theme System. UI Automation item lifetime Retirement does not clear cached automation peers. In WPF 10.0.0, item peers hold reference-type rows weakly (ItemAutomationPeer._item uses ItemWeakReference, and DataGridCellItemAutomationPeer._item is weak), and teardown cuts the strong column, row-item and DataContext references. Tool items in a DataGrid, ListBox or TreeView, their types and a collectible tool context can therefore be released after retirement, also while a UI Automation client is attached. Rows are held strongly, and a collectible tool assembly stays loaded, in these cases: the first item cached by a peer store has an unreliable hash code (for example ComponentResourceKey); the store switches to list mode and holds every later key strongly; the items are boxed value types; the ItemAutomationPeerKeepsItsItemAlive switch makes _item strong; a UI Automation client holds an item element, which keeps its control alive through ElementProxy._peer. Enumerating ItemPeersStorage or _WeakRefElementProxyStorage materializes the weak keys, so their contents do not show an owning reference. Resource URIs /DBTools.Presentation;V<PresentationVersion>;component/Resources/Theme.xaml Raw and reloadable XAML declares stable namespaces with assembly=DBTools.Presentation. XAML compiled inside Presentation uses the form without assembly=. See Theme System for URI rules and Assembly Loading Contract for the distribution layout. Tests Project Target Content DBTools.Presentation.Pure.Tests net10.0-windows Presentation behavior without Revit, including the tool-specific behaviors, converters and controls under Tools/<TOOL>/, the tool window host and the logger window view. References Core for the tool window, window runtime and logger window integration fixtures, and every tool assembly for the embedded payload XAML sweep. DBTools.Presentation.Local.Tests net10.0-windows Revit-hosted structural preview fixtures. Both projects are under src/DBTools.Presentation/Tests/ and use explicit <Compile> membership. Test files mirror the owner folders. Presentation grants internals to both projects and to the Core test projects, whose fixtures use the internal host boundaries.

developer-guide/projects/sandbox.html.title: DBTools.Sandbox | DB Tools
developer-guide/projects/sandbox.html.summary: DBTools.Sandbox DBTools.Sandbox is a standalone executable that validates one product year and hosts tool windows for UI development without Revit. It targets net10.0-windows for Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027; build/Distribution/RevitYearContract.cs defines the supported years. Source layout Path Contents App/Startup/ SandboxEntry (BCL-only entry point), CLIOptions, SandboxCandidate, the SandboxMode enum (Interactive, Headless) App/ The WPF application Composition/ Sandbox runtime services and SandboxWindowFactory Features/WindowCatalog/ The window catalog shown in interactive mode Runtime/ Sandbox logging and window runtime configuration Validation/ Candidate, manifest, metadata and window validators Tests/ DBTools.Sandbox.Pure.Tests Runtime Sandbox starts a new default-context process for each candidate year. The entry point checks the year directory before any Core, Presentation or WPF type loads, loads the candidate's top-level assemblies and Tools/ assemblies from their paths, and then starts WPF. The candidate files are the only product assemblies in the process; the project compiles against Core, Presentation and HandyControl without copying their runtime files. Sandbox reads window specifications from the tool manifests through Core's SandboxCatalog and hosts them in the stable Presentation window shells. Design samples can implement Presentation.ToolWindows.IToolWindowSandboxComposer to compose raw view fragments after the window session is created. Ordinary samples need no composition callback. Sandbox installs the Unowned default-owner policy in the window runtime. The SGT design-time sample supplies its own unavailable 3D state and reason. Building real windows and checking their cleanup requires the Windows process. For the options, the validation steps and the manifest rules, see Sandbox Validator. See also Sandbox Integration and Assembly Loading Contract.

developer-guide/tools/common/elevation-t.title: DBTools.ElevationTags | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/elevation-t.summary: DBTools.ElevationTags NAME DBTools.ElevationTags - the assembly behind Align Elevation Tags and Set Elevation Symbol Text SYNOPSIS source src/Tools/Common/ElevationTags/ (MAP.md, manifest.yml) assembly DBTools.ElevationTags entry ElevationTagsToolModule commands ElevationTagsCommand DBTools.AlignElevationTagsInView (run profile InlineUi) ElevationTagsSymbolTextCommand DBTools.SetElevationSymbolText (run profile InlineUi) view src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/ElevationTags/ElevationTagsSettingsPackView.xaml DESCRIPTION The Align command and the view-activation task both call ElevationTagAlignmentService.Run. It runs SpotElevationTextAligner on the active view in one transaction. The settings pack draws the same placement with SpotElevationPreviewLayout. Set Elevation Symbol Text runs SymbolTextWorkflow, which asks for the text, and SymbolTextEditor, which copies families and types. The user page describes the behavior. STRUCTURE Paths are under src/Tools/Common/ElevationTags/. Path Contents App/Composition/ The module, the commands, and ServiceCollectionExtensions, which registers the service, the task and both workflows. SettingsPackContextFactory reads the types with SpotElevationTypeProjector. Features/ The workflow, the task, SpotElevationTextAligner, SpotElevationSymbolResolver, SpotElevationTextFont, SpotElevationTextComposer and SpotElevationTypeProjector. Features/SymbolText/ SymbolTextWorkflow, SymbolTextPolicy (text and reuse rules), SymbolTextTemporaryDirectory, and Revit/ with SymbolTextEditor and SymbolTextVariantMarker. Settings/ ElevationTagsSettings, SettingsPackContext and its pattern, type and preview contexts, SpotElevationPreviewLayout and SpotTextLocationParser. CONTRACTS Placement. SpotElevationTextAligner.ComputeTextOffset owns the rule. f = view.Scale / 12 converts paper inches to model feet. The near edge of the text is 2f/128 + f/8 from the leader end along the shoulder (the margin), and f/64 from the shoulder line (the gap). Above Leader and Below Leader take the side toward the spot origin. A rise within LevelTolerance (1e-9 of the leader length) counts as a leader that runs down. The Text Location only selects the edge that TextPosition marks, so the text box does not move: the bottom center for Above Leader, the top center for Below Leader, and the top corner nearest the leader end for In-line with Leader. The current text position plays no part, so a second run moves nothing. ComputeTextOffset_places_the_text_by_text_location_and_leader_direction and the Revit AlignElevationTagsWorkflowTests check this. Preview follows Align. SpotElevationPreviewLayout holds the margin and the gap at f = 1 in its own constants, LabelGapFromLeaderEnd and LabelGapFromShoulder. Change them together with ComputeTextOffset. Preview_and_align_place_text_on_the_same_side checks only the side. Font size. SpotElevationTextFont.EmSizeInches makes the capital height equal TEXT_SIZE, for Align and the preview. Align measures with GDI+. Shared_font_em_size_gives_the_capitals_the_requested_height checks the rule. Matching. Align compiles the nonblank patterns with IgnoreCase. An empty list means DefaultTagNamePatterns. A bad pattern is logged and skipped. TypeSelection filters the preview by type name only, with case. CollectValidationErrors blocks Save without a nonblank pattern or with a bad one. Run_FiltersByConfiguredPatterns_AndCountsOnlySuccessfulUpdates checks Align. Failures. A spot whose names cannot be read, and a spot whose update throws, add to FailedCount. The first of each kind is logged. Collection and transaction failures propagate. Run_CountsSpotsThatCouldNotBeFilteredByNameAsFailed and Run_LogsTheFirstUpdateFailureOfEveryRun check this. Text Location. SpotTextLocationParser.ParseTextLocation maps 0, 1 and 2 to AboveLeader, BelowLeader and InLineWithLeader, and throws for any other value. Align counts that spot as failed, and the preview leaves the type out. ParseTextLocation_rejects_a_missing_or_unknown_value checks this. Elevation base. TryUpdateSpot compares the SPOT_ELEV_BASE display string with Project Base Point and Relative. For the first, it subtracts the base point Z when the base point and the survey point differ in any coordinate. No test covers another Revit language. Auto-update admission. ViewActivationTask.AdmitAsync skips the task when AutoUpdateEnabled is false or the pack warning is active. ShouldRunInternalAsync admits only FloorPlan, EngineeringPlan and CeilingPlan. A failure in the run shows the Core error banner, and ViewActivationHook skips the task for that document session (DocumentSessionKey); it sets no warning. A failure in AdmitAsync also sets the pack warning. AlignOnViewActivatedTaskTests checks the run failure. One Undo step for symbol text. SymbolTextEditor.Apply runs in the transaction group DB Tools - Set elevation symbol text, and assimilates it or rolls it back. EditFamily runs with no project transaction open. A variant gets its text in the family document, is saved as <name>.rfa in a unique temporary folder, and is loaded by path. SymbolTextTemporaryDirectory deletes the folder and only logs a failure. SymbolTextEditorTests and SymbolTextTemporaryDirectoryTests check this. Reuse. A family with the variant name is reused only when its one text element holds the text, and a spot type only when it uses that symbol. The source family must hold one text element even when the variant exists. SymbolTextPolicyTests and Apply_validates_source_text_even_when_the_target_already_exists check this. Owned variants. SymbolTextVariantMarker stores ElementId, SourceId (both UniqueId values), SourceName and Text. The marker is valid only on the element whose UniqueId is in ElementId, with the name <SourceName> - <Text>. Cleanup looks only at the marked types that the selected spots leave, and at their marked families. It deletes one only when nothing else uses it, no other worksharing user owns it, and Revit deletes nothing else with it. Apply_cleans_only_unused_owned_variants_and_keeps_copied_or_user_types and TryDeleteVariant_rolls_back_a_native_host_deletion_that_also_removes_spots check this. FLOW AlignElevationTagsWorkflow.Execute refuses an unsupported view with a Warning banner. SpotElevationTextAligner.Run collects the OST_SpotElevations instances in the view and matches their names. Without a match, it starts no transaction. One transaction, DB Tools - Align spot elevations, calls TryUpdateSpot for each match. It skips a spot without a leader and a Relative base. BuildTagText builds the text to measure: the elevation in the type's units, with the indicator, or with EL. when the indicator is blank. MeasureTag measures it, and ComputeTextOffset places it along RightDirection and UpDirection. The spot gets the computed TextPosition when X or Y differs after rounding to two decimals of a foot. Z stays. DATA Item Value Settings section Tools.ElevationTags, read into ElevationTagsSettings: AutoUpdateEnabled (true), TagNamePatterns, and TypeOffsets by type name, in paper inches Settings pack common.elevation_tags Pack warning core.common.elevation_tags. It disables DBTools.AlignElevationTagsInView and auto-update. A failed admission sets it. Task ID structural.elevation_tags.updater Marker schema DBToolsElevationSymbolTextV1, GUID 535cae92-1d19-45ed-98ee-d06c501980ea, vendor DBTools DIAGNOSTICS Log lines start with [ElevationTags]. Debug level adds the counts, and up to 5 sample spot names when nothing matches. The first update failure logs the Warning Some elevation tags could not be updated; continuing.. TESTS ./test.sh test --tool ElevationTags # pure scope, the default ./test.sh test --tool ElevationTags --scope local -y 2026 # -y 2027 for Revit 2027 Pure tests cover the rules above that need no Revit. Local tests open gm_test_model.rvt (Model paths). The workflow tests build a spot symbol from the installed template and check each Text Location in plans turned 0, 30 and 90 degrees. ElevationTagsSettingsPackViewTests lives in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tests/. SEE ALSO Hooks, Feature Warnings, Settings Packs

developer-guide/tools/common/gm-producti.title: GM Production Contracts | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/gm-producti.summary: GM Production Contracts These Global Mapper (GM) behaviors are performance or correctness requirements. Each section names the source that implements the contract and the effect of breaking it. A change to a contract is a product change; update this page with it. See Global Mapper for the tool design. Paths are relative to src/Tools/Common/GM/. Usage index sampling cap Features/Usage/Revit/Operations/Indexing/UsageIndexSource.Families.cs, QuerySampleInstanceIdsBySymbol The usage index samples one family instance per family type (symbol), at most 2500 instances (MaxSampleInstances in UsageIndexSource.cs). It streams view-independent (model) instances first and returns as soon as it has 2250 samples. Only when the model instances give fewer than 2250 samples does it add view-owned instances of the active view, up to the cap. Unbounded iteration scales with views times instances: a project with 200 views and 50,000 instances stalls for minutes. One geometry pass per usage kind Features/Usage/Revit/Operations/Indexing/StyleMaterial/UsageStyleMaterialCollector.cs, QueryStyleMaterialUsageChunk Style and material usage are captured from the same sample. Instance geometry is requested once for styles and once for materials, both with IncludeNonVisibleObjects = true. Symbol geometry is requested only when the instance has no geometry. Style geometry uses the owning or active view; material geometry uses view-independent Fine detail. Sharing one geometry result between them changes coverage. The combined chunk shares element lookup and the traversal of family-dependent styles. One instance for parameter discovery Features/Families/Revit/FamilyScanner.ParameterNames.cs, QueryMappableParamNamesForFamily Parameter-name discovery reads the parameters of every type of the family and of one instance. Parameter definitions are family-level, so every instance has the same definitions; scanning more instances adds cost and no data. Deep scan runs only on request Features/DeepScan/Workflow/DeepScanWorkflow.cs A deep scan opens family documents with EditFamily, which takes seconds per family. It runs only from a user action: Scan Family on a family row, deep scan of all visible families, or deep scan of unscanned families with zero instances (after a confirmation). Background prewarm only reads the deep scan cache; it never starts a scan. See GM specification. Parameter discovery filter Revit/ParameterDiscovery/ParameterDiscoveryEligibility.cs Discovery excludes read-only parameters, built-in parameters (InternalDefinition with a valid BuiltInParameter) and blank definition names. It does not filter on UserModifiable, because Revit can report a parameter that the API can write as not user-modifiable. Removing the read-only or built-in filter offers parameters that cannot be written or should not be mapped. Adding a UserModifiable filter hides valid mapping targets. Simple style canonicalization UsageStyleMaterialCollector.RecordStyle; Features/Usage/Revit/Operations/Indexing/UsageIndexSource.StyleMaterial.cs, BuildStyleCanonicalizationMap Style usage records the raw style ID and its canonical projection ID only. Recording every equivalent alias multiplies dictionary insertions per geometry object without improving the result. Style maps built once per usage build UsageIndexSource.StyleMaterial.cs, BuildStyleMaterialUsageAsync Style canonicalization, category projection and object-style classification run once per usage build, and their results are passed to each chunk of 25 instances (UsageChunkSize). Rebuilding them per chunk repeats a full FilteredElementCollector scan for every chunk.

developer-guide/tools/common/gm-spec.htm.summary: Global Mapper architecture specification Overview Global Mapper (GM) collects Revit content, builds mapping intent, and executes reviewed replacement plans. This specification describes its state, execution, persistence, and lifetime contracts. Source: src/Tools/Common/GM/. GM describes entry points and test surfaces. Architecture Composition and document scope App/Composition/Revit/GmModelessSessionFactory captures the launch UIDocument and Document and creates a QueuedModeless App run scope through GmSessionDocumentGate.CreateBoundScope. That helper binds the scope's concrete gate to the launch document before it returns the scope, so no consumer resolves an unbound gate. A binding failure disposes the new scope. The gate compares DocumentSessionKey values on each callback. The key uses the document hash code for session scoping. It does not guarantee collision-free identity. The persistence key is the nonblank document path, or the title|path|hash text of that captured session key for an unsaved document. Unsaved documents load saved data only under their captured session key. AddGm() registers the concrete GM gate without replacing shared IRevitCallGate registrations. Each feature registers its host-neutral services through a *ServiceCollectionExtensions class in its Composition folder and its Revit adapters through a *RevitServiceCollectionExtensions class in its Revit/Composition folder. AddGm() calls AddGmFeatureServices() in App/Composition and then each feature's Revit extension. It registers Mapping's IChangeWriter implementations before Shared Parameters adds its own. App registers only project state, UI state, session composition, and the gate. GM Revit readers, writers, family batches, transaction runners, and Commit Review consume the concrete gate. RevitMappingPlanExecutor rejects an invalid document or session-key mismatch before writers begin. RunCleanupAsync uses the underlying gate with CancellationToken.None so owned documents can close after authority or work cancellation ends. Commit Review uses the bound parent gate to create an InlineUi child scope through the same helper, bound to the expected document. It resolves apply services only after the helper returns. One outer Revit callback contains planning, modal review, apply, finalization, and refresh. During that modal session, forced-queue, off-thread, or second-callback work is refused. AppSessionProjectionBuilder.CreateProjection receives the host-neutral SessionExecutionContext, the dialog context, the mapping session, the workspace (including a required IViewOps implementation), and feature services. It returns AppSessionProjection: the panes, the session's one MappingConflictViewModel, type creation, the shared-parameter loader, and the row refresh graph. Runtime and design-time composition use that conflict instance. SessionExecutionContext carries the session's executor, logger, error notifier, operation gate, workspace signals, row signals, live-plan update suppression, and origin-clear suppression. The runtime wraps that same session context in MappingDocumentExecutionContext, exposed as Session, with its ExpectedDocument. The bound gate carries the session authorization key. Host-neutral panes and rows receive the session execution context. Commit Review receives the document execution context. Authorization identity and persistence identity have separate consumers. WindowSessionServices supplies the attached owner and progress overlay. BannerNotifierFactory uses that owner. Before Attach, every overlay member, CancelRequested included, throws InvalidOperationException. Dispose is idempotent and terminal: overlay members and Attach then throw ObjectDisposedException. The owner provider outlives disposal, so a failure notification queued after the window closes still resolves its owner. GmWindowAttachment supplies feature dialogs with a late-bound getter for the attached window. Design-time composition uses explicit host-neutral collaborators, including DesignTimeViewOps. AppSessionBuilder constructs startup, initialization, Deep Scan, preference clearing, background prewarm, Family Mapping commands, pane lifecycle, disposal workflows, and the AppSessionRuntime with its OperationStateReaction and GmWindowPresentationProjector. It passes UIStateSession.Create and SessionWorkflows.Create the session's executor, logger, and error notifier, plus the operation gate for UI state, rather than the session execution context. PaneViewModelBuilder returns PaneComposition: the panes and the Family Mapping scan, row refresh, type creation, and row set. RowRefreshFactory builds one row collaboration graph per session and returns RowRefreshComposition: CrossPaneRowRefresh, RowRefreshCoreServices, CommitReviewRowServices, UIStateFactory, and OptionRenderingRefresh. App/Sessions/RowRefresh/CrossPaneRowRefresh sequences Usage rows, Family Mapping refresh, indicators, live-update suppression, row locks, and workspace events. Each cross-pane trigger is one named method on it: RefreshRowsAfterFilterChange, RefreshRowsAfterUsagePageActivationAsync, RebuildRowsAfterInitialLoad, RefreshRowsAfterUsagePublication, ScanFamiliesAsync, RebuildRowsAfterDeepScanAsync, RefreshRowsAfterSavedMappingClear, RefreshRowsAfterCommitAndContinueAsync, and RefreshRowsAfterCommitAndClose. It implements feature-owned ICommitReviewRowRefresh, IFamilyMappingCrossPaneCommands, and IDeepScanUsageRefresh. FilterRefreshWorkflow, StartupRowWorkflow, and PageActivationWorkflow call those triggers. App/Sessions owns session records and runtime lifetime. Composition owns construction. Feature implementations do not import DBTools.GM.App. FamilyMappingFactory returns FamilyMappingComposition: FamilyMappingViewModel, FamilyMappingScanWorkflow, FamilyMappingRowRefresh, FamilyMappingTypeCreation, and one MappingRowSet spanning family/type and supplied Usage rows. FamilyMappingScanStateApplier belongs to scan sequencing. The row builders and refresh owners receive the same row set. The factory shares one FamilyMappingState across these objects. FamilyMappingState.SelectedFamilyRow holds the selected family row. FamilyMappingViewModel.SelectedFamilyRow reads and writes it, raises one notification per change, and loads the row's views when the workspace is ready and the row is not null. FamilyMappingScanWorkflow and FamilyMappingScanStateApplier capture and restore the selection on the state. Public surface and resources GM production payload types default to internal. Manifest activation requires public GmToolModule and GmCommand. Public conflict projection values retain their public binding properties. Dependency objects, converters, selectors, and attached behaviors are stable public Presentation types. The design-time view models are internal with public binding/fragment properties. Sandbox and production consume the same raw resources and fragments. Compiled resource validation checks manifest logical names. Materials and Object Styles reuse UsageFamilyListStyle, UsageFamilyItemContainerStyle, and UsageFamilyRowTemplate from Presentation/Tools/GM/GmViewResources.xaml. Each pane supplies its own family list and selection. The shell supplies double-click navigation. The row supplies the context-menu apply command. Mapping options expose nullable SimilarityScore values. Presentation GmSimilarityBrushConverter owns the brush bands: 90–100 Success, 70–89 Secondary, 50–69 Warning, and 0–49 Muted. A null score uses Body. Alphabetical rendering retains ranking Score values but leaves SimilarityScore null. The converter resolves score brushes through the owning Window resource dictionary. Missing keys yield Gray. Detached elements use their own resource scope. Blank, disabled, separator, and Deep Scan template states use DynamicResource brushes. Source reference Paths below are relative to src/Tools/Common/GM/. Contract Source Launch and document gate App/Composition/Revit/GmModelessSessionFactory.cs, Revit/Documents/GmSessionDocumentGate.cs Session graph App/Composition/Revit/AppSessionBuilder.cs, App/Composition/AppSessionProjectionBuilder.cs, App/Composition/RowRefresh/RowRefreshFactory.cs Modeless lifetime App/Sessions/Revit/GmModelessSession.cs, App/Sessions/SessionOperationGate.cs State and names Domain/ProjectStates/ProjectStateStore.cs, Domain/ElementNames/ElementNamesCache.cs Persistence App/Persistence/StatePersistence.cs, App/Persistence/UIStateCache.cs, App/Sessions/UIStateLifecycle.cs Scan admission Features/DeepScan/DeepScanOrchestrator.cs, Features/DeepScan/Refresh/DeepScanRefreshWorkflow.cs Usage publication Features/Usage/Index/UsageIndexLoader.cs, Features/Usage/Index/UsageIndexSnapshotBuilder.cs, Features/Usage/Index/UsageMatchIndex.cs Options and similarity Features/Mapping/State/MappingOptionCache.cs, Features/Similarity/Naming/NamingSimilarity.cs Execution Features/Mapping/Domain/Execution/MappingPlanExecutor.cs, Features/Mapping/Domain/Execution/MappingApplyResultBuilder.cs, Features/Mapping/Revit/Execution/Batch/FamilyBatchExecutor.cs Review Features/CommitReview/Workflow/CommitReviewApplyWorkflow.cs, Features/CommitReview/Workflow/CommitReviewFinalizer.cs Intent identity Features/Mapping/Domain/MappingIntent/MappingIntentKey.cs, Features/Mapping/Domain/MappingIntent/MappingIntentStore.cs Data and contracts Domain and feature contracts Shared value language Domain/ owns the value language that several features share, and it imports no feature namespace. Domain/Mapping owns MappingKind and its extensions. Domain/MatchingOption owns MatchingOptionKind, MatchingOptionCandidate, and MatchingOptionSortMode. Domain/Categories owns CategoryOption and CategoryReference. Mapping keeps the WPF-bearing MappingRow and MappingOption presentation types and the intent, conflict, operation, plan, and execution behavior. Project state Domain/ProjectStates owns ProjectState, family/type records, reference index/values, project parameters, scan state, projection, and the scoped ProjectStateStore. The store imports no feature or App namespace. CurrentProjectState and CurrentProjectStateCategoryId identify the loaded snapshot and its category in one replacement operation. IProjectStateBuilder and ProjectStateBuildRequest are inward contracts. App/State/ProjectStateBuilder queries Families, Usage, Shared Parameters, and Previews and projects their results into those values. Family-only refresh retains loaded Usage and Shared Parameters sections and invalidates derived usage caches before preparing rows. A failed build preserves published state. Commit Review planning builds the selected category plus pending-intent owner families without publishing. CarryForwardInto supplies loaded sections and unchanged-family Deep Scan evidence to that planning state. Duplicate detection also stays unpublished. CarryDeepScanEvidenceInto supplies only unchanged-family evidence to its fresh full state. The ProjectStateStore retains evidence across category-filtered state replacement. A rebuild restores it only when the family's type set and per-type instance counts remain unchanged. After commit, ReplaceProjectStateAfterCommit discards directly changed families and containing ancestors across all categories. Direct changes include mapped/owning families, families of mapped types, and material/object-style families found by AffectedFamilyResolver. Commit Review planning uses that same resolver. Its plan context owns planning identity and evidence. Discarding evidence removes scan state, type payloads, DeepScanResults, and fast parameter discovery together. Element names and categories Domain/ElementNames owns IElementNameQuery, ElementNamesCache, and ElementNameLookupKind. Revit/ElementName/ElementNameQuery implements the Revit adapter. App registers it with state/cache wiring. Categories registers curated-category services. ElementNamesCache exposes read-only family, type, style, material, and category name views. Each view reflects later merges and clears. Only the cache writes names: MergeNames, MergeFamilyAndTypeNames, name loading, Clear, and ClearFamilyAndTypeNames. A merged nonblank name inserts or overwrites the entry. A blank or omitted name keeps the cached entry. Strict name loading requires a nonblank cached name for every requested ID. The cache stores no blank name, so a missing name is queried again. Omitted/blank provider values stay unresolved. GetResolvedFamilyName prefers cache, then project-state family name, and throws if neither exists. GetCachedFamilyName uses the same order and returns null instead. GetCachedTypeName, GetCachedMaterialName, and GetCachedStyleName return the nonblank cached name or null. A name equal to its ID text is a name. Display getters retain explicit ID/unavailable-name fallbacks. Duplicate family and type names prefer the names captured with the detection, then cached names. A missing family, style, or material name falls back to a nonblank candidate name, then the ID text. A missing type name shows Type <id> (name unavailable). WorkspaceState.SelectedCategory is the single typed CategoryOption value exposed by IWorkspaceState. CategoryFilter derives its display label. Null and Id zero select every family. Other signed IDs select exactly that category, including negative built-in Revit IDs. Both IFamilyQuery methods use those rules. GetFamiliesAsync reuses state only when category identity matches, families exist, and all family names are nonblank. It still filters the reused result by the requested category.
