WorkspaceState.SortMode uses MatchingOptionSortMode through mutation, persistence, restoration, and option projection. CurrentProjectStateCategoryId identifies loaded state. FamilyMappingState.AppliedCategoryId identifies applied rows. Applying a different category resets category-scoped rows before application and records the category only after rows apply. Cancellation between state publication and row application therefore causes a reset on retry. Mapping intent, rows, and conflicts Features/Mapping/Domain owns immutable intent, conflict, operation, plan, and host-free execution values. It uses the shared kinds from Domain/ and does not import mutable Rows types. MappingIntentKey validates its nine-field shape through named factories and FromPersisted. It rejects invalid zero identities while retaining signed category IDs such as -2000011. MappingIntentStore stores a ParameterMappingIntentSnapshot for a Parameter key, a SharedParameterMappingIntentSnapshot for a SharedParameter key, and an ElementMappingIntentSnapshot for every other kind. An update with another snapshot type throws ArgumentException before it runs the callback or changes the store. Style and material source and target IDs are positive. AffectedFamilyResolver returns no families for a nonpositive ID. Commit Review planning fails an applied style mapping with a nonpositive source or target as an invalid mapping. The Rows package owns row-to-intent translation, projection, origin mutation, and family-apply behavior. Conflict/Rows owns row conflict matching. Detection consumes an immutable MappingSelectionSnapshot. MappingConflictWorkflow hydrates returned MappingIntentKey values into loaded rows. MappingConflictTarget defines three closed variants: a positive element selection, a type-parameter policy, or a display-only message. Resolution chooses an original side or an explicit MappingConflictBulkAction. Display labels and sentinel IDs do not encode executable policy. Duplicates implements Mapping-owned neutral selection/resolution contracts without exporting its own selection types. Mapping owns the session and document execution contexts, row signals, navigation values/lifetimes, MappingUpdateSuppression, and OriginClearSuppression. Mapping Domain/Planning owns nested-family, style, and type-reference plan language. Commit Review's CommitReviewDocumentEditBuilder owns mutable family-batch assembly. Mapping's neutral composition registers MappingIntentStore. Commit Review composition registers CommitReviewPlanVerifier. Revit/Composition registers mutation adapters, attached through AddGm. Shared Parameters implements Mapping's focused embed port and uses Mapping operation identities. Domain/Parameters/FamilyParameterDiscoveryResult carries normalized ScopedParameterName values, complete/partial state, and contextual read errors. ProjectStateStore.GetDeepScanParameterDiscoveryForFamily uses completed family scan state first, then DeepScanResults. Family Mapping uses that lookup for both scan availability and parameter names. Complete discovery supplies names. Partial discovery uses complete fast discovery when available, otherwise it clears the names. Family Mapping and Shared Parameters publish choices only from complete discovery. Their factories and consumers require IFamilyParameterQuery and ISharedParameterQuery. Shared Parameters also requires IAuthoringCategoryQuery. Duplicate parameter scoring requires complete discovery on both sides. Instance/Type suffixes are display labels. Parameter mappings retain scope and require equal source/target scope. Element identities Revit family, type, instance, material, style, view, and category IDs use long. Revit boundaries use ElementIdConverter.ToLong and FromLong. Saved-mapping and UI-state JSON accept integer-valued number tokens, including values in the 32-bit range. Family-document materials resolve by name rather than host numeric ID. Counts, indexes, depths, enum/order casts, synthetic duplicate group IDs, SharedParameterDuplicateMatcher sequence IDs, and MappingOption.StableStringId hashes use int. SharedParameterValueCopier rejects Map From values outside Int32 for Revit Integer storage. ElementId parameter destinations parse Map From text as long. Persistence and saved mappings Domain/Cache owns tool-wide cache results and metadata. Persistence adapters derive the GM root with AppPaths.GetToolCacheDir("GM"). UI-state and saved-mapping stores create their directories when writing. App/Persistence owns document UI-state storage. App/Sessions/UIStateLifecycle sequences the session's startup restore and close persistence. StatePersistence requires both IUIStateCache and ISavedMappingStore in production. Design-time projection does not construct unused persistence. JSON writes flush a unique sibling temporary file and publish it atomically. Cancellation or I/O failure preserves the last good snapshot. Only confirmed missing files/directories count as absent. Access, sharing, invalid-path, and other I/O faults propagate. UI-state and Deep Scan snapshots are disposable caches: malformed, invalid, or old snapshots are discarded and logged. Saved mappings are user data and use strict nullable-ingress validation with contextual failures. Cache results are immutable hit/miss values. Hits always contain data. Persistence and cache stores propagate unhandled failures to the operation boundary for logging. DeepScanCacheCoordinator retains warnings for hydration failures, key preparation failures, and optional cache writes. DocumentPersistenceCoordinator is a root-provider singleton shared by scoped StatePersistence and IUIStateCache instances. It owns the document gate, cache mutation gate, and separate UI-state/saved-mapping clear generations. IUIStateCache serializes asynchronous writes and document clears with the cache mutation gate. StatePersistence serializes document loads, clears, and saves and tracks separate UI-state/saved-mapping clear generations. An older open session cannot restore either snapshot after another window clears it. A freshly loaded window can persist new state. UIStateLifecycle attempts enabled close writes independently, retains failures in write order, and resets one-shot suppression even on failure. Confirmed clears drain before close persistence and disposal. PaneStateProjector supplies SavedAt. Saving preserves the supplied timestamp. Saved Mappings validates exact document identity and every persisted key before admission. Parameter mappings retain ScopedParameterName scope. The persistence port exposes load, save, and clear. MappingIntentStore owns merging. Commit Review constructs the restore workflow, merges persisted intent, and reapplies through row owners. Clearing saved mappings follows this order: Remove saved origins/selections from loaded rows. Clear mapping intent, duplicate intent, and the in-memory persisted list. Clear storage. Run the required App-bound refreshRowsAfterSavedMappingClear operation. CrossPaneRowRefresh rebuilds loaded Usage rows, refreshes Family Mapping rows, reconciles indicators under suppression, releases suppression, refreshes locks, and publishes cache status. Reapply calls Usage, FamilyMappingRowRefresh, Shared Parameters, and row locks directly. Option cache and similarity MappingOptionCache keys candidates by mapping kind, source ID, category, ordered target ID/name pairs, and source label. Category lookup does not fall back to general entries. Prewarm uses the same identity. Candidate snapshots use private read-only lists, so replacing entries cannot mutate earlier results. NamingSimilarity.Normalize and numeric-suffix stem comparison retain letters/digits in invariant lowercase. Numeric-suffix siblings with equal cleaned stems score 1.0 before Dice evaluation. Dice uses lowercased raw-name bigrams, including punctuation and whitespace, with multiplicities. Its score is twice the multiset intersection divided by the sum of raw lengths minus two. For a raw length below two, equal raw lengths score 1.0 only with equal nonempty cleaned stems. Other short-name pairs score zero. Each scoring pass owns its immutable name-profile cache. Deep Scan Deep Scan owns family scans, projection, usage resolution, feature cache, and refresh workflow. DeepScanCacheCoordinator requires DeepScanCache, IFamilyParameterQuery, and IDeepScanUsageResolver. Successful usage resolution carries Resolution, which requires its style, material, and nested-family ID collections. Failed resolution carries FailureReason. Family scan StyleIds and MaterialIds contain element IDs. ProjectStateStore.InvalidateDeepScanUsageProjections invalidates cached projections, which recompute on the next read. A user scan collects a complete family batch and finishes cache preparation before one validated ApplyBatch admission. Usage refresh data is prepared before completed scan state publishes. Cancellation or required failure before admission preserves the prior projection. Host lookup completeness is separate for styles, materials, and families. An item failure marks only its domain incomplete and prevents partial singleton-name resolution or resolver-cache reuse. Other complete requested domains remain usable. Affected families retain warning diagnostics and incomplete usage. Unexpected collector/category traversal failures abort construction. Partial parameter discovery invalidates fast choices, is omitted from duplicate scoring, and removes prior reusable cache entries before admission. A later complete query can repopulate choices. Partial usage remains visible but cannot become reusable complete cache data. DeepScanCacheCoordinator removes prior reusable entries for incomplete parameter discovery or usage scans before admission. Failure to resolve a removal identity or remove an entry propagates and prevents admission. A cache write failure without required removals logs a warning. Cache operations use a local persistence gate plus an exclusive per-file process lock. Each batch reloads authoritative disk state once while holding both. Startup hydration reads eligible families against one load. User scan removes/writes its family batch with one load and one atomic save. This serializes owners across Revit processes. Disposal drains persistence before releasing the DI-root owner. Snapshot admission validates entries and parameter/usage completeness flags as a whole. It discards incompatible snapshots rather than salvaging entries. Clear Cache holds a session-lifetime registration through deletion, projection/UI refresh, and completion. It shares session-operation admission with scans. Shutdown drains it before disposing collaborators. A confirmed clear increments DeepScanOrchestrator's generation after disk deletion and before projection clearing. Hydration rejects its whole candidate batch if that generation changes or the captured ProjectState reference changes during reading. It never replaces an already completed family scan. CrossPaneRowRefresh implements IDeepScanUsageRefresh: apply Usage data, rebuild loaded rows when needed, reconcile Family Mapping state/indicators under suppression, refresh locks, then await the Shared Parameters authoring rebuild. DeepScanRefreshWorkflow invalidates options and awaits that refresh. That rebuild evicts authoring snapshots and rebuilds the loaded tree with pending intent and selection. Completion events describe changed cache state and publish even when rebuilding faults or cancels. The outcome then propagates to the operation boundary. Eligible-cache hydration finishes only after its queued UI refresh runs. AuthoringRebuildWorkflow serializes rebuild and application. If evidence invalidates during a build, including the first build, it builds again before applying. Disposal cancels held/queued rebuilds and prevents later application. Duplicates The Duplicates feature owns detection, selections, rows, resolution, tree, pane state, and type mapping. Detection/DuplicateDetectionEngine calls the family, style, material, and shared-parameter matchers, assigns aggregate group IDs, and returns DuplicateDetectionResult. The feature's Domain, Selection, Rows, Resolution, Tree, Pane, and TypeMapping folders own their respective contracts and behavior. SharedParameterDuplicateMatcher lives beside family/style/material matchers under Detection/Matching. CurrentDuplicateDetection owns the last fully completed artifact. Detection collects its unpublished full state, executes stable DuplicateKind stages, hydrates names, then publishes and returns the same artifact reference. Earlier failure/cancellation preserves the prior artifact. Family-row counts use that same detection state. The immediate rebuild receives the artifact explicitly. Other readers inject CurrentDuplicateDetection. Cached refresh runs a worker request on the GM window's dispatcher and waits for it. A reentrant request replaces the queued request. The outer refresh runs the latest queued rebuild before returning, including propagating its failure. The debounced rebuild runs in the pane's safe-execution boundary. A failure shows one "GM Duplicates Rebuild" error banner; rows that the rebuild cleared stay cleared. Cancellation, during the delay or inside the boundary, logs at debug level and shows no banner. Each request ends its pending state, IsRebuildPending, whatever its outcome. PreviewDuplicateMatcher matches style/material candidates only when both resolve to the same signature. Unavailable previews never match, including each other. Duplicates imports neither Shared Parameters nor Commit Review. Families and Family Mapping Families' neutral composition registers FamilyQuery and IFamilyQuery. Its Revit composition registers FamilyDocumentService, FamilyScanner, and scanner ports. IFamilyScanner has two operations, GetProjectSnapshotAsync and GetFamilyIdsAsync. Both select a category with one nullable signed ID: null or 0 selects every family. Any other value, including a negative built-in Revit category ID, selects exactly that category. The snapshot's includedFamilyIds add those document families to a category scope; they do not filter. FamilyQuery converts a null CategoryOption or an Id of 0 to a null ID. FamilyDocumentService owns document lifecycle/query, not Mapping material preparation. Families consumes its own IFamilyInstanceCountQuery, implemented by Usage's live source. A thrown Document.Close or false result is a cleanup failure under the shared strict close policy. FamilyMappingViewModel owns binding state and interactions. FamilyMappingScanWorkflow owns asynchronous scan/cache/post-commit sequencing and its private scan-state applier. FamilyMappingRowRefresh owns row build/refresh, saved-mapping reapply, and usage reconciliation. PaneViewModelBuilder creates one FamilyApplyIntent and one UsageIntentReconciler on the session MappingIntentStore. The Usage pane, family presentation, and family selection receive FamilyApplyIntent. Only FamilyMappingRowRefresh receives UsageIntentReconciler. Type rows read ProjectStateStore.SymbolIds. A project-state replacement derives the store's family inventory and symbol-to-family map; a fresh scan replaces the inventory with the scanned families, their counts, and the positive type IDs of the current state; a category snapshot restore replaces it with the snapshot's copies. Ordinary category navigation reuses a category snapshot or matching loaded state. RescanFamiliesAfterCommitAsync discards every category snapshot and rebuilds from the document, including when category identity stays unchanged, so newly created types reach rows. App's CrossPaneRowRefresh sequences cross-pane work. Usage Usage owns indexing, matching/options, preview cache/versioning, rows, selection, traversal, and pane state. AppSessionProjectionBuilder constructs one UsageIndexLoader and FamilyUsage after session state, names, and operation gate exist. The loader retains those collaborators. It is not a context-free service. RebuildPlanningUsageIfNeededAsync returns Task and builds only a missing index when usage intent exists. RebuildUsageAfterCommitIfNeededAsync returns true only when it builds the index. UsageIndexSnapshotBuilder starts and drains five catalog/index tasks, aggregates non-cancellation faults, and creates an unpublished candidate without touching the match index. Name resolution, project-state usage storage, and Deep Scan refresh preparation precede publication. Index publication aligns the match index, target universe, hydration generation, and option cache. UsageMatchIndex shares one in-flight family hydration among concurrent callers. An index publication invalidates hydration started against the prior generation. UsageIndexPublished runs synchronously on the publishing thread, including workers. RowRefreshPublicationWiring dispatches row projection to the GM window's dispatcher and calls CrossPaneRowRefresh.RefreshRowsAfterUsagePublication, then the duplicate rebuild. Rows track publication version. Detect suppresses publication-driven duplicate rebuild and rebuilds once after scanning, retaining the keep target. Passive option projection suppresses intent capture. An unavailable saved target remains disabled for review. An explicit edit can clear or replace it. UsageViewModel owns target selection and bound collection/preview mutation. Selection-family flow performs one family lookup, name hydration, and row population. UsagePreviewService owns calculation, caching, and request-version order. UsageWorkflow consumes IUsageIndexLoader and its own rows without App/Family Mapping imports or row locks. CrossPaneRowRefresh.RefreshRowsAfterUsagePageActivationAsync suppresses live-plan updates across loading, reconciliation, and indicators, then refreshes locks and cache state after suppression. Shared Parameters and UI execution Shared Parameters owns domain values, authoring, formulas, Revit adapters, rows, tree, views, and pane state. SharedParameterDuplicateReconciler owns stateful duplicate-row mutation and reentrancy. SharedParameterConflictProjector performs stateless tree/Commit Review projection. SharedParametersViewModel.ViewMode (SharedParametersViewMode: ByFamily, ByParameter) selects the view. It is session state, starts at ByFamily, and is not persisted. IsByFamily drives the tree, splitter, SP Authoring pane, instance navigator, Auto-zoom and Zoom. In ByParameter, SharedParametersView hosts the raw ParameterUse/Views/ParameterUseView.xaml (ParameterUseViewXaml on GmWindowViewModel, Gm.RawView converter) with the ParameterUses view model (ParameterUseViewModel, created by ParameterUseViewModelFactory). SharedParametersViewModel implements ISharedParametersNavigation: ShowParameter(definition, repair) switches to ByParameter and selects the definition. ShowFamily(familyId) switches to ByFamily, sets ShowAllCategories when the trim hides the family's category, and selects the family's first type through SharedParameterTreeNavigationWorkflow. The category source is IAuthoringCategoryQuery. Its Revit adapter, AuthoringCategoryQuery, returns the category of every non-in-place Family in the project, annotation categories included. ICuratedCategoryQuery keeps only GetCuratedFamilyCategoriesAsync for the Families tab. The tree shows the categories that AuthoringCategoryActionEvaluator returns, unless ShowAllCategories is true. The evaluator is Pure and calls no Revit API. Its input is the authoring rows of each category for the selected SP Group (warm-up builds every category), fast parameter discovery, the SP Group definitions, the threshold, the best Map From score per family and definition from the authoring rows, the WrongGuid hint names from ISharedParameterGuidConflictQuery, the wrong-GUID and hand-fix family IDs of the latest full use scans, the intents, and the selected category. A family reason is WrongGuid, HandFix, Mappable (a missing definition with a score at or above the threshold, complete discovery only) or PendingSource (an applied MapFrom intent without a source, or an intent with HasConflict). The selected category is always returned. RefreshCategoryTrim recomputes the trim after an intent, threshold, option-rendering or scan-result change and rebuilds the tree only when the shown category list changes. The category tool tip is AuthoringCategoryAction.ToolTip. SharedParameterDefinition.Guid comes from ExternalDefinition.GUID in SharedParameterGroupQuery. Guid.Empty means the definition was not read from the file. ISharedParameterGuidConflictQuery (SharedParameterGuidConflictQuery) scans project SharedParameterElements by name and adds SharedParameterFamilyMigration.FindFamilyNames per conflicting name as HintFamilyNames. It opens no family. The conflicts drive GuidWarnings in the SP Authoring pane and the Two GUIDs in this project status in By parameter. IParameterUseQuery (Revit/ParameterUse/ParameterUseQuery) wraps Core SharedParameterUseScan.Find through GmSessionDocumentGate. It resolves the company ExternalDefinition from the open shared parameter file and passes the instance categories that project bindings of the name hold. ParameterUseQueryCache keeps reports per query key and project-state version. SharedParameterAuthoringService writes and CommitReviewFinalizer (Keep) clear it, and a clear makes ParameterUseViewModel reload its group. By parameter reads project-only reports (ScanFamilies false) for the list status and the family table. It runs a full scan, under a cancelable overlay, only for a definition in repair mode. Scan families and Scan again run the same command: it removes the selected definition's cached reports (ParameterUseQueryCache.Remove, no clear event) and scans again; the item keeps its earlier report until the new one arrives, and a cancel is not an error. LatestFullScanReports feeds HandFix and WrongGuid to the category trim and the GUID warning text. Family-table ticks write SharedParameterMappingIntentSnapshot entries through MappingIntentStore, one per family type, with the same keys that By family writes. Both views therefore share one intent store and one plan. The table omits a family whose complete discovery already has the definition name. ParameterUseSuggestionProjector scores Map From choices with AuthoringMapFromScorer. Repair ticks live in ParameterUseRepairStore, a session store per MappingIntentStore. They are not persisted. Each entry (ParameterUseRepair) holds the definition, the full-scan report and the SharedParameterRepairSelection. Ticks call SharedParameterRepairEligibility.Evaluate to open Move project binding and to show BindingBlockers. Dependent rows (Copy stored values, Move schedule uses, View filters) follow MovesBinding. PendingOperationState counts the store. CommitReviewFinalizer clears it on Keep, and RefreshAsync clears it. CommitReviewOperationBuilder.BuildOperationsAsync reads the store first. With a repair and any other pending operation, it adds RepairOnlyPlanIssue and returns no operation. PlanInitializationProjector then reports Repair must be applied on its own and disables Apply. Otherwise the plan holds one SharedParameterRepairOperation per repaired name (MappingOperationKind.RepairSharedParameter, ResolvedExecutionStage.SharedParametersRepair, ApplyChangeKind.SharedParametersRepair, stage name Shared Parameters (Repair)). A repair plan therefore never follows another stage and never reaches family-batch preparation. SharedParameterRepairWriter resolves the company definition, calls SharedParameterRepair.Plan and Apply through ISharedParameterRepairEngine inside the gate, and reports remaining hand-fix uses as operation warnings, so the result is Completed with Warnings. Core Apply scans again, compares SharedParameterRepairState, and runs both phases in its own transaction group inside the Commit Review apply group. A failure fails the operation, and GM rolls the attempt back. Binding safety: SharedParameterAuthoringService.ApplyHostBindAndCopyAsync inserts a binding only when the project has no SharedParameterElement with the GUID. An element without a binding uses SharedParameterMigration.Bind for an instance binding and refuses a type binding. A new category on an instance binding uses SharedParameterMigration.Rebind and refuses on a type binding. A change of binding kind refuses. The Map From copy runs after these in its own transaction. Before any change, SharedParameterGuidConflictGuard refuses a same-name non-shared parameter and a same-name SharedParameterElement with another GUID in the project. SharedParameterEmbedGuardedApplier also checks the family document. At plan time, CommitReviewOperationBuilder adds a GUID-conflict issue for each bound or embedded definition that ISharedParameterGuidConflictQuery reports, and Commit Review disables Apply. Map From reads numeric formula inputs at the Revit boundary. The preview evaluator does not parse displayed parameter text. Measured values use Revit's display unit. Preview output uses 15 significant digits. Numeric preview accepts signed/unsigned E/e exponents, including substituted invariant G15 values. An unresolved parameter reference or function call fails the preview, and its error names the identifier. The projector shows that error as preview-unavailable text and leaves Revit formula validation unchanged. Formula mode returns zero from the value copier without target resolution or writes. The embed applier counts authored formulas separately from value updates: one formula has authored=1, updated=0, affected=1. MapFrom retains copied-value counts. Detached Usage selection-preview and authoring property notifications use ISafeExecutor.RunWithoutThrowingAsync. The shared boundary owns logging/banners without rethrowing into WPF dispatch. Shared-parameter group/category/authoring work and contested overlay admission retain the UI context before collection mutation. Preview failures propagate to their owning command/tree-selection boundary for one report. Commit Review planning and continuation Commit Review planning resolves names, builds planning state, loads parameter groups, and prepares rows/usage inside one ISessionOperationGate operation. Collaborators do not reacquire that non-reentrant gate. The gate releases before the review dialog opens. Refresh takes a separate operation. Planning cancellation remains control flow. Other faults can produce invalid-plan state. Commit Review receives closing state and MappingSessionContext with IWorkspaceState rather than mutable App state. Planning/DocumentEdit owns mutable batch assembly. Report/OperationRows/OperationRowProjector produces family, pending, result, and error rows. Workflow owns apply/finalization. Revit/CommitReviewSessionFactory composes the child scope, planning, transaction groups, and modal presenter through the bound document gate. CommitReviewRowServices is feature-owned and constructed by App's row composition. Commit continuation uses ICommitReviewRowRefresh, implemented by CrossPaneRowRefresh. It returns Refreshed, Canceled, or NoSelectedCategory. Only a successful family scan proceeds to usage preparation, family reconciliation, and row locks. Canceled stops through cancellation. NoSelectedCategory skips refresh without a success log. Committed mappings remain persisted in either case. The refresh workflow consumes ISessionOperationGate for busy state. Commit-and-continue invalidates authoring snapshots, duplicates, and cached family views before rescanning. Returned outcomes rebuild the applied Shared Parameters tree. A successful continuation rescans Duplicates immediately when that page is active. View operations and catalogs ViewOps owns navigation. A positive missing element ID returns false without changing view or selection. Nonpositive IDs are argument errors. Unexpected Revit faults propagate. Previews owns cross-feature material/style catalogs and preview values. Line-style eligibility The shared line-style query checks the capability required by Revit commit. A grouped curve is restylable only when its group and every enclosing group have exactly one placed instance of their type. Attached detail groups also check their parent model group. Multi-instance groups are excluded before capture with their type name, placed count and Edit Group reason. GM never enters Edit Group mode and never ungroups elements. A style used only by those excluded members has no selectable source targets, even when the style remains available as a target for other sources. The writer captures every pair's population before the first pair mutates the document. Curves with no alternate Lines projection style, no resolvable projection or a non-Lines current style are also excluded. The query retains scalar curve IDs and per-source target intersections for restylable curves. It does not retain Revit wrappers for excluded members, and readback never revisits them. Each successful pair's affected count equals its pre-apply Usage quantity. A defensive group-edit failure at commit rolls back only that pair and surfaces the reason. GroupEditErrorMatcher recognizes such a failure by the failure-definition GUIDs of the commit exception (ITransactionFailureDefinitionSource), not by message text: Revit's BuiltInFailures.GroupFailures GroupPropagationFailedUngroup, GroupPropagationFailedSketch, ModifyingMultiGroups and AtomViolationWhenMultiPlacedInstances. Workflows Session operations and shutdown Domain/SessionOperation/ISessionOperationGate exposes serialized work, overlay progress, busy state, and UI cancellation. App/Sessions/SessionOperationGate implements admission and cancel-and-drain, and logs busy-step timing through its injected ILogger<SessionOperationGate>. The gate has two runners. RunImmediateOverlayAsync shows a cancelable overlay at once, renders it before the work starts, and takes no caller token. RunWithOverlayAsync takes the caller's cancelable flag, overlay options, and token. Its cancelable default is false, as for IProgressOverlay.RunAsync, so a cancelable overlay is an explicit argument. CancelActiveOperation cancels the active work token whatever the overlay flag. MappingUpdateSuppression separately controls nested live-plan suppression. Work reports progress only through the SessionOperationProgress that CreateProgressScope returns. That scope forwards steps, step advances, text, and reported steps to the gate's busy state and overlay. The Hidden (default) value ignores every call. The Domain/Workspace IWorkspaceSignals port carries feature requests for whole-window refresh. App/Sessions/WorkspaceSignals implements that port, alongside WorkspaceState implementing IWorkspaceState. An operation failure remains primary. Caller cancellation propagated through the linked work token is translated back to the caller token. Teardown independently attempts stopped-step logging, busy-state reset, and busy-text reset. The resets run directly or in one call to the GM window's dispatcher. An aborted or unscheduled dispatcher call produces one teardown failure. The linked cancellation source is always released. One failure propagates unchanged. Multiple failures aggregate in primary-first order with contextual teardown wrappers. A failing StateChanged subscriber cannot hide the work failure or skip the other reset. BackgroundPrewarm and OptionRenderingRefresh retain their transitive task and cancellation source. Replacement cancels and drains the active pair before starting the next. Each option-rendering refresh runs in a "GM Option Rendering" safe-execution boundary that waits for and disposes its predecessor even when its own token is already canceled. A refresh failure is reported once; a replacement and the close drain treat the predecessor's result as reported. The close drain throws only new cancellation or disposal failures and unexpected task faults. The session refuses ordinary close while Commit Review or Type Mapping owns an interaction. The first admitted close publishes closing state, cancels Mapping/startup, observes startup, and retains one terminal shutdown task. Repeated closes join that completion. The shutdown workflow independently attempts prewarm drain, option-rendering drain, confirmed preference-clear drain, session-operation cancel-and-drain, close persistence, and synchronous graph disposal, in that order. It then issues one terminal Close. Closed performs idempotent view-model cleanup and App run-scope disposal. Failures retain lifecycle order and do not skip later cleanup. Pane and scope collaborators remain alive until running work drains. Dev Mode retirement is synchronous and requires Idle for immediate collection. Commit Review reports Busy, so reload waits for Keep, Roll back, X, or cancellation followed by close. Revit shutdown can force ToolWindowRegistry.RetireAll. Retirement diagnoses pending work, aborts owned dispatcher operations, cancels without draining, rolls back an open apply group through the inline commit gate, disposes child/session scopes, and skips close persistence with a log entry. It opens no dispatcher frame. An existing normal-close task stops before its next stage when retirement takes over. DevModeStatus exposes Idle or Busy: <operations> in the root UI Automation ItemStatus. It includes name lookup, navigation, both auto-zoom debounces, duplicate rebuilds, Type Mapping, Commit Review, cache posts, and pending page selection. App, Family Mapping, and Shared Parameters navigation use Mapping-owned NavigationLifetime leases. Leases start inside admitted callbacks or around awaited execution. Both feature auto-zoom debounces use 200 ms and the lease token. Disposal cancels outside the lifetime lock and prevents later selection, activation, or zoom. Core alerts use observed nested modal loops and diagnose reload during a dialog. Mapping execution RevitMappingPlanExecutor validates document identity and supplies document operations to MappingPlanExecutor. MappingPlanExecutor owns the stage loop, capture boundaries, and result builder. Result accounting The MappingApplyResult constructor validates and snapshots recorded operation results. Succeeded operations require positive affected counts. Skips require zero. Failed operations can retain counts for writes completed before failure. Root succeeded/failed/skipped and affected totals derive from one recorded-result snapshot. Caller collections cannot mutate the completed result. Family success requires changed work and a successful reload. Failed-rule totals and fatal operation diagnostics must agree. Exception-backed diagnostics retain the original exception internally. MappingApplyResultBuilder logs each exception reference once with operation context. Commit Review receives stable operation text, codes, IDs, and family context. Exception types, messages, and stacks stay in logs. Writer exceptions are attributed to every unrecorded operation owned by that writer. Family cleanup always attempts close and retains close diagnostics after primary errors. Cancellation plus cleanup failures propagate primary-first through family-batch and outer writer containment. Skipped group-owned references produce Mapping warnings. An Edit Group restriction rejecting a line-style transaction at commit fails that pair. Successful sibling results retain their affected counts, but Commit Review rolls back an attempt with fatal mapping diagnostics. Writer failures A writer exception after all owned operations are recorded is a workflow failure. The result builder logs writer/stage context once and rethrows the original exception with its stack. Recorded operations alone cannot produce a successful final result in this case. With unrecorded owned operations, the executor records their failures and continues to later writers. Population capture Replacement capture precedes the first mutation that can change its population. ApplyContext captures the original symbol populations, target occupancy and type-parameter source values before the writer loop. Host material references are captured at the fixed boundary after Host recreation and before Nested Families or Type Replacements, including plans with no Host operations. They refer to recreated element IDs without consuming values introduced by later type-parameter migration or family reloads. Each family document captures all applicable material, object-style and nested-symbol references before its operation loop. Missing sources are explicit capture results. An absent source in a traversed family is zero work with a non-fatal reason. A missing host source or an ambiguous family material name remains an error. Apply never discovers an incoming population. Family material capture includes writable type parameters and the per-type defaults of instance material parameters. Revit does not allow formulas on Material data type parameters. Formula-determined parameters are outside this material replacement population. Reference kinds are explicit. Blank type names are valid and match ordinally. Capture does not change FamilyManager.CurrentType. Transactional apply restores the captured type. Object-style capture identifies the actual subcategory parameter or boundary curves of each filled region. Family-owned execution uses BatchOperationSet keyed by MappingOperation.OperationId and FamilyBatchResult.ResultsByOperationId. Style and prepared-material payloads use the same IDs. Nested, style, material, and embed dispatch uses canonical operation types and direct appliers. Each applier receives a FamilyBatchApplyContext for its family-tree node: the apply context, host document, retained family document, root family ID, path summary and family identity. The family document is null after its retained document closes; an applier requires it only when it writes. Intermediate counts must be nonnegative, and succeeded plus failed documents cannot exceed attempted. Invalid producer output fails validation. Family document lifetime Family-owned batch execution discovers the complete applicable family tree and captures each original population before applying any family mutation. IFamilyDocumentService.DescribeRootFamilyAsync returns a FamilyDocumentReference (ID, name, identity and category key), and OpenRootFamilyDocumentAsync opens the edit document from that reference. The open rejects a modifiable host document and requires the family to match the reference identity and category. When the ID no longer resolves to a matching family after a reload, a unique match by name is used. FamilyBatchDocuments retains one edit document for each family identity through capture, apply, and reload. Discovery spans the whole commit. After discovery, documents with no applicable work in themselves or their descendants are closed before apply. Remaining documents close after their last root-batch use. Final cleanup closes anything left, including after cancellation. Each release closes in reverse open order and reports individual close failures. Discovery logs the peak and retained counts and reports progress per root. Cleanup uses the underlying Revit gate without requiring the launch document to remain active or the work token to remain uncanceled. EditFamily creates independent copies, so no captured element key is carried into a second edit session. Family element references use UniqueId within their retained document plus parameter identity. Family type references use explicit reference kind, family type name, and family parameter name. Built-in parameter identity uses the typed Revit enum without narrowing its underlying 64-bit value. Document-local ElementId values remain diagnostics and population indexes only. Missing keys produce a diagnostic and do not trigger a live rescan. Shared family identity and reload Shared nested families use a name/category identity. Nonshared copies include their embedding path. Discovery opens the project's shared definition when one exists, so a parent's stale embedded copy cannot become the original population for another root. If the same shared family is reached through several roots, applicable operation populations are merged and each normalized operation is applied once. An equivalent alias receives a merged notice. If its representative fails, the alias is reported as failed as well. Conflicting targets for the same source fail preflight. After a nested or root reload, the load allowlist selects FamilySource.Family only for shared identities changed by that target traversal. Unchanged shared children use FamilySource.Project, which preserves the target document's existing child instead of reloading a stale source copy. Parent material capture excludes shared-symbol projections: the child owns those values and only surviving writes count. Before reload, project-owned shared material projections are restored from the target document explicitly. Revit can otherwise propagate those type values even when the shared-family load callback selects Project. Nonshared symbol overrides remain part of the parent population. Family results Family-document success requires both changed work and a successful reload. A failed family traversal or reload marks every operation actually executed in that traversal as failed, including merged aliases. An affected count can show writes made before the failure. The original exception remains attached to the diagnostic for logging and review. Family-document attempt/success/failure counts include every examined root and child document, including zero-work captures. A reload or close failure keeps the completed affected counts and marks the affected document operation results failed. Material projection ownership A parent FamilySymbol's material type value is a projection of the child's authored FamilyType value. When that child has the same planned material operation, the child owns the write and its count. For nonshared children, root-only operations and traversal-depth leaves retain their parent-side references. Shared projections are always child-owned. Missing captured host references produce a nonfatal diagnostic. Line-style verification Line-style query snapshots retain curve IDs and per-source offered intersections, not Revit element wrappers or target sets per curve. A line-style apply performs one fresh discovery sweep, then verifies actual styles by reading the captured IDs. Complete original-source intersections are regrouped under the final source styles. Unexpected population splits or missing curves fail verification for the committed pairs. Their operation results retain the committed affected counts, and the writer returns the errors instead of throwing away those operation results. Commit Review and the subsequent accepted Usage refresh share this result. A rollback does not publish it. CommitReviewLineStyleLifecycle exports it once, and only while the session's query cache still holds the snapshot that was current when post-apply verification succeeded. Explicit Detect and Usage refresh boundaries invalidate prior snapshots. Object-style attribution identifies the family returned by LoadFamily, its retained name, and its ownership of original instances. Style availability depends on the family category and kind. Post-apply verification Commit Review checks operation identity and successful operation results for all replacement kinds, including runtime replacements created by Create Type. Symbol and line-style counts can be checked against incoming populations. Family material and object-style Usage count families while operation results count references. An overlapping successful target is therefore checked through its operation result and writer readback, not by equating those different quantities. Commit Review results and finalization Result Contract Completed Requires MappingApplyResult and derives success from Outcome Canceled Contains neither Mapping result nor failure prose WorkflowFailed Requires a nonblank reason. Can retain a rolled-back Mapping result for diagnostics Warnings can complete successfully and remain committable. Only positive succeeded operations without fatal diagnostics project applied or persistable intent. Such an operation with no matching intent entry logs a warning and is not saved. A matching entry without persisted state, such as one with PersistSelection off, is not saved and logs at Debug. Verification requires no planned type, host, style, or material source references to remain. Otherwise the verifier's four-field failure summary blocks mapping projection. One Global Mapper: Apply session group stays open through modal review. Apply admits a reviewed plan only while CanApplyPlan is true: the plan has an operation, and validation found no nested-family replacement or type creation without a positive OwnerFamilyId. ApplyCommand checks it for availability and again when it runs. The first attempt clears it; Retry Apply is admitted by CanRetry. Apply and Retry Apply execute and verify inside an inner attempt group. Failure or cancellation rolls back the attempt and permits retry. Retry reuses the reviewed plan but constructs a new apply context and rereads the document. Keep + Continue and Keep + Close GM assimilate the session group into one Undo entry before recording mappings. Roll back, X's rollback answer, cancellation, and abnormal exit roll it back. An unknown rollback outcome propagates to the error banner rather than asserting that nothing was kept. Active-view refresh follows successful verification. A refresh warning does not disable Keep. After review closes, RefreshAfterReviewAsync refreshes GM after any admitted attempt, including failed or rolled-back attempts. Type replacements retain their selecting intent key, so acceptance records intent for its actual owner. Apply transactions log each Revit failure at Warning with definition ID and failing elements. Pre-commit issues retain their validation label. Family-document material replacement resolves source and target by material name. Errors retain planned operation ID and host source/target IDs. Family-document material IDs and affected elements are diagnostic details. Report grouping uses the owning operation even when operations share a host pair or family documents assign different IDs. Reloaded family identity Family-owned apply retains the family ID returned by Revit reload. Accepted mappings use that identity, including existing saved and pending mappings for the same family. Rollback leaves mapping identities unchanged. MappingApplyResult.ReloadedFamilyIds snapshots changed root identities. Finalization remaps applied/persistable family keys and targets before merging. MappingIntentStore also remaps existing saved/pending intents, manual family-apply state, and usage links. One replaced identity must not retain a second saved mapping. Host replacement Each host replacement is atomic per instance. Placement and required facing, hand, and point-rotation transfer must finish before source deletion. Ordinary parameter copies use best-effort transfer. A failed replacement becomes an item error only after its subtransaction reports a completed rollback. If rollback throws or reports any other status, the primary and rollback failures escape together so the enclosing transaction aborts instead of committing an uncertain document state. ParameterValueTransfer reads the target after Parameter.Set returns false. It accepts the copy as a no-op only when its storage type and value exactly match the requested source value. It applies no numeric tolerance to Double values. A remaining mismatch becomes a nonfatal HostParameterCopyWarning with the source instance, parameter, and reason. Setter exceptions remain failures. These warnings appear only after the replacement subtransaction commits. A later required-state failure rolls back and retains the fatal replacement error. Commit Review preserves each distinct diagnostic, opens the operation diagnostics section, and reports Completed with Warnings. It counts nonfatal diagnostics. Within each diagnostic-code group, it includes distinct messages in first-seen order. Code groups sort by descending diagnostic count, then by code ignoring case. Host parameter transfer treats a writable instance Phase Created value as instance-owned even when the family symbol exposes the same built-in parameter ID. The type-bound rule excludes generated IfcGUID. Revit read scheduling GmSessionDocumentGate validates Action callbacks as synchronous before wrapping their launch-document check. It rejects async void before Core can see only the synchronous decorator. Generic results also undergo synchronous-result validation. Independent reads for one action start together. Startup waits for every family-category, shared-parameter-category, and parameter-group read to settle. Ordinary startup faults take priority over cancellation. Aggregate faults contribute their non-cancellation leaves recursively. A single ordinary fault keeps its identity and stack. Multiple ordinary faults form an aggregate in family-category, shared-parameter-category, then parameter-group order, regardless of completion order. Other exception wrappers keep their context. With cancellation alone, the first cancellation in that order keeps its token. Family expansion starts view and parameter-name reads together and awaits them in original order, so the first read's failure or cancellation remains primary. Selected-type instance examples are read once through type selection. Core's queued-turn policy determines which waiting calls share a callback. Testing See Global Mapper testing for fixture ownership, hidden-desktop dialog hosting, model baselines, and run commands. Limitations Family-tree discovery retains edit documents through capture and applicable writes, so peak open-document count grows with the discovered tree. Grouped curves are eligible only when each enclosing group type has one placed instance. Family-document material replacement resolves by name, not host numeric ID.

developer-guide/tools/common/gm.html.title: Global Mapper (GM) | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/gm.html.summary: Global Mapper (GM) Overview Global Mapper finds duplicate or related Revit content, captures mapping intent, and previews and applies replacements through Commit Review. Its main window is modeless. Commit Review is modal and keeps a reversible apply group open until the user keeps or rolls back changes. The architecture specification defines state, capture, execution, and lifetime contracts. The user guide describes mapping workflows. Architecture Source and registration Source: src/Tools/Common/GM/. The assembly and tool ID are DBTools.GM. manifest.yml registers: Surface Value Module DBTools.GM.App.Composition.Revit.GmToolModule Command and availability DBTools.GM.App.Composition.Revit.GmCommand Run profile QueuedModeless Ribbon Common panel, Global Mapper, order 30, icon key gm Main raw view DBTools.ToolViews.GM.GmWindow.xaml, Modeless Commit Review raw view DBTools.ToolViews.GM.GmCommitReviewWindow.xaml, Modal Sandbox uses internal design-time view models with public binding properties: DBTools.GM.App.DesignTime.GmWindowDesignTimeViewModel and DBTools.GM.Features.CommitReview.DesignTime.GmCommitReviewWindowDesignTimeViewModel. Generated src/Tools/Common/GM/MAP.md indexes source files and manifest values. Ownership Owner Responsibility App/Composition Service registration, session and row graph construction App/Sessions Workspace implementations, cross-pane row refresh, UI-state restore and close persistence, attachment, close, shutdown, modeless lifetime App/Startup, App/Navigation Initialization, page activation, prewarm, pending navigation App/Persistence, App/State UI-state storage and feature-to-domain state construction Domain Project state and its family inventory, identity, element names, parameters, categories, workspace, cache and operation contracts Features/Categories Curated categories Features/Families Family inventory and document lifecycle Features/FamilyMapping Family/type rows, nested usage, scan, selection, and type creation Features/Mapping Intent, row-to-intent translation, conflicts, plans, and replacement execution Features/CommitReview Review planning, modal workflow, reports, verification, finalization, refresh port Features/DeepScan Family scanning, completeness, cache, hydration, refresh Features/Duplicates Detection, matching, selections, tree, and type mapping Features/Usage Indexing, options, matching, preview, selection, and usage rows Features/SharedParameters Authoring, formulas, parameter operations, rows, and tree Features/Similarity Name scoring and score presentation Features/Previews Material/style catalogs and preview values Features/SavedMappings Strict persistence envelope, clear, and reapply Features/ViewOperations View and element navigation Revit Tool-wide document and name adapters Feature packages own their local domain, planning, execution, Revit, views, and workflow where present. App composes cross-feature sequences through feature-owned ports. Features do not import App. GM identifiers spell out SharedParameter; none abbreviate it to SP. ICuratedCategoryQuery has GetCuratedFamilyCategoriesAsync for the workspace category list (Annotation Symbols, Detail Items, and Structural Framing) and GetCuratedSharedParameterCategoriesAsync for the Shared Parameters authoring categories (Doors, Mechanical Equipment, Walls, and Windows). Each returns the listed categories that the document has, sorted by label. WPF presentation GmWindowPresenter loads App/Views/GmWindow.xaml through ToolWindowFactory. Its binding source is App/ViewModels/GmWindowViewModel. Commit Review binds to Features/CommitReview/ViewModels/GmCommitReviewWindowViewModel. The runtime and design-time view models expose raw fragment bytes for six feature panes. Stable GmRawViewConverter parses those fragments. OneTime fragment bindings use the nearest categoryTabs ancestor. The host assigns shell and raw-root DataContext synchronously before the first dispatcher pump, so the first DataBind/layout pass can materialize each pane. OneTime retains it across tab switches. Feature panes bind to their feature view models. Parent commands, category selection, and empty-state labels address the shell DataContext. Stable WPF registrations, controls, converters, selectors, attached behaviors, and shared resources live in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/GM/, namespace DBTools.Presentation.Tools.GM. Each raw view merges Presentation’s Resources/Theme.xaml and references stable dictionaries with versioned ResourceUri values. GmViewResources.xaml owns Mapping and Similarity styles without a second theme merge. Payload views have no code-behind, dependency properties, or implicit payload-type templates. Bindings use INotifyPropertyChanged sources or OneTime for immutable values. Raw templates use string keys with explicit fallbacks. GmViewXaml exposes embedded bytes for raw-XAML tests and hosted views. App Pure reads the GM assembly's fixed logical resources directly. Mapping target ComboBoxes use GmComboBoxDropDownCommandBehavior. It runs the selection command at Background priority when an open drop-down closes with a different logical item. It also runs the command when WPF changes a closed combo's selection through keyboard navigation or TextSearch. WPF uses Up and Down to select adjacent items while the drop-down is closed. For noneditable combos, Left and Right also select adjacent items, and Home and End select the first and last items. Page Up and Page Down navigate only while the drop-down item host is visible. Binding, refresh, and option-population changes outside those input routes do not run the command. The open command supplies lazy options when the user opens a target combo. Commit Review owns one Revit callback around planning, ShowDialog, finalization, and refresh. Core WindowOwnerModalityScope disables Revit and other top-level windows through that callback and restores only the windows it disabled. During planning, the GM owner remains available for its overlay and Cancel action. ShowDialog disables that owner while the review dialog is visible. User close returns the session finalization. Forced retirement returns none. IsRetired is true for both outcomes and cannot distinguish them. Keep triggered from WPF Closing queues the final Close because WPF rejects reentrant Close there. Duplicate Type Mapping uses a registered modeless shell owned by GM, with Manual startup and a taskbar entry. Commit Review also retains Manual startup, an explicit finalization decision, and a cleanup close gate. Cleanup requests cancellation, waits for a safe rollback boundary, and propagates cancellation, timeout, or rollback failures. A failed cleanup leaves the review window open. Row refresh and owner closure follow successful cleanup. Design-time shared-parameter composition uses the production feature/projection graph with explicit host replacements, including NoopFamilyParameterQuery. Authoring receives a registered parameter-signature provider. Data and contracts The architecture specification defines project state, mapping intent, persistence, and execution results. Workflows Startup performance Startup logs Information-level elapsed time for five overlay steps. Usage indexing logs each catalog/index source duration and completion state. Failure or cancellation records the interrupted step and elapsed time, including queued Revit-call time. Overlay visibility is not the timing source. Family population counts use one symbol-count sweep. Type IDs retain collector order and cache per project state. View-owned collection discovers owner IDs through a quick filter, then visits eligible owners with instances, retaining Revit view-visibility filtering. Style/material indexing share one capped sample and 25-instance chunks with separate geometry options. Family-dependent styles are visited once per usage build. Each option-building pass owns immutable name profiles and retains numeric-suffix and multiset-bigram scoring. Features/Usage/FamilyFastIndex/UsageFamilyFastIndexCollector records material and object-style evidence without Revit types. It keeps distinct paths, direct and nested usage flags, and maximum depth for each positive ID. UsageFamilyFastIndexBuilder reads a placed instance through Revit and supplies traversal contexts to the collector. Row refresh and UI dispatch App/Sessions/RowRefresh/CrossPaneRowRefresh owns every cross-pane row refresh trigger and its order: filter change, Usage page activation, startup, Usage publication, category change, Deep Scan, saved-mapping clear, and commit with Continue or Close. Each trigger is a named method that documents its order. FilterRefreshWorkflow, PageActivationWorkflow, and StartupRowWorkflow call these methods. Domain/ProjectStates/ProjectStateStore owns the family inventory: FamilyIds, the positive SymbolIds, FamilyInstanceCounts, and SymbolToFamily. A project-state replacement derives the inventory from the new state. A fresh family scan and a category snapshot restore replace it through ReplaceFamilyInventory. Name resolution, initialization, Deep Scan, and snapshot storage read the store when they run. The session operation gate, pending page selection, Duplicates pane rebuilds, Usage publication, option rendering, and Family Mapping inline previews dispatch UI work through the GM window's dispatcher, which WindowSessionServices provides after the window exists. They do not use the ambient application dispatcher or the default owner registry. A failed option-rendering refresh shows one "GM Option Rendering" error banner. A replacement refresh and the close drain do not report it again. A failed debounced Duplicates rebuild shows one "GM Duplicates Rebuild" error banner. Testing Pure tests mirror App, Domain, and Features owners. Test builders, external fakes, and assertions live in Tests/Support. Project-state and name-cache tests live under Tests/Domain. Duplicate projection tests live under Tests/Features/Duplicates. The root Revit name adapter mirrors its complete path at Tests/Integration/Revit/Revit/ElementName/ElementNameQueryTests.cs. CommitReviewPlanContextTests mirrors Features/CommitReview/Planning. Saved mappings, authoring, and usage matching also mirror their subjects. UsageFamilyFastIndexCollectorTests directly tests fast-index aggregation in the Pure suite. UsageFamilyFastIndexBuilderTests checks extraction from placed instances and missing-sample handling in Revit. Tests/Integration/Revit/App/Sessions/Revit/GmModelessSessionTests.cs launches the production session through its queued App run scope and GmWindowViewModelBuilder. It observes the raw view in the stable shell on the dispatcher. Normal-close tests overlap close requests and await shared completion, shutdown, one Closed event, cleanup, and scope disposal. Retirement tests wait for Idle, retire synchronously, and check collection without another dispatcher pump. ForcedRetirement_AfterApply_RollsBackTheOpenGroupAndReturnsWithoutHanging retires after a real apply and checks model restoration and group finalization before child-scope disposal in the same Revit turn. Revit-hosted Commit Review tests use testing/TestSupport/GM/Fakes/HiddenCommitReviewDialogHost in place of ShowDialog to satisfy hidden-desktop window ownership. Its dispatcher frame ends on retirement. IToolWindowSession.Closed does not complete after forced retirement, so awaiting that event would retain the Revit callback until timeout. A 60-second deadline retires a session left open and fails the test. GM Revit-hosted fixture models, named views, family symbols, line styles, materials, and expected production outcomes are required repository baselines. Missing baselines and false production results fail with the model path and running year. Fixture teardown and transaction-group finalization failures also fail and are aggregated with a primary test failure when both occur. DBTools.GM.Pure.Tests.csproj contains owner-local fixtures and shared test support and references the desktop DBTools.GM.csproj. The production assembly grants the Pure assembly internal access. Revit references are compile-only; loading a Revit-typed member requires a Revit host. The repository wrappers run the GM checks. Run the ones that the change can affect (Choosing checks): ./build.sh BuildApp ./build.sh BuildTests ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope pure ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 The Pure project targets net10.0-windows and requires Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App. Revit-hosted tests use the local scope through the daemon fleet. Limitations The session key uses the document hash code, which can collide. The specification describes family-document and line-style limits.

developer-guide/tools/common/tdv.html.title: DBTools.TDV | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/tdv.html.summary: DBTools.TDV NAME DBTools.TDV - the assembly behind Import From Library and Export To Library SYNOPSIS source src/Tools/Common/TDV/ (MAP.md, manifest.yml) assembly DBTools.TDV entry TdvToolModule commands TdvImportCommand, TdvExportCommand (run profile InlineUi) views App/Views/TdvWindow.xaml, Features/Library/Settings/Views/LibrarySettingsView.xaml behavior src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/TDV/TdvPanZoomBehavior.cs DESCRIPTION The commands run ImportTransferWorkflow and ExportTransferWorkflow. Both use LibraryTransferWorkflow to select a library and LibraryDocumentService to open it without activating it. WindowSession then shows the modal window, and TransferExecutor copies the checked views into the destination document. The user page describes the behavior. STRUCTURE Paths are under src/Tools/Common/TDV/. Path Contents App/Composition/ TdvToolModule registers the settings section and the core.library pack. ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddTdv registers scoped services, because they need the scoped call gate and transaction runner. App/Sessions/ WindowSession implements ILibrarySelectionDialog and ITransferDialog. WindowSessionDialogRunner owns the modal loop and Dev Mode retirement. App/ViewModels/ TdvWindowViewModel partials: rows and filters, transfer and result dialog, preview. Features/Library/ LibraryCatalog, RevitYearProbe, LibraryDocumentService, the settings context and view, and the library workflows. Features/Transfer/ TransferExecutor partials, DestinationTransactionGroup, the DraftingView reader, type resolver and writer, TransferProjector, and the import and export workflows. Features/Preview/ PreviewExporter, PreviewImageExporter and PreviewCache. CONTRACTS One callback. TransferExecutor.ApplySelectionAsync throws InvalidOperationException unless RevitCallGateApiContext.IsActive is true. It also rejects one document as both source and destination. TransferExecutorTests checks the callback and cancellation guards. One group for each transfer. DestinationTransactionGroup binds to the document given to BeginAsync, rejects any other document, and never uses the active document. Each row runs in its own transaction, Transfer: <name>. FinalizeAsync assimilates the group Transfer Drafting Views on success. It rolls the group back on cancellation or an operation failure. DestinationTransactionGroup_BindsBeginItemAndFinalizeToOneNonActiveDocument checks this. Deferred success. Row successes and counts wait until the group finalization reports TransferFinalizationOutcome.Committed. RolledBack marks attempted rows TransactionRolledBack. Unknown marks them Unknown and counts no success. TransferProjectorTests checks the projection. Names. TDV adds no suffix. Blank names, duplicate names and, without Replace, existing names fail with DestinationNameRequired, DuplicateTargetName and DestinationNameConflict before the row transaction. The checks trim the names and ignore case. TransferProjector.BuildConflictRefreshAsync applies the same rules in the window. TransferProjectorTests checks them. Types. DraftingViewTypeResolver.EnsureDestType creates a missing type only for Retain Original, by duplicating the first destination drafting type in name order. A named type that is missing fails. Revit tests in TransferExecutorTests check the creation and the refusal, but not the seed order. Copy. DraftingViewWriter skips viewports, elements whose name contains ExtentElem, and the categories in s_skipCategoryNames. The check compares Category.Name with English names. It copies one element at a time with UseDestinationTypes, groups first. It pairs each source group member with its copy, so the overrides reach the members. Transfer_DraftingViewGroup_PreservesPerElementOverridesOnGroupMembers checks the overrides. Revit year. LibraryCatalog and LibraryDocumentService.OpenLibraryAsync both use RevitYearProbe. Open throws on a mismatch, so Revit never upgrades a library and CreateNewLocal never sees another version. OpenLibraryAsync_WhenFileYearMismatchesSession_FailsLoud checks this. Warning. LibrarySettingsContext.ValidateAsync fails when an entry has neither a valid main path nor a valid fallback. Validation_marks_each_tree_path_and_returns_a_contextual_failure checks this. Close. Save and sync always close the library. A Document.Close that returns false throws. When the save or sync and the close both fail, the save or sync failure comes first in the AggregateException. TryClose returns false only for the active document. LibraryDocumentServiceTests checks the failure order and the active-document refusal. Last transfer only. TransferDialogResult takes AddedCount and ReplacedCount from the last transfer in the window. ExportTransferWorkflow.SaveOrCloseLibraryAsync uses them to save or discard the library. No test runs two transfers in one window. FLOW LibraryTransferWorkflow calls LibrarySelectionWorkflow, which builds a LibraryCatalog from the settings. It throws SafeExecutionRefusedException when the settings hold no path or no valid path. OpenLibraryAsync copies a workshared library with CreateNewLocal and opens all worksets. It opens other files in place. Both use Application.OpenDocumentFile, so the host stays active. ITransferDialog.ShowDialog takes the destination, the source and the column header. An import passes the host, the library and Import?. An export passes the library, the host and Export?. After an import, TryCloseAsync discards the library. After an export with changes, SyncAndCloseAsync or SaveAndCloseAsync persists and closes it. Without changes, TryCloseAsync discards it. Then ReactivateDocument activates the host with OpenAndActivateDocument. On a failure, the workflow closes the library without saving and rethrows. A retired window (WasRetired) skips persistence. DATA Item Value Settings section Core.MasterLibrary, read into LibraryOptions.Files (MainPath, FallbackPath, Alias) Settings pack core.library, title Library Files Pack warning core.library.invalid. It disables DBTools.ExportToLibrary and DBTools.ImportFromLibrary. Cache AppPaths.GetToolCacheDir("TDV"): LibraryLocals\<ms>_<guid>\<name>_<user>.rvt and Preview\<ms>\ Preview A 1024-pixel PNG, cropped to the content. The preview export sets the application background to RGB 43, 44, 61 and restores it. PreviewCache keeps 32 images, first in, first out. Writes Destination drafting views and missing drafting view types. On export, the library file. DIAGNOSTICS Most log lines start with [TDV]. Each transfer logs Begin transfer run <id> and Completed run <id> with the counts and FinalizationOutcome. A row failure logs a warning with its exception, and the row keeps only the code and message. TESTS ./test.sh test --tool TDV # pure scope, the default ./test.sh test --tool TDV --scope local -y 2026 # -y 2027 for Revit 2027 Pure tests cover the catalog, path formatting, settings, library selection, conflict projection, rows, the preview cache and the dialog runner. Local tests cover the executor, the document service, the workflows, the window session and the view model. LibraryDocumentServiceTests includes a workshared round trip on a temporary central model. The Revit tests open gm_test_model.rvt and sgt_test_model.rvt (Model paths). TdvPanZoomBehaviorTests lives in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tests/. SEE ALSO Settings Packs, Feature Warnings, Revit Execution

developer-guide/tools/experimental/erft..title: DBTools.ERFT | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/erft..summary: DBTools.ERFT NAME DBTools.ERFT - the assembly behind the Extreme Roof Framing Tool SYNOPSIS source src/Tools/Experimental/ERFT/ (MAP.md, manifest.yml) assembly DBTools.ERFT entry ErftToolModule command ErftNewCommand (run profile InlineUi, panel Testing) hook ErftContextualRibbonInjector (Edit ERFT on contextual Modify tabs) view App/Views/ErftWindow.xaml, src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/ERFT/ DESCRIPTION FramingAdjustmentWorkflow runs both flows. RunNewModalFlow picks a target and the sources, then calls PlanPreparationBuilder.Prepare. RunEditModalFlow takes a loaded StoredPlan and calls PrepareFromStoredPlan. The window changes the tolerance and rounding of AdjustmentPlanStore.Current and recalculates. Apply runs AdjustmentPlanExecutor. Lengths are in feet, and element IDs are long. The user page describes the behavior. Structural Preview describes the 3D presenter. STRUCTURE Paths are under src/Tools/Experimental/ERFT/. Path Contents App/Composition/ ErftToolModule, AddErft (scoped services), ErftNewCommand and ErftContextualRibbonInjector. App/Sessions/ WindowSession implements IWindowSession: the modal shell, alerts, banners and the preview host. App/ViewModels/ ErftWindowViewModel, TolerancePreset. Features/Selection/ Selection filters, pickers, SourceSelectionCollector and SourceSelectionValidator. Features/Operations/ Column, beam, target geometry and member profile readers. Features/Domain/ AdjustmentPlan, FramingGraphBuilder, TargetSurfaceProjector, FramingAdjustmentFailure. Features/Planning/ Plan preparation, edit reconstruction, target re-pick, AdjustmentEvaluator and RoundingEvaluator. Features/Execution/ AdjustmentPlanExecutor and AdjustmentWriter. Features/Persistence/ StorageSchema, StoredPlanMapper and SystemPlanRepository. Features/Preview/ PreviewSceneBuilder and PreviewProjector. Features/State/ AdjustmentPlanStore holds the current plan. Features/Workflow/ FramingAdjustmentWorkflow and the IWindowSession port. CONTRACTS Sources. SourceSelectionFilter admits host FamilyInstance columns with a LocationPoint and framing with a Line that is not StructuralType.Brace. SourceSelectionPicker drops members whose structural material matches \bconcrete\b, case-insensitive. If a reader returns fewer members than the user selected, the launch fails with Selection/SourceExtractionFailed. Column check. A selection with no column must have a beam within the connection tolerance of a model column, or it fails with Selection/NoColumnConnection. The check runs on clones of the selected beams, so it changes no connection. The plan graph uses the selected members only. SourceSelectionValidatorTests checks this. Graph. FramingGraphBuilder.ConnectionToleranceFeet is 0.5 / 12 ft. A beam end connects to the first column, in selection order, whose top is within the tolerance (inclusive). A free end then connects to the nearest other beam segment that is closer than the tolerance. An end whose connection would make a cycle stays Free, with a warning. The processing order is the columns, then a Kahn sort of the beams. Among beams with no open dependency, beams that frame to columns go first, then lower IDs. FramingGraphBuilderTests checks the connections. Target. The bottom surface is every face whose normal Z, at the middle of its UV box, is -0.1 or less in host coordinates. A link uses GetTotalTransform. TargetSurfaceProjector returns the nearest point in 3D over all triangles, not a vertical intersection. Expected target failures return a TargetGeometryFailureReason, not an exception. TargetSurfaceProjectorTests checks the projection. No Revit test uses a loaded linked target. Rounding. RoundingEvaluator.ApplyRounding uses Math.Round (midpoint to even), Math.Ceiling or Math.Floor of delta / tolerance. A column, or a beam at both ends, is NoChangeNeeded when the rounded change is 0 (IsWithinTolerance: less than half the tolerance). A beam end on a beam takes the adjusted Z of the supporting beam at the XY parameter, clamped to the segment. AdjustmentCalculationTests checks the rounding and the propagation. Apply. AdjustmentWriter runs one transaction, ERFT Apply Adjustments, in the active document. It purges retired entities, sets FAMILY_TOP_LEVEL_OFFSET_PARAM, STRUCTURAL_BEAM_END0_ELEVATION and STRUCTURAL_BEAM_END1_ELEVATION, tags each changed member and saves the system. A FramingAdjustmentFailureException rolls it back and becomes a failed result. Before the writer runs, AdjustmentPlanExecutor refuses rows with Error as Apply/PlanHasErrors. AdjustmentWriterTests and FramingAdjustmentEndToEndTests check this. Snapshot. StoredPlanMapper.CreateSnapshot stores only Pending rows. SystemPlanRepository.Save replaces the one record of the system, so a later Apply drops the members that it did not change. CreateSnapshot_IncludesOnlyPendingAdjustments checks the filter. Admission. StoredPlanMapper.Deserialize requires the tolerance, the rounding mode, the Columns and Beams lists, positive element IDs, a matching SystemId and a host target or a link and linked target pair. It fails with a Storage/* code. StoredPlanMapperTests checks this. Profiles. MemberProfileExtractor places one temporary instance of each type on the lowest level and deletes it. It commits three transactions for each type in the host document, outside any group. Expected ProfileLoops/* conditions fail one type. Other faults propagate. The ExtractProfiles_* cases in PlanPreparationBuilderTests check this. Apply gate. While IsApplyInProgress is true, the session ignores Apply and Pick, and CanClose blocks closing. An expected failure keeps the window open. A thrown failure closes it and reaches the command. WindowSessionTests checks this. FLOW TargetSelectionPicker obtains a floor or roof target. SourceSelectionPicker picks the sources. SourceSelectionCollector extracts and checks them. PlanPreparationBuilder reads the target, builds the graph, calculates, and extracts the profiles before the window opens. ShowModal returns RepickTarget, Applied or Cancelled. Re-pick hides the shell, runs TargetRepickWorkflow and shows the same shell again. Edit: ErftContextualRibbonInjector reads the Tag and SystemId of the selection and chooses one system. Its RunEditFlow calls RunEditModalFlow in a command context that Core creates for ErftNewCommand. EditReconstructionBuilder reads the current geometry and offsets of the stored members. DATA All fields are simple String fields with vendor DBTools. Schema GUID Fields DBTools_ERFT_V2, on members C736C6F5-34C8-4E50-A890-E5420C3E5391 Tag (ERFT), SystemId, MemberRole (Column or Beam), OriginalOffset, Timestamp DBTools_ERFT_System_V2, on a DataStorage 06C087B9-DA5B-4E3B-9496-13C7C8732B0E SystemIdString, DataJson (camel-case StoredPlan JSON) Apply deletes entities of the retired schemas DBTools_ERFT and DBTools_ERFT_System only when the vendor and name match. It deletes a DataStorage that has no entity left. DIAGNOSTICS FramingAdjustmentFailure.Tag formats codes as [SpecFail/<code>]. Alerts and repository failures show the tag. Profile extraction logs one Info summary of total, extracted and unsupported types. TESTS ./test.sh test --tool ERFT # pure scope, the default ./test.sh test --tool ERFT --scope local -y 2026 # -y 2027 for Revit 2027 Pure tests cover the graph, projection, rounding, storage admission, preview projection and the window session. FramingAdjustmentEndToEndTests uses gm_test_model.rvt with transient host floors. A Revit 2027 case checks the cleanup of retired schemas on 2027/Regression/realtest_model.rvt without saving it (Model paths). SEE ALSO Hooks, Structural Preview

developer-guide/tools/experimental/recor.title: DBTools.RecordSet | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/recor.summary: DBTools.RecordSet NAME DBTools.RecordSet - the assembly behind Record Set SYNOPSIS source src/Tools/Experimental/RecordSet/ (MAP.md, manifest.yml) assembly DBTools.RecordSet entry RecordSetToolModule command RecordSetCommand (run profile InlineUi) views App/Views/RecordSetWindow.xaml, Features/ManageItems/Views/ManageItemsWindow.xaml controls src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/RecordSet/ policy Policies/recordset_policy.json (DBTools.ToolConfigs.RecordSet.recordset_policy.json) script Features/Operations/Cad/CoreConsole/Scripts/rs_xrefs.lsp (DBTools.ToolCad.RecordSet.rs_xrefs.lsp) DESCRIPTION RecordSetCommand calls AppLauncher.Launch, which opens the modal Record Set window. The window builds an ExecutionPlan, an ordered list of PlanItem records, and shows it as a tree. Planning reads files, Revit TransmissionData and Core Console listings, and writes nothing to the target. ExecutionPlanExecutor runs the plan and is the only writer there. The user page describes the behavior. STRUCTURE Paths are under src/Tools/Experimental/RecordSet/. Path Contents App/Composition/ RecordSetToolModule calls AddRecordSet. AppLauncher builds RecordSetWindowServices and RecordSetWindowViewModel. App/ViewModels/ The view model, in partial files. RecordSetPreviewSyncCoordinator runs the preview 350 ms after the last change. Features/Domain/ SourceFile, HostModel, PlanContext, ExecutionPlan, the plan items and PlanMessage. Features/Planning/ HostImporter, PlanningService, TargetPathRules, CadXrefDiscovery, PlanningLimits, and the Preview/ builders. Features/Execution/ ExecutionPlanExecutor, and PlanExecutionWorkflow, which owns the overlay and the result alert.
