Features/Operations/ SafeFileSystemOperations, RevitOperations, and Cad/ with CadPreviewer, CadExecutor and CoreConsole/. Features/Policy/ PolicyReader, FilePolicyEvaluator and PolicyGlobMatcher. Features/Metadata/, Features/ManageItems/ The name catalogs. The view model applies the CatalogEdit lists of MetadataCatalogWorkflow. CONTRACTS Common links. PlanningService.BuildContext counts links by ExternalReferenceKey: the full path from WindowsPathOperations.NormalizeCaseFullPath, and the LinkType. A key that occurs twice or more is common, and TargetPathRules.ComputeLinkTargetPath puts it in Common Linked Files. PlanningWorkflowTests and TargetPathRulesTests check this. Destinations. PreviewDestinationAllocator keeps one source for each destination. Another source gets name (n).ext, with the lowest free n from 2, and the plan gets a Warning. PreviewDestinationAllocatorTests checks this. Embedded policy. PolicyReader reads only the embedded resource. ValidatePolicy throws for a policy that breaks its schema, and for a root that is not a drive path or a complete UNC share. No code reads delete_mode, require_sentinel_for_delete or SafeOperationRuntime.TrashRoot. PolicyReaderTests checks this. Preflight. Before the lock, ValidatePreconditions reloads the policy, checks the root, and checks that each output path of each item is under the target. It requires free space minus max(TotalBytes, PredictedOutputBytes) to be at least min_free_bytes (10 GiB in the shipped policy). A failure writes no lock and no manifest. ExecutionPlanExecutorTests checks this. Contained writes. SafeFileSystemOperations resolves junctions and other redirects before each containment check. CAD and Revit items check their host path again directly before the adapter call. The check and the write are separate operations, so a path that changes between them is not caught. SafeFileSystemOperationsTests checks the redirects. Lock and manifest. The lock uses FileMode.CreateNew. After the lock, the executor writes a manifest with the status ok, cancelled or failed, and always tries to release the lock. cancelled needs owner cancellation, and the window passes CancellationToken.None. FailurePrecedence rethrows a single failure, or throws an AggregateException of all failures, the first one first. ExecutionPlanExecutorTests checks this. Bind All. The preview plans CadBindAllItem only when CadXrefDiscovery.BindRefusals is empty for the whole Xref graph. Before each bind, the executor lists the graph again and throws on a refusal. PreviewPlanBuilderTests and PlanExecutionWorkflowTests check this. Core Console results. CoreConsoleRuntime.RunScriptAsync accepts a run only with exit code 0 and a result file whose JSON has "ok": true. CadExecutor also requires changed to name every planned Xref, and unbound to be empty. CadExecutorTests checks this. Revit repath. RevitOperations reads desired reference data when the file is transmitted, else last-saved data. It skips PathType.Content. It resolves a relative path from the host folder, or from the central folder for a workshared local. It keeps the path type and the load state. It writes only when a reference changes, and then sets IsTransmitted = true. The Revit test TransmissionDataAdapterTests checks all but the central folder. CAD options. A null PlanOptions member follows Core Console availability in each preview, until the user changes an option. PreviewPlanStateTests and RecordSetWindowViewModelTests check this. Execute failures. ExecuteAsync runs through RunWithoutThrowingAsync with a null notifier, so no banner appears. A failure is logged once and opens the logger window. ExecuteCommand_WhenCompletionAlertFails_ContainsFailureAndRestoresBusyState checks this for one failure. FLOW HostImporter.ImportHosts calls PlanningService.ScanHost for each host. A RevitOperationException rejects only that host. Each edit clears the preview. The debounced sync calls PlanExecutionWorkflow.SyncPreviewAsync in Task.Run. PreviewPlanBuilder.BuildPlanAsync runs PreviewPlanState.Create (finds Core Console), PreviewHostPlanner.PlanHostsAndLinks, PreviewCadPlanner.PlanAsync (each DWG destination once, with the CAD settings of its first host), PlanRevitRepaths, PreviewPlanTotals.CountCopyBytes, PredictOutputBytesAsync and PreviewPlanTotals.Complete (limits, summary, fingerprint). PlanExecutionWorkflow.ExecuteAsync opens a progress overlay that cannot be canceled. The executor writes the lock and the sentinel, runs the items in order, writes the manifest and releases the lock. Progress is the weight of the completed items over the total weight. Item Segment action Weight FsCreateDirItem fs_create_dir 1 FsCopyItem, CadCopyItem fs_copy, cad_copy 3 CadRepathItem cad_repath 2 CadBindAllItem cad_bind_all 4 RevitRepathItem revit_repath 2 UIWarnItem, UIInfoItem ui_warn, ui_info 0 Each item record in Features/Domain/ passes its PlanAction and weight to PlanItem and builds its ToFingerprintSegment text. An added item type needs a case in ExecutionPlanExecutor.ExecutePlanItemAsync, which throws for an unknown item, and in ValidatePreconditions for its output paths. The fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the segments in plan order, cut to 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters. It identifies the plan in the lock and the manifest. Core Console CoreConsoleRunner writes <stem>.scr, <stem>.input.txt and <stem>.result.json in the temporary folder. The .scr file holds the script lines and then one call of an entry function. It does not load the script, because SECURELOAD refuses a file from the temporary folder. After accoreconsole.exe exits, the runner stops the Autodesk helper processes that remain in its process tree. accoreconsole.exe /i "<dwg>" /s "<stem>.scr" rs-list-xrefs result: xrefs (name, path, found, overlay, inserted, inblock) rs-repath-xrefs input: name, stored path, new path; result: changed, unmatched, failed rs-bind-all-xrefs input as above, argument BIND or INSERT; result adds bound, unbound The script writes its result with (open result "w" "utf8"), which needs the Unicode AutoLISP engine (LISPSYS 1 or 2). DATA Item Value Settings None. Names and CAD options live in the view model. Limits PlanningLimits: 80 GiB of copies, 10,000 items, and the fallback folder names Lock .recordset.lock, with the lines run_id=<run id> and fingerprint=<fingerprint> Manifest _recordset_manifests/<run id>.json: run_id, fingerprint, target_root, utc, summary (hosts, unique_links, copy_bytes, predicted_output_bytes, items) and status Run ID UTC yyyyMMdd-HHmmss and 4 random hexadecimal characters Link types RevitLink is Rvt, CADLink is Dwg, all others are Other, in DetermineLinkTypeOrThrow DIAGNOSTICS Log lines start with [RecordSet]. A Revit failure reads Revit operation '<operation>' failed for host '<path>': <reason>. A Core Console failure names the function, the DWG, the exit code, the result text, standard error and standard output, each cut to its last 2,000 characters. TESTS ./test.sh test --tool RecordSet # pure: DBTools.RecordSet.Pure.Tests ./test.sh test --tool RecordSet --scope local -y 2026 # -y 2027 for Revit 2027 ./test.sh test --tool RecordSet --fixture CadLiveTests # DBTools.RecordSet.Cad.Pure.Tests Pure tests cover planning, the policy, execution, the file system, the CAD adapters with a fake accoreconsole.exe .cmd file, and the view models. CadLiveTests is in its own project in the pure scope, so the default run skips it. It runs rs_xrefs.lsp in a real Core Console on generated drawings, and it is ignored unless ACCORECONSOLE names an existing file. Local tests cover composition, the view model in Revit and TransmissionDataAdapterTests, which opens sgt_test_model.rvt and its linked model (Model paths). SEE ALSO Revit Execution, Architecture overview

developer-guide/tools/experimental/vtc-s.title: View Template Comparer (VTC) specification | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/vtc-s.summary: View Template Comparer (VTC) specification Overview This page specifies the data contract of View Template Comparer (VTC): what it reads from a view template, how it keys and compares settings, and how it applies, copies and stores them. The VTC developer guide describes the architecture. Architecture TemplateExtractor and RevitLinkSettingsAdapter read snapshots. TemplateDifferenceEvaluator compares them; TemplateApplier applies selected changes. TemplateStorage owns cached JSON. See VTC architecture for composition and views. Data and contracts Scope VTC compares two view templates of the current document. Category edits stay staged locally until Process. Imported categories are ordinary category rows on their own tab. Revit-link settings are limited to settings that the public Revit API can both read and write. VTC reads and writes a setting through the public API or does not handle it. Tabs The tree follows the Visibility/Graphics dialog. SettingTab values: ModelCategories AnnotationCategories AnalyticalModelCategories ImportedCategories Filters RevitLinks Worksets DesignOptions CategoryTabClassifier sends a model category with a positive ID (an imported DWG, SAT or similar category) to ImportedCategories. Internal categories, which the dialog does not show, are classified as model categories. Other category types keep their native tab. Imported categories Extraction emits imported parents and their layers and subcategories as CategoryGraphicsData. Layers and subcategories inherit the imported parent's tab. Imported rows keep SettingType=CategoryOverride and use the same compare pipeline as every other category. There is no import-specific apply path. Inline edit, Inspector edit, Preview, pending overrides, batch apply, merged save and snapshot apply all use the standard category path. A selection whose side is missing resets visibility and graphics as for any other category row. Revit links Data TemplateSnapshot.RevitLinks is a list of RevitLinkSetting records: public sealed record RevitLinkSetting( long LinkElementId, RevitLinkTargetKind TargetKind, // RevitLinkType or RevitLinkInstance string LinkName, string LinkDisplayName, RevitLinkSettingKind SettingKind, RevitLinkSettingValue Value); Each row is one target and one native setting. VTC extracts both RevitLinkType and RevitLinkInstance targets; they are keyed, labeled and copied separately. Setting kinds RevitLinkSettingKind has 11 values, all members of RevitLinkGraphicsSettings: Kind Kind LinkVisibilityType ColorFill LinkedViewId ViewRange ViewFilterType Phase NestedLinks PhaseFilter ObjectStyles ViewDetailLevel Discipline The adapter binds all 11 kinds directly to typed public API members for Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027. Extraction RevitLinkSettingsAdapter.Extract enumerates link targets, reads View.GetLinkOverrides(...) (a new RevitLinkGraphicsSettings when there are none) and emits one row per setting kind. Simple settings use the native LinkVisibility or ElementId value. Phase, Phase Filter, Detail Level and Discipline use their public getter and setter and are stored as one row each. Linked element names are read from the linked document when it is loaded. These names identify Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter across models. Keys and comparison RevitLinkDiffEvaluator keys each row as link.{type|instance}.name.{LinkName}.{SettingKind}, for example link.type.name.ARCH_Model.rvt.LinkVisibilityType. LinkName is the only cross-model key. Compare, save, load and apply all use it; there is no element-ID key. If a key is ambiguous within a target kind, compare throws InvalidOperationException ("Revit link key '...' is ambiguous. ..."). TemplateDifferenceEvaluator compares typed SettingValue cases. DiffTreeBuilder groups the rows under Revit Links by LinkDisplayName, with one leaf per setting kind. Library storage TemplateStorage stores saved templates as JSON in the VTC cache directory (AppPaths.GetToolCacheDir("VTC")). It is the only code that derives cache file paths. Callers use logical template names. A rooted name, or a name with a path separator, is rejected before any path is derived. SavedTemplateInfo exposes only the name and modification time. Load and save accept only one complete TemplateSnapshot shape: required top-level members and collections must be present, explicit nulls and invalid nested elements are rejected, and the same validation runs before an in-memory snapshot is saved. There is no normalization and no recovery of other formats; incompatible data raises TemplateStorageException. Saved Revit-link rows must have a non-blank LinkName and LinkDisplayName, defined TargetKind and SettingKind values and a value valid for the kind: a visibility mode from 0 to 2, no mode for linked-view IDs, a detail level from 0 to 3, a defined discipline, and no enum value for other kinds. GetSavedTemplates returns an empty list when the cache directory does not exist, without creating it. Other enumeration failures raise TemplateStorageException (operation enumerate). TemplateExists returns false for a missing file or directory. Other probe failures raise TemplateStorageException (operation probe), so the save is refused instead of overwriting. Only SaveTemplate creates the directory. An existing name is replaced only after the user answers Replace; otherwise the file is written with overwrite disabled, so a template that another process saved under the name after the probe is kept and the save fails with TemplateStorageException. MergedTemplateBuilder writes RevitLinks rows like any other diff rows. Revit-link rows take part in Preview, Process, Create Merged and merged save. Sources: src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Domain/Template/TemplateSnapshot.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/Library/Operations/TemplateStorage.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/RevitLinks/. Workflows Apply and copy Apply Applying a Revit-link row reads the current link overrides, changes only the selected setting and writes the settings back with View.SetLinkOverrides(...). Targets are resolved by LinkName only. Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter are remapped by linked-element name. Dependent rows first set the required top-level visibility mode. A selection whose side is missing resets only that setting to its host default. Applying from the Revit-link modal uses BatchApply in one VTC Process Apply transaction, with one sub-transaction per setting and one Undo entry. A missing comparison key is an ElementNotFound conflict; an unexpected fault rolls back the whole apply. Copy The context menu of a concrete link group or leaf row (not the Revit Links tab root) has Open Revit Link Settings... and Copy Revit Link Settings To.... Opening the modal from a leaf row shows the full group of that link target, so the modal always shows all 11 kinds. A successful modal apply refreshes the main comparison. The modal and the copy command work on one template side. RevitLinkActionSourceResolver selects the only side with a value, or a viable selected side, and reports "no Revit-link value" or a real two-sided ambiguity without showing UI. On ambiguity App asks which template to use; it never defaults to Left. Copy uses TemplateRuntime.GetRevitLinkTargets() and CopyRevitLinkSettings(...) and always copies all 11 kinds. Each target is copied in its own transaction; the transactions run in the Copy Revit Link Settings transaction group (started through RevitTransactionGroups.Begin) and are assimilated into one Undo entry. An expected failure skips only that target and is logged; an unexpected fault rolls back every target. Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter are copied by finding the source linked-element name in the target linked model; raw linked-document IDs are not copied across models. If the source linked document is unloaded and the name is not available, the raw ID is reused only when source and target reference the same linked model. Otherwise copy fails. Testing See VTC testing for Pure and Revit-hosted fixture inventories. Limitations A Revit-link key must be unique within its target kind. Cross-model Linked View, Phase, and Phase Filter remapping requires the linked-element name. When the source link is unloaded, raw IDs are reused only for the same linked model; copying to a different linked model fails.

developer-guide/tools/experimental/vtc.h.title: View Template Comparer (VTC) | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/vtc.h.summary: View Template Comparer (VTC) Overview View Template Comparer (VTC) compares two Revit view templates of the current document, stages category edits locally, and applies the selected differences and eligible pending overrides through one command, ApplySelectedChangesCommand (button label "Process"). It can also create a merged template and save templates to a local library. The data contract (tabs, imported categories, Revit-link settings, keys, apply and copy rules, library storage) is in the VTC specification. Architecture Source: src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/. The manifest registers DBTools.VTC on the Testing ribbon panel with InlineUi, order 50, and icon key vtc. Command and composition VtcCommand is the Revit entry point. It validates the command context and calls App/Composition/VtcWindowLauncher. VtcWindowLauncher owns the modal launch: it resolves the document's templates, shows an alert when there are none, has VtcWindowCompositionFactory build the collaborators, and creates VtcWindowSession through Core's ToolWindowFactory. After the dialog closes it opens the logger window when Debug Mode is on. It always retires the comparer and linked-file windows; a dialog failure is reported before any retirement failure. VtcWindowCompositionFactory creates one graph per document: TemplateExtractor, RevitLinkSettingsAdapter, TemplateDifferenceEvaluator, TemplateApplier, TemplateMaterializer, TemplateStorage (cache directory AppPaths.GetToolCacheDir("VTC")) and the one document facade, TemplateRuntime. TemplateRuntime (Revit/Template) resolves template IDs and exposes compare, extract, batch apply, create merged, apply model, Revit-link targets and copy, and line and fill pattern queries. App batch-session code depends on the App/Sessions/ITemplateSessionRuntime port, which TemplateRuntime implements. VtcWindowSession owns the modal window session. ToolWindowFactory supplies the stable shell for the raw VTC view. Comparison owns the workspace, Inspector and Preview views; Library owns its workspace view; the Revit-link modal reuses the Comparison diff control. AlertPresenter is the only alert boundary in App. Composition gives the alert service only to the presenter; view models and workflows use the presenter for standard alerts, custom requests and selections. VtcWindowBatchWorkflow handles App session reactions for Process and Library work. The App view model owns Revit-link prompts, modal hosting, refresh and result presentation. TemplateRuntime passes Revit-link batch apply and copy, and the classification of expected conflicts, to Template Apply. VtcWindowCommandRuntime reports a refused operation through SafeExecutionRefusalReporter as VTC {operation}. Sources: src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Revit/Template/TemplateRuntime.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/TemplateApply/Execution/TemplateApplier.Operations.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/App/Composition/VtcWindowCompositionFactory.cs. Source layout VTC has several features under Features/, each with its own domain, planning, state, Revit and UI code: Path Content Features/Comparison Diff tree (DiffTreeBuilder, DiffTreeIndex, DiffTreeNode, DiffTreeProjector), preview projection, window comparison state (VtcWindowComparisonCoordinator), category tab classification and RevitLinkActionSourceResolver Features/Library TemplateStorage, SavedTemplateInfo, TemplateStorageException Features/RevitLinks RevitLinkDiffEvaluator, RevitLinkSettingsAdapter, RevitLinkTargetResolver, the Revit-link settings window Features/TemplateApply TemplateApplier partials, pending overrides (PendingOverrideState), apply results and conflicts, MergedTemplateBuilder, SnapshotSelectionPolicy, pattern rendering and override editors Features/TemplateComparison.cs, Features/TemplateDifferenceEvaluator.cs Host-neutral comparison result and evaluator Domain/ Tool-wide vocabulary: TemplateSnapshot, SettingDifference, SettingValue, SettingTab, RevitLinkSetting, RevitLinkSettingKind, RevitLinkSettingValue, RevitLinkTarget, RevitLinkTargetKind and the graphics data types Revit/Template TemplateExtractor, TemplateMaterializer, TemplateRuntime App/ Composition, sessions, view models, views and design-time data TemplateDifferenceEvaluator is host-neutral. TemplateExtractor and RevitLinkSettingsAdapter own the Revit mechanics behind TemplateRuntime. SettingDifference.LeftValue and RightValue hold typed SettingValue cases. Compare, apply and App code pattern-match these cases. Display settings use VTC enums (DetailLevelKind, DisplayStyleKind, PartsVisibilityMode, ViewDisciplineKind, ShowHiddenLinesMode); conversion to Revit enums happens only at the Revit API boundary. SettingPreviewItem and DiffTreeProjector.ViewFilter are Comparison contracts, so feature projections do not import App view models. DiffTreeNode holds comparison and display state only. PendingOverrideState holds pending override DTOs with no tree or UI dependency. TemplateApplyResult is the only apply outcome; the App view model (TemplateApplyOutcomeProjection) projects it onto setting keys for row feedback and filters and stores no outcome on comparison nodes. DiffTreeBuilder only builds a tree from differences. DiffTreeIndex keeps the rebuilt roots and owns key lookup, canonical node paths, selection collection in tree order and Revit-link subtree queries for the coordinator, the preview projection and the Revit-link modal. MergedTemplateBuilder (Features/TemplateApply/Planning/MergedTemplate) builds the merged TemplateSnapshot from the comparison result, the selections, the base side and the name. View-model operations only orchestrate effects. App composes outcome templates into Comparison views at runtime; Comparison raises only selected-node, override-edit and preview-setting requests for App to coordinate across panes and modals. Views VTC views are raw XAML EmbeddedResource items with explicit logical names: DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.VtcWindow.xaml (main view) DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.ComparisonWorkspaceView.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.ComparisonInspectorView.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.ComparisonPreviewView.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.DiffViewControl.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.LibraryView.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.RevitLinkSettingsWindow.xaml VtcWindowSession loads the main resource through ToolWindowFactory and owns the one-time owner attachment and cleanup. VTC has no custom close gate and no native pick loop. Shared resource dictionaries are in DBTools.Presentation/Tools/VTC/: VtcDiffViewStyles.xaml and VtcComparisonViewStyles.xaml. The namespace DBTools.Presentation.Tools.VTC holds the converters VtcConflictConverter and VtcRawViewConverter. VtcResourceTemplateSelector resolves App outcome templates and returns an empty template in a standalone view. Alert bodies use full type-name string keys with TypeNameTemplateSelector. Every content and item slot has an explicit template; immutable record values bind OneTime and mutable view-model state uses INotifyPropertyChanged. Each raw view merges Theme once, before the VTC dictionaries; the shared dictionaries do not merge Theme. Vtc.TreeView is based on the implicit TreeView style with VTC overrides; each tree sets its own scrolling and virtualization. Named item selectors set TextSearch.TextPath for prefix typing and automation names on their template text. SavedTemplateInfo, ViewFilterOption, LinePatternData, FillPatternData and TemplateOption return their display label from ToString(), so automation peers and text fallbacks show the label. Preview navigation is available only for navigable setting keys. Double-click override editing responds to the left mouse button only, on eligible rows. Keyboard focus moves to the comparison row after the Inspector tab loads. Pending focus and close requests are canceled on retirement. The linked dialog's context-menu selection commands bind to its own view model. The raw linked view has the automation name "Linked file override differences". The main window initializer uses the log prefix VtcWindow. Data and contracts The specification defines tabs, typed setting values, imported categories, Revit-link identity, and library storage. Workflows Process and merged templates ApplySelectedChangesCommand applies the selections and eligible pending category overrides in one VTC Process Apply transaction, with one SubTransaction per setting so an expected conflict rolls back only that setting. Category application checks CanCategoryBeHidden and IsCategoryOverridable before changing visibility or graphics. Unsupported visibility is skipped with a warning. When graphics overrides are unsupported, empty overrides are skipped with a warning. Required overrides produce a [VTC_READ_ONLY] conflict with kind ReadOnlyParameter. An apply failure becomes a per-setting conflict only after its sub-transaction confirms RolledBack. If the rollback throws or reports another status, the batch stops with a BatchApplyException that contains the apply failure and then the rollback failure. An unconfirmed rollback never publishes a pending-override conflict key. Create Merged (TemplateRuntime.CreateMergedTemplate) runs template creation and the pending-override batch in one transaction group, Create Merged View Template, started through RevitTransactionGroups.Begin and assimilated into one Undo entry. Expected per-setting conflicts are reported and the new template is kept. Any other fault rolls the group back and leaves no template, so a retry with the same name works. TemplateMaterializer copies the Left template with ElementTransformUtils.CopyElements and a duplicate-type handler that keeps destination types, so Revit shows no dialog. It catches no copy failure: a fault rolls back the group and reaches RunOrReport as an Error alert. VtcWindowBatchWorkflow.SavedTemplates treats template extraction or merge and the cache save or delete as the change. After that change, the list refresh has its own error boundary: a refresh failure is logged with the template name and shows one warning that the cache operation succeeded; success is shown only after the refresh succeeds. Both save commands ask Replace saved template 'X'? through AlertPresenter before they overwrite an existing name; Cancel writes nothing. Testing DBTools.VTC.Pure.Tests (no Revit host): DiffTreeBuilderTests, DiffTreeIndexTests, DiffTreeNode*Tests, DiffTreeProjectorTests: grouping, selection state and change notification, including imported-category tabs and Revit-link grouping by link name. PendingOverrideStateTests, PendingCategoryOverrideTests: staging, eligibility, restore, clear, merge-save application and failed-pending collection. TemplateApplyOutcomeProjectionTests: keyed conflict and success projection for row feedback and result filters. TemplateStorageTests: the real storage service with a temporary cache directory, including imported-category data and RevitLinks rows. The project references the VTC product assembly directly, not DBTools.App. TemplateDiffEvaluatorTests, RevitLinkDiffEvaluatorTests: snapshot comparison over SettingDifference rows. RevitLinkActionSourceResolverTests: sole-side, selected-side, ambiguous-side and no-value resolution. AlertBodyTemplateProviderTests: the provider and its raw DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml resource (WPF only). VtcRawXamlParseTests: the linked-file view's accessible name and its view model passed to the composed diff view. Raw comparison view tests use the registered ToolWindowFactory session and the stable behavior bindings. Revit-hosted tests (the local scope) in DBTools.VTC.Local.Tests open the Global Mapper (GM) and Super Girt Tool (SGT) test models, create temporary templates and roll back every change after each run: VtcWindowViewModelTests: Process, Create and link flows around real template extraction, apply and creation, alert orchestration and the Revit-link modal and copy. RevitLinkBaselineTests: extract and apply round trips of LinkVisibilityType and LinkedViewId on RevitLinkType and RevitLinkInstance targets in sgt_test_model.rvt. RevitLinkExtendedTests: the other RevitLinkGraphicsSettings members on the SGT linked model. RevitLinkSnapshotRemapTests: snapshot compare and apply with deliberately mismatched target and linked-element IDs, LinkName pairing and linked-element-name remap failures. ImportedCategoryRoundTripTests: imports a shared CAD file inside the rollback scope and checks that imported categories use the normal category compare and apply path. SgtModelExtractionTests, GmModelExtractionTests: extraction from existing views and presence of link targets in the open models. Limitations Comparison requires two view templates in the same document. Revit-link settings are restricted to the public API; linked-element remapping requires a resolvable name or the same-model ID condition in the specification.

developer-guide/tools/structural/analyti.title: DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/analyti.summary: DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel NAME DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel - the assembly behind Analytical Snap To Level SYNOPSIS source src/Tools/Structural/AnalyticalSnapToLevel/ (MAP.md, manifest.yml) assembly DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel entry manifest.yml ribbon tool, no moduleType command AnalyticalSnapToLevelCommand (run profile InlineUi) DESCRIPTION The command resolves AnalyticalSnapToLevelWorkflow. The workflow asks for a level, calls AnalyticalSnapper.Run and shows a summary alert. The tool has no settings, hooks or warnings. The user page describes the behavior. STRUCTURE Paths are under src/Tools/Structural/AnalyticalSnapToLevel/. Path Contents App/Composition/ AnalyticalSnapToLevelCommand, available through CommandAvailability.HasSelection Features/AnalyticalSnapToLevelWorkflow.cs The level picker, the run and the summary alert Features/AnalyticalSnapper.cs Run, which checks and writes each element, and the four skip reasons Features/AnalyticalSegment.cs SnapTo, the end-point rule, without Revit types CONTRACTS No module. The manifest has no moduleType. ToolModuleRibbonRegistrar registers the button, and AppToolModuleState.RegisterCommandServices adds the workflow from [CommandService]. AnalyticalSnapToLevelCommandTests checks the attribute. End-point rule. SnapTo sets both Z values of a Beam. For a Column, it sets the Z nearer the target, or the start on a tie. X and Y do not change. AnalyticalSegmentTests and AnalyticalSegmentEdgeCaseTests check this. Skips. Run checks OST_AnalyticalMember and AnalyticalMember, then TryResolveRole, GetCurve() is Line and the snapped length. The first failure is the reason. AnalyticalSnapperRevitTests and AnalyticalSnapToLevelWorkflowTests check NotStraight and WouldCollapse. One transaction. All writes run in one transaction, DB Tools - Snap Analytical Elements to Level. Run catches nothing per element, so the transaction rolls back the whole run when SetCurve fails. No test checks the rollback. Refusals. An empty selection, a cancelled picker and a model without levels throw SafeExecutionRefusedException before any write. AnalyticalSnapToLevelWorkflowTests checks the first two. FLOW Execute refuses an empty selection. PickTargetLevel sorts every Level by Elevation and calls IAlertService.SelectSingle. FormatLevel writes <name> (Elev: <elevation>) with F2 in the current culture. BuildAdjustedCurve returns null when the snapped line is shorter than Application.ShortCurveTolerance. Otherwise SetCurve writes it. The processed count includes members that do not move. The workflow groups the skips by reason, in first-seen order. It lists at most AnalyticalSnapToLevelWorkflow.MaxListedIds (10) IDs for each reason, and only the count for NotAnalyticalMember. Then it calls EnsureWindowIfDebugMode. DATA Item Value Reads The selection, Level.Elevation, StructuralRole and GetCurve(), in internal feet Writes AnalyticalMember.SetCurve only DIAGNOSTICS Log lines start with [AnalyticalSnap]. They are all Debug level: the target level, each snap or skip, and the totals. TESTS ./test.sh test --tool AnalyticalSnapToLevel # pure scope, the default ./test.sh test --tool AnalyticalSnapToLevel --scope local -y 2026 # -y 2027 for Revit 2027 Pure tests cover AnalyticalSegment. Local tests cover the command attributes, the snapper and the workflow. They create temporary analytical members in gm_test_model.rvt (Model paths) and roll them back. Without the model, they are inconclusive. SEE ALSO DBTools.FramingJoins, Revit Execution

developer-guide/tools/structural/foundat.title: Combined Foundation Tags | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/foundat.summary: Combined Foundation Tags Overview Combined Foundation Tags updates pier/footing association parameters and moves combined tags to footing corners. Source: src/Tools/Structural/FoundationTags/. The assembly and tool ID are DBTools.FoundationTags. Architecture Ownership App/Composition/FoundationTagsToolModule binds settings, registers the pack, and delegates feature registration to ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddFoundationTags. Features/UpdateCombinedFoundationTagsWorkflow and Features/Move/MoveCombinedFoundationTagsWorkflow own manual execution and completion reporting. Queued result-selection gates receive the workflow logger. Pure geometry types are Point2D, FoundationTagsPoint, FootingCornerPoints, and NearestPointResult. FoundationTagsGeometry owns SelectCornerByViewOrientation, FindNearestPoint2D, and IsValidCornerName. Commands Ribbon command Identity Split-button order Update Combined Foundation Tags DBTools.UpdateCombinedFoundationTags 0 Move Combined Tags DBTools.MoveCombinedFoundationTags 1 Both use InlineUi on the Structural panel in group foundation_tags. Their command and availability classes are UpdateCombinedFoundationTagsCommand and MoveCombinedFoundationTagsCommand under App/Composition. Icon keys are update_combined and move_combined. Organize Foundation Types occupies order 2 in the same group. Data and contracts Settings Configuration section: Tools.FoundationTags. Pack: structural.foundation_tags, titled Combined Foundation Tags. AutoUpdateEnabled defaults to true. Pattern lists default empty and resolve to: Property Default pattern TagFamilyPatterns ^DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag(?: No Elevations)?$ PierFamilyPatterns ^Foundation Pier(?: - Round)?$ FootingFamilyPatterns ^(?:Footing\|Pile Cap)-Rectangular$ The UI allows three patterns per group through Core RegexPatternListContext. It validates syntax and tracks pending changes. FamilyNameClassifier compiles the configured patterns for both workflows. Workflows Update Features/CombinedFoundationTagsUpdater collects visible FamilyInstance elements from the active view. Configured family patterns classify piers and footings. Updates affect host-document instances. Compute each pier's top as Top Level elevation plus Top Offset. Write Foundation Pier Top by GUID. Find the nearest pier to each footing using XY location points, within two feet inclusive. Write that pier's type mark to Associated Pier and its top to Associated Pier Elevation. Publish current-run result IDs and timestamped selection sets. The updater creates one Core GroupPlacementQuery.CreateRunQuery(document) per run. It caches group membership, ancestor placement checks and each group type's instance count. UpdateParameterWriter compares the current and target values before checking group restrictions. For repeated groups, it skips only changed parameters whose InternalDefinition.VariesAcrossGroups is false. Equal values succeed without writing. Varying parameters still write, so a footing can be Modified and Failed in one run. This includes nested members when any enclosing group type has multiple placed instances. A single placement remains writable. Group failures enter Failed once per element and share the ten-line detailed log limit. The final diagnostic reports the total failed/skipped count. When a pier-top write is skipped for a repeated group, its computed top remains available to footings. If computation fails, both grouped and ungrouped piers supply the stored top instead. Length parameters cannot vary between group instances, and the Revit API cannot enter group edit mode. Text parameters such as Associated Pier can vary when the project definition permits it. A missing or invalid Top Level records a pier failure. Missing Top Offset uses zero. Piers without LocationPoint cannot participate in nearest-point matching. Equal-distance ties retain the first candidate. Without a pier, the updater clears the association text to an empty string. It keeps a stored elevation and reports failure because these length parameters cannot be cleared. Parameter.ClearValue requires HideWhenNoValue, which the shipped definitions do not set. An elevation without a stored value needs no clearing. Double writes compare values rounded to two decimal places in internal feet. String comparison is ordinal. UpdateParameterWriter returns failures for missing, read-only, wrong-storage, or rejected parameter writes. The updater records these failures and continues. A footing can appear in both Modified and Failed sets when one parameter changes and another fails. Unexpected exceptions escape the parameter transaction and roll back the run. Parameter writes and selection-set publication use separate transactions inside one transaction group. The group assimilates to one Undo entry. A selection-set failure preserves committed parameter writes, then propagates after assimilation. Other failures attempt group rollback and preserve concurrent cleanup faults. UpdateRunState counts distinct element IDs and records grouped skips as a subset of Failed. UpdateRunResult contains UpdatedCount, FailedCount, GroupSkippedCount, and read-only snapshots of Modified and Failed IDs. UpdateRunMessage appends the grouped skip count and the group edit reason to the existing banner counts. Automatic runs use the same updater without a result banner. Grouped skips return successfully and do not suppress later activations. The manual workflow offers Select Modified and Select Skipped when updates exist. Those banner actions check that the source document is still active before selecting IDs. With no updates, it shows an Info or Warning toast without selection actions. If neither Modified nor Failed contains an ID, selection-set publication returns without creating or pruning sets. Selection sets use DB Tools - FoundationTags - Modified Elements (...) and DB Tools - FoundationTags - Skipped Elements (...) names with Eastern-time timestamps. Repeated names receive suffixes starting at (2). Pruning retains five sets across both kinds, ordered by descending element ID. Move Features/Move/MoveCombinedFoundationTagsRunner collects visible IndependentTag instances, resolves a tagged host or linked structural foundation, and filters tag family/type names by the configured patterns. Only the host tag moves. Linked footing geometry transforms into host coordinates. The desired name is the trimmed tag name, or its type name when the tag name is blank. Supported values are case-insensitive Top Right, Top Left, Bottom Right, and Bottom Left. The runner tessellates fine-detail footing geometry, including nonvisible objects, in the instance's local frame. Local XY extents define four rectangular corners. FoundationTagsGeometry.SelectCornerByViewOrientation labels them against the view's RightDirection and UpDirection. The edge most aligned with view-right becomes horizontal. A tie uses the second declared edge. The tag retains its current Z. Unsupported names, missing point locations, and geometry without usable corners are skips. All candidate moves share DB Tools - Move Combined Foundation Tags. Unexpected transform, geometry, tessellation, or tag-write errors log the tag ID and propagate, rolling back every move. MoveRunResult separates moved, skipped, candidate, total-view-tag, structural-foundation, and pattern-rejection counts, with rejected-name samples for diagnostics. Prerequisites and repair Manual commands and automatic updates validate shared parameters without modifying them. The required definitions are owned by Features/Prerequisite/PrerequisiteRequiredParameters: Parameter GUID Type Instance category Initial group Associated Pier a268a56a-e6c8-45ef-97a9-89a8608bc48f Text Structural Foundation Identity Data Associated Pier Elevation 56651179-1f6f-4f3b-b269-adb0532dc124 Length Structural Foundation Identity Data Foundation Pier Top 1927a728-1a38-4907-a71d-aae1c8eb5f8c Length Structural Columns Constraints The GUIDs match the company's DB shared parameter file (group DB Structural), so projects that use that file already satisfy the prerequisites. A project with a parameter that has a required name and another GUID, such as one set up with the DB Tools GUIDs used before November 2026, reports GUID_MISMATCH. When the company parameter is bound and a parameter with the name and another GUID has no binding, and loaded families show it on their types or placed elements (SharedParameterFamilyMigration.FindFamilyNames), the row reports FAMILY_GUID_MISMATCH. The description of GUID_MISMATCH, FAMILY_GUID_MISMATCH and DUPLICATE_NAME ends with up to five such family names (PrerequisiteRequiredParameterStatus.FamilyUse). The status opens no family, so a label that uses the other GUID directly does not show in it; Install/Repair finds it. The data type check uses ForgeTypeId.NameEquals, which ignores the schema version, so a parameter created in an earlier Revit (autodesk.spec.aec:length-2.0.0) matches SpecTypeId.Length of a later one. Background checks (the monitor, its retry and the automatic update) only record invalid prerequisites: they activate core.structural.combined_tags, which disables the commands, and show no banner. The commands report the problem when the user runs them. UpdateCombinedFoundationTagsCommand and MoveCombinedFoundationTagsCommand call Features/Prerequisite/PrerequisiteRepairOffer.EnsureReady before their workflow. A family document has no project parameters, so it refuses one with SafeExecutionRefusedException and leaves the warning unchanged. It returns true when every row is OK. Otherwise it activates the warning and shows one Warning alert, Required shared parameters need repair, that names the command and lists each failing parameter with its status and description, with the buttons Cancel and Repair. Repair runs EnsureInstalledAndValid with PrerequisiteRepairPrompt, owned by the command's window owner. Cancel, in the alert or in the schedule prompt, changes nothing and throws OperationCanceledException: safe execution logs one Warning, [Cancel] <command> canceled after <n>ms, shows no banner, and Revit sees Result.Cancelled. A successful repair clears the warning and shows a Success banner, Install/Repair succeeded. Run <command> again. with the repair Summary; EnsureReady then returns false, so the command returns normally without its workflow and Revit keeps the repair (Result.Succeeded). A failure of the success banner is logged and does not fail the command. A refused repair (InvalidOperationException) logs a Warning and becomes SafeExecutionRefusedException, so safe execution shows its Warning banner. The commands are the only callers of the workflows, so the workflows do not check the parameters again. Unexpected validation faults remain errors and do not assert invalid prerequisites. PrerequisiteSharedParameterInstaller reads every binding through Core's SharedParameterBindingLookup. When Revit's binding map holds a dead key (see shared parameter migration), the status rows, PlanRepair and EnsureInstalledAndValid throw SafeExecutionRefusedException with Revit's parameter bindings for this model are in an invalid state; save, close and reopen the model, then try again. and change nothing. EnsureReady lets it propagate before it activates the warning or shows the alert, so safe execution shows it as a Warning banner. Settings shows it under Status not available in place of the list, and as the status message and banner of a failed Install/Repair. PrerequisiteEvaluator classifies it as Invalid, so the monitor and the automatic update activate the warning and do not retry. Settings → Combined Foundation Tags shows the status of the active document and offers Install/Repair; the warning card's Fix action (FixLabel Install/Repair) runs the same repair. A successful repair clears the warning and re-enables the commands. Construction of the settings context is passive and leaves the list unchecked. FoundationTagsSettingsPackView binds its ShownCommand to LoadRequiredParametersCommand and runs it from its Loaded event, so the pack reads the active document each time it is shown. The view compiles into DBTools.Presentation, so it binds the command by name and does not reference the context type. The Settings window is modal, so the active document cannot change while it is open; each opening creates a new context. SettingsRuntime receives the settings host's UIApplication explicitly and classifies the active document (ActiveDocumentKind: None, Family or Project). Without a project the list stays empty, HasRequiredParameters is false, and the view shows the theme's empty state with RequiredParametersEmptyTitle and RequiredParametersEmptyDetail (No project open, A family is active, or Status not available with the failure message). CanInstallOrRepair is true only after the status of a project loaded, and gates Install/Repair; FixWarningAsync throws {action} requires an active Revit document. or {action} requires a project. The active document is a family. LoadRequiredParameters replaces immutable RequiredParameters status rows. RequiredParametersList shows one item per parameter: the name with a status chip at the right (green for OK, amber otherwise); a muted line with the data type, category and group (Length · Structural Foundations · Identity Data); for a status other than OK, the Description; and the schedule use. Data type, category and group are the required values by the names Revit shows (PrerequisiteParameterLabels): LabelUtils.GetLabelForSpec, the project's Category.Name or else LabelUtils.GetLabelFor, and LabelUtils.GetLabelForGroup. A value that Revit cannot name reads Unknown data type (<id>), Unknown category (<value>) or Unknown group (<id>), never the bare identifier. Every line wraps, so each value reads in full at any window width without horizontal scrolling or a tooltip. The list is a ListBox whose template has no scroll viewer, because the Settings page scrolls; it keeps keyboard focus, and each item exposes AutomationProperties.Name (the parameter), ItemStatus (the status) and HelpText (the description). Nothing uses its selection. The item bindings use OneTime. HasWarning belongs to the session context and is not persisted in FoundationTagsSettings. Install/Repair uses embedded definitions in group DBTools.Structural.FoundationTags. Their columns and values match the company file: VISIBLE 1, an empty DESCRIPTION, USERMODIFIABLE 1 and HIDEWHENNOVALUE 1. Only the group name differs; a project does not store it. It creates a temporary shared-parameter file, restores Revit's original shared-parameter path, and attempts temporary-file deletion. The embedded definitions supply the required parameters. EnsureInstalledAndValid(IPrerequisiteRepairConfirmation) runs a read-only preflight. PlanRepair returns the project plan without family details. It uses Core's CheckMigrate, CheckRebind and CheckBind to find value refusals. It also lists each schedule field and every rule from a view filter that Revit removes with a replaced parameter or an empty duplicate. FindScheduleFields scans main and embedded schedules. FindFilterRules lists all rules from affected filters, but it does not show their AND/OR logic or inverted rules. The confirmation tells the user to record that logic before Continue. A rebind keeps schedule fields and view filter rules. The method also plans loaded families through Core's family migration (SharedParameterFamilyMigration.Plan). It creates one SharedParameterFamilyTarget per required parameter, with the embedded definition and the required category plus every category that a matching parameter already binds. A known refusal, such as a WRONG_DATA_TYPE, a Length value on a member of a group placed more than once, or a family use that Core cannot change, stops before any change. The preflight cannot predict target-only project values that family migration creates. A later project migration can refuse after Continue when it finds a value that it cannot keep. That migration runs inside the repair transaction group, which rolls the family and project changes back. When the project plan lists schedule fields or view filter rules, the confirmation decides before any deletion. A declined repair returns a result with Canceled set and changes nothing. After Continue the repair plans again, including families, before it opens the transaction group. A refusal of either new plan stops it. If the refusals, schedule fields or filter rules differ (PrerequisiteRepairPlan.IsSameAs), it changes nothing and asks again with the new plan. A family loaded while the question was open is therefore changed or refused like any other. Repair cannot keep or recreate the listed schedule fields or view filter rules. The user adds the company parameter and restores every listed rule by hand. The repair runs in one transaction group and assimilates it only after every prerequisite is OK. A failure or refusal at any step rolls the group back and leaves the project unchanged, so the warning stays active. It first changes the loaded families (SharedParameterFamilyMigration.Migrate): each family parameter with a required name and another GUID becomes the company parameter, with its group, kind, formula, references and values, and the family is reloaded. Only then does it delete a parameter with another GUID: Revit removes a deleted shared parameter from the labels of the loaded families that use it, which is how labels lost their parameter before this order. A parameter with the required name and another GUID is a GUID_MISMATCH that moves its values to the company parameter, and an element whose two values differ refuses. An unbound company parameter can already exist because a loaded family defines its GUID. Preflight checks its first binding with CheckBind; the repair binds it after migrations and rebinds. Only a missing company parameter is created by the final install step. The repair then replaces each GUID_MISMATCH parameter through Core's shared parameter migration. A replacement keeps the old categories (a type binding becomes an instance binding of the same categories), the parameter group, the variance between group instances, and every value: element values on the same elements, and type values copied to every instance of the type. The company definition replaces the old visibility, description, user-modifiable and hide-when-no-value settings; each difference is reported. Next it rebinds an installed required parameter that is bound as a type parameter or lacks the required category (WRONG_BINDING_TYPE, WRONG_CATEGORY) through SharedParameterMigration.Rebind, which keeps its GUID, categories, group, the variance between group instances and every value, and copies each type value to every instance of that type. It then binds an existing unbound company parameter through SharedParameterMigration.Bind. The final install step creates and binds definitions that do not exist yet. Repair refuses, and changes nothing, when the old parameter or the parameter with the company GUID has another spec, when a value cannot be written or read back, when a project type-bound value has no instance, when a rebar container overrides the parameter, when a Length parameter holds values on members of a group placed more than once (Revit lets such a value change only in group edit mode and does not let a Length parameter vary between group instances), when several parameters have the required name and none has the required GUID, or when a same-name duplicate of an installed required parameter holds values (SharedParameterMigration.HoldsAnyValue); the message names each such duplicate. Repair also refuses before binding when a placed family defines the target GUID only as a type parameter in a category bound as an instance parameter. A family type parameter with no placed instance stays on its type because an instance binding does not change it. The family plan refuses, naming the family: a label or nested family that uses a required name with another GUID directly (in Revit 2027 one line per label with its detail group, position and formatting), a type parameter in a family of a category that the parameter binds as an instance parameter, a nested shared family, an in-place or non-editable family that defines the name or may define it, another data type, and an element whose family value and project value differ. Revit 2026 cannot read annotation labels, so it refuses every direct shared-parameter element. An annotation-family refusal says the labels could not be read. A model-family refusal names the direct use without calling it an annotation label. Every refusal tells the user to reload the edited family into the project. A check transaction that Revit does not roll back throws SharedParameterRollbackException; it is not an InvalidOperationException, so EnsureReady lets it propagate as a failure instead of a refusal. A write that Revit blocks for another reason takes the same path. SharedParameterMigrationException lists every value that could not be carried over. A global parameter with a required name is not a project parameter; repair ignores it. The returned PrerequisiteRepairResult holds one SharedParameterFamilyReport per replaced family parameter, one SharedParameterMigrationReport per replaced parameter, one SharedParameterRebindReport per rebound parameter, each deleted duplicate, each removed schedule field and every rule that Revit removes from an affected view filter. Settings appends its Summary to the status message and the banner: each changed family with its kept type and element values and PrerequisiteRepairResult.FamilyFileNote (the family files on disk keep the other GUID), the kept and copied value counts, the definition differences, the deleted duplicates, the removed schedule fields with PrerequisiteRepairResult.ScheduleAction (add the company parameter to each schedule again by hand), and every rule removed from an affected view filter with PrerequisiteRepairResult.FilterAction. Repair deletes a same-name duplicate of an installed required parameter (DUPLICATE_NAME) only when it holds no values, after the family step. Deleting a replaced parameter or a duplicate also removes the schedule fields that use it; Revit removes a combined parameter field whole. From each view filter that uses the deleted parameter, it removes every rule set that has a rule on the parameter, with all of that set's rules. The filter keeps its categories and other rule sets; a filter with no rules left applies to every element of its categories. SharedParameterMigration.FindFilterRules lists the rules of each removed rule set, including rules on other parameters and category rules. It does not show AND/OR logic or inverted rules, so the confirmation tells the user to record that logic before Continue. FoundationTagsScheduleFieldTests and FoundationTagsViewFilterTests check these results. Settings uses PrerequisiteRepairPrompt, the production IPrerequisiteRepairConfirmation. It shows a Warning alert through Core's IAlertService, owned by the settings window (IOwnerAwareContext), with a table of each schedule, field and parameter, a table of each view filter, rule parameter, rule and deleted parameter, the reminder to record each filter's logic, the manual steps, and the buttons Cancel and Continue (IPrerequisiteRepairConfirmation.ConfirmRemovals, asked when PrerequisiteRepairPlan.RemovesUses). Cancel leaves the status message Install/Repair canceled. Nothing changed., shows no banner and keeps the warning; this applies to the pack button, to FixWarningAsync and to Repair in PrerequisiteRepairOffer. Loading calls PlanRepair and marks each row with ScheduleUse ("Used in N schedules") and ScheduleUseDetails (one Schedule: Field line each), and with FilterUse ("Used in N view filters") and FilterUseDetails (one Filter: rule parameter, rule line per removed rule), shown at the end of that parameter's item with the WarningBar surface. Tests answer the confirmation or the alert service with fakes. The Revit API does not expose the formula of a calculated field, so FindScheduleFields cannot list a calculated field that uses the parameter. An instance binding already containing the required category remains unchanged. Hosted tests cover these paths with text and length values, extra categories, type bindings, two group instances with distinct values, a failure after values are written, an incompatible spec, and schedule fields in main, combined and embedded definitions with Cancel and Continue. Elements in design options and elements owned by another user in a workshared model are not tested. The updater accesses these parameters by GUID. The warning disables Update, Move, and Organize Foundation Types. Its title is Combined Foundation Tags Disabled. Clear it after resolving the prerequisite issue. Automatic updates and monitoring CombinedFoundationTagsAutoUpdateTask runs Update in FloorPlan and CeilingPlan views when enabled and no warning blocks it. Invalid prerequisites set the warning without a banner. NotApplicable and TransientNotReady evaluations skip execution. An unexpected runtime fault sets no prerequisite warning. Core's ViewActivationHook suppresses the failed task for that document session. PrerequisiteMonitorTask checks prerequisite state, sets or clears the warning without a banner, logs an invalid state at Information, and schedules an Idling retry for transient initialization states. PrerequisiteRetryCoordinator retains each original event source and detach callback. Evaluation faults log and can be checked again on the next view activation. The monitor disposes its own retry coordinator at synchronous App shutdown. An injected coordinator remains caller-owned. Disposed lifetimes reject scheduling. Failed-detach entries retain cleanup state without retry work. A late Idling event can retry detachment. Testing Pure tests cover geometry, rotated views, corner names, regex classification, prerequisite lifecycle, and write results. Revit-hosted tests under Tests/Integration/Revit/ cover commands, modules, updates, moves, monitoring, repair, and settings. The GM test model has the three parameters from the company file. A test that needs invalid prerequisites deletes, unbinds, rebinds or replaces a parameter with Tests/Support/FoundationTagsPrerequisiteStates inside a transaction group that it rolls back. FoundationTagsFamilyRepairTests builds families through the API with Tests/Support/FoundationTagsFamilyFixtures (a footing, a generic model with a formula and a labeled dimension, a multi-category tag that carries the parameter only in Revit 2027, because Revit 2026 refuses an annotation family that carries it, and a host with a nested family) that define the required names with other GUIDs, and checks the repair, its refusals and a second repair. The API cannot put a dimension into a group in a family, so a grouped labeled dimension is not tested. The API cannot create a label, so FoundationTagsRealtestLabelTests needs a staged realtest_model.rvt with an annotation family that uses a required name with another GUID directly in its labels: one test records what deleting that parameter does to the family, the other checks that Install/Repair refuses and changes nothing. Each test reports Ignored (skipped) when the model has no such family. The staged 2026 and 2027 models have one: the Top Right label of "DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag" shows an Associated Pier with another GUID, and the family Footing-Rectangular carries that parameter. testing/RevitTestModels/README.txt describes the case. Both tests write what they find to the test output. LeaveDeadBindingKey looks up the binding of a parameter, then changes its group variance and rolls the change back; no rollback restores the binding map, so a test calls it only in a project that it creates and closes. ./test.sh test --tool FoundationTags --scope local -y 2026 Limitations Association updates use host-document pier and footing instances. Move supports host tags referencing host or linked foundations and only the four listed corner names. Length values cannot be cleared with the shipped shared-parameter definitions. Install/Repair does not change a label that uses a required name with another GUID directly: Revit 2026 has no label API, and the Revit 2027 reference assembly exposes only reads. It refuses and names the family instead. It cannot open an in-place or non-editable family; it refuses one that defines the parameter, and one for which a rolled-back rebind of the project parameter cannot tell. Family files on disk keep the other GUID.

developer-guide/tools/structural/framing.title: DBTools.FramingJoins | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/framing.summary: DBTools.FramingJoins NAME DBTools.FramingJoins - the assembly behind Allow Join and Disallow Join SYNOPSIS source src/Tools/Structural/FramingJoins/ (MAP.md, manifest.yml) assembly DBTools.FramingJoins entry manifest.yml ribbon tools, no moduleType commands AllowJoinSelectedCommand, DisallowJoinSelectedCommand (run profile InlineUi, split button group framing_joins) DESCRIPTION Both commands resolve FramingJoinsWorkflow and call ExecuteAsync with a FramingJoinOperation. The tool has no settings, hooks or warnings. The user page describes the behavior. STRUCTURE Paths are under src/Tools/Structural/FramingJoins/. Path Contents App/Composition/ The two commands, available through CommandAvailability.HasStructuralFramingSelection Features/FramingJoinsWorkflow.cs ExecuteAsync: the selection, the filter, the transaction and the banner Features/FramingJoinsWorkflow.Core.cs ExecuteCore, the loop over JoinOperationTarget delegates Features/FramingJoinTargetBuilder.cs The category filter on plain IDs CONTRACTS No module. The manifest has no moduleType. Each command adds the workflow through [CommandService], as in DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel. FramingJoinsCommandTests checks the attribute on both commands. Targets. CollectStructuralFramingIds keeps only IDs in OST_StructuralFraming, without duplicates. The workflow keeps only FamilyInstance elements. Neither step reports what it drops. FramingJoinTargetBuilderTests checks the filter. Both ends. ExecuteCore calls the operation for end 0, then end 1, and counts a target after both calls. FramingJoinsWorkflowTests checks the calls and the count. FramingJoinsWorkflowRevitTests checks the Revit join state of a temporary beam. Failure. A failed call logs an error and throws InvalidOperationException with the element ID and the cause. The transaction then rolls back every target. FramingJoinsWorkflowTests checks the exception. No test checks the rollback. Refusals. The workflow throws SafeExecutionRefusedException for an empty selection (Select structural framing elements.) and for a selection without a framing instance (No structural framing elements in selection.). No test checks these. Info banner. The No elements were modified. banner cannot show. The workflow refuses an empty target list, and ExecuteCore returns the full count or throws. FLOW ExecuteAsync collects the targets, and builds a JoinOperationTarget for each with StructuralFramingUtils.AllowJoinAtEnd and DisallowJoinAtEnd. One transaction runs ExecuteCore: DB Tools - Allow Join Selected or DB Tools - Disallow Join Selected. NotificationBannerService.ShowToast shows a Success banner, such as Allow Join Selected with Allowed joins on <n> element(s). Then it calls EnsureWindowIfDebugMode. DATA Item Value Reads The selection and the category of each element Writes The join state at ends 0 and 1 of each framing instance DIAGNOSTICS Log lines start with [AllowJoin] or [DisallowJoin]. A failure logs Failed to apply <operation> join operation for element <id>. as an Error. Debug level adds the count. TESTS ./test.sh test --tool FramingJoins # pure scope, the default ./test.sh test --tool FramingJoins --scope local -y 2026 # -y 2027 for Revit 2027 Pure tests cover the filter and ExecuteCore. Local tests cover the command attributes and one run in gm_test_model.rvt (Model paths). Without the model or a framing type, that run is inconclusive. SEE ALSO DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel, Revit Execution

developer-guide/tools/structural/joist-g.title: DBTools.JoistGirderWeight | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/joist-g.summary: DBTools.JoistGirderWeight NAME DBTools.JoistGirderWeight - the assembly behind Update Joist Girder Weights SYNOPSIS source src/Tools/Structural/JoistGirderWeight/ (MAP.md, manifest.yml) assembly DBTools.JoistGirderWeight entry JoistGirderWeightToolModule command UpdateJoistGirderWeightsCommand (run profile InlineUi) view src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/JoistGirderWeight/JoistGirderWeightSettingsView.xaml DESCRIPTION The ribbon command and the auto-update task both call JoistGirderWeightUpdater.UpdateAll. It estimates Wt for each girder that matches the family pattern and writes it. The four patterns are .NET regular expressions from the settings. The user page describes the behavior, and Revit Execution the Core types. STRUCTURE Paths are under src/Tools/Structural/JoistGirderWeight/. Path Contents App/Composition/ JoistGirderWeightToolModule registers the settings section and pack. ServiceCollectionExtensions registers the auto-update task and the workflow. Features/Workflow/ WeightUpdateWorkflow runs the command and shows the banner. Features/AutoUpdate/ AutoUpdateTask is the view-activation task. Features/JoistGirder/ JoistGirderWeightUpdater collects, checks and writes. JoistGirderClassifier compiles the patterns. JoistGirderWeightEvaluator holds the formula. Features/Load/ Operations/ElementLoadReader reads loads, LoadParser parses text, and LoadResolutionEvaluator picks the total or dead plus live. Settings/ JoistGirderWeightSettings and SettingsPackContext, which holds the pack state and validation. Features/DefaultPatterns.cs holds the defaults. CONTRACTS One transaction. UpdateAll checks every candidate, then writes all valid girders in one transaction, Auto Update Joist Girder Weights. No test checks this. Bad pattern. A pattern that does not compile throws JoistGirderConfigurationException before any write. The workflow shows it in a banner. AutoUpdateTask also activates the pack warning. UpdateJoistGirderWeightsWorkflowTests and AutoUpdateTaskTests check this. Other auto-update failures. ViewActivationHook skips the task for the rest of the document session, keyed by DocumentSessionKey. Core's ViewActivationHookTests check the mechanism. Load groups. The same patterns find and classify the loads. ClassifyLoadGroup tries Dead, then Live, then Total, and throws if none matches. JoistGirderClassifierTests checks the groups but not the order. Empty and invalid patterns. An empty pattern means the default, in JoistGirderClassifier and SettingsPackContext.LoadCore. CollectValidationErrors reports bad patterns, and the inherited BlockSaveOnInvalid makes Save refuse them. SettingsPackContextTests checks the errors, but no test checks the refusal for this pack. Admission. ViewActivationTask.AdmitAsync reads the settings once. It skips the task when auto-update is off or the pack warning is active. AutoUpdateTask runs with that copy. AutoUpdateTaskTests checks this. One warning. GetSingleWarning requires exactly one pack warning in manifest.yml. JoistGirderWeightToolModuleTests checks its ID, pack and disabled tool. FLOW The command calls WeightUpdateWorkflow.Execute, which calls JoistGirderWeightUpdater.UpdateAll. UpdateAll collects the OST_StructuralFraming instances whose family name matches. It uses the type name only when the family name is empty. TryBuildUpdate checks Wt, number of joists, load, length and depth, in that order. The first failure is the skip reason. One transaction sets Wt. Updated counts the Set calls that do not throw, and ignores their bool result. The workflow shows the summary in a banner. Auto-update runs UpdateAll through its own TransactionRunner and InlineRevitCallGate, and discards the summary. Formula JoistGirderWeightEvaluator.EstimateWeight takes feet and works in inches. Its factors are local constants, such as allowableStress (50 ksi) and connectionFactor (0.6). N Number of Joists, used as the number of equal spaces P point load, kips, at each of the N - 1 panel points L length, in D depth, in s = L / N panel spacing R = P (N - 1) / 2 end reaction M = R L / 2 - sum of P x (distance to midspan), over the panel loads between one support and midspan F = M / (0.95 D) chord force A = F / (50 ksi x 0.6) chord area top = A L x 0.28356 lb/in^3 x 1.06 top chord weight bottom = 1.13 x top web = 0.7 x top Wt = (top + bottom + web) / (L / 12), in lb/ft DATA Item Value Settings section Tools.JoistGirderWeight, read into JoistGirderWeightSettings Settings pack structural.joist_girder_weight Pack warning core.structural.joist_girder. It disables the command DBTools.UpdateJoistGirderWeights and auto-update. The startup settings check sets it for a bad saved pattern. Reads Instance and type parameters. For loads, also each document ParameterElement whose name matches a load pattern. Writes Wt only DIAGNOSTICS Log lines start with [JoistGirder]. Debug level adds the counts and the sample skips. A bad pattern logs a Warning: Update failed for document … from the command, or Auto-update disabled due to configuration: … from auto-update. TESTS ./test.sh test --tool JoistGirderWeight # pure scope, the default ./test.sh test --tool JoistGirderWeight --scope local -y 2026 # -y 2027 for Revit 2027 Pure tests cover the patterns, formula, load parsing and settings. Local tests cover composition, the updater, the workflow, auto-update and the settings view. JoistGirderWeightSettingsViewTests lives in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tests/. The Revit tests open gm_test_model.rvt (Model paths), whose Vulcraft Joist Girder instances have no usable load. Without the model, they are inconclusive. SEE ALSO Hooks, Feature Warnings, Settings Packs

developer-guide/tools/structural/organiz.title: Organize Foundation Types | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/organiz.summary: Organize Foundation Types Overview Organize Foundation Types renames foundation family types, assigns type marks, and merges types with equal dimensions. It processes all matching types in the active document. It does not use the current selection or persistent settings. Architecture Registration and ownership Source: src/Tools/Structural/OrganizeFoundationTypes/. Owner Responsibility App/Composition/OrganizeFoundationTypesCommand Manifest command, active-document availability Features/FoundationType/OrganizeFoundationTypesWorkflow Confirmation, organizer invocation, completion alert, Debug logger window Features/FoundationType/FoundationTypeOrganizer Collection, dimension comparison, rename, merge, deletion Features/TypeMark/TypeMarkGenerator Mark generation and pure formatting helper Features/TypeMark/TypeMarkPolicy Preserve or overwrite mode manifest.yml registers DBTools.OrganizeFoundationTypes as an InlineUi split-button item in foundation_tags, order 2, icon key organize_types. Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags occupy orders 0 and 1. The structural.foundation_tags pack's core.structural.combined_tags warning disables all three commands. A typical documentation workflow runs this organizer, then Update Combined Foundation Tags, then Move Combined Tags. Data and contracts Families and parameters The family-name comparison uses StringComparison.Ordinal. Family Category Dimensions Prefix Sort order Foundation Pier Structural Columns b, h P b * h Foundation Pier - Round Structural Columns d RP Diameter Footing-Rectangular Structural Foundation Width, Length, Foundation Thickness F Width, length, thickness Pile Cap-Rectangular Structural Foundation Width, Length, Foundation Thickness CAP Width, length, thickness All sorts are ascending. Dimensions use Double parameters. Type marks use the String parameter Type Mark. Dimension text uses Revit's feet-and-fractional-inches formatter. Missing dimension parameters display ?. Duplicate keys use the nullable raw dimension values. Marks and names Family group Mark format Name format Example Rectangular pier P-{n}, starting at 1 {b}x{h} ({mark}) 2'-6"x2'-6" (P-1) Round pier RP-{n}, starting at 1 {d} DIA. ({mark}) 2'-0" DIA. (RP-1) Footing or pile cap {prefix}-{widthFeet}.{n}, starting at 0 {width}x{length}x{thickness} ({mark}) 3'-0"x3'-0"x1'-0" (F-3.0) widthFeet is the floor of the width in internal feet. Each family group maintains its own ordinal set of marks encountered during processing. Generation searches from the starting counter for an unused mark in that set. It does not reserve marks on types that have not yet been processed. The confirmation asks whether to overwrite existing marks. Yes selects TypeMarkPolicy.OverwriteExistingTypeMarks. No selects PreserveExistingTypeMarks. Preserve mode generates marks only for blank values, but still renames types and merges duplicates. SetParam leaves a missing, non-String, or read-only Type Mark unchanged, so a generated name does not guarantee a mark write. Workflows Processing and transactions Collect and sort the four family groups. Compare each type's dimension tuple with retained types in its group. For a duplicate, reassign its instances to the retained type. For a retained type, assign its mark when permitted and rename it. Delete successfully merged source types after processing the group. The first successfully retained type for a dimension tuple becomes the merge target. Dimension comparison is exact. Each rename/mark operation and duplicate reassignment runs through a nested transaction-runner call. A failed reassignment rolls back that type's changes and records a skip. The organizer deletes a duplicate only after all its instances change type. All groups share the outer DB Tools - Organize Foundation Types transaction. A deletion error logs at Error and propagates, rolling back the complete operation. Per-type failures log at Debug and increment the skip count. The final warning and completion alert include skipped totals and up to five type id: reason samples. The alert also reports renamed and merged counts. Testing Pure TypeMarkGeneratorTests covers sequential numbering, gaps, width groups, prefixes, and invalid arguments. Revit-hosted OrganizeFoundationTypesTests covers confirmation, completion reporting, duplicate merges, and document changes inside a rolled-back fixture transaction group. Limitations Family names must match the four listed names exactly. Dimension equality is exact, including missing values; missing dimensions can therefore cause types to merge.

developer-guide/tools/structural/sgt.htm.title: DBTools.SGT | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/sgt.htm.summary: DBTools.SGT NAME DBTools.SGT - the assembly behind Super Girt Tool SYNOPSIS source src/Tools/Structural/SGT/ (MAP.md, manifest.yml) assembly DBTools.SGT (net10.0-windows; net10.0 portable build for pure tests) entry SgtToolModule command SgtCommand (run profile InlineUi) hook ContextualEditHook (Edit SGT Wall on Modify | Structural Framing) window App/Views/SgtWindow.xaml (raw embedded XAML; sandbox window DBTools.SGT.Main) stable src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/SGT/, src/DBTools.Presentation/StructuralPreview/ DESCRIPTION SgtCommand launches NewSessionWorkflow, which calls SgtWindowSession.RunModalFlowAsync. ContextualEditHook calls it directly with a WindowSessionLaunchRequest: New with a wall target, or Edit with a SystemId. The session owns one transaction group for the life of the modal window. Wall analysis builds a Plan; the window edits it through PlanStore; preview and placement read the same resolved member contracts. The user page describes the behavior, and Structural Preview the 3D host. STRUCTURE Paths are under src/Tools/Structural/SGT/. Path Contents App/Composition/ SgtToolModule, SgtCommand, ContextualEdit/ and every service registration (ServiceCollectionExtensions and the feature *ServiceCollectionExtensions). App/Startup/, App/Sessions/ NewSessionWorkflow, StartupAnalysisWorkflow, SgtWindowSession, WindowSessionLifecycle, WindowSessionBuilder, SessionAnalysisOwner. App/State/PlanSynchronization/ PlanSynchronizationCoordinator writes grid values into the plan. App/Views/, App/ViewModels/ SgtWindow, SgtWindowViewModel, and the preview view and presenter. The presenter is in App because it routes grid input through WindowSessionSurfaceCoordinator. Domain/ Plan, PlanStore, geometry, segmentation, gaps and resolved member contracts. Features/ BulkEdit, ChangeReview, Girt, Openings, Orientation, Placement, Preview, SegmentFlyout, WallAnalysis. Revit code is in their Revit/ folders. Persistence/ SystemStorageMapper, StoredSystem, ISystemRepository, Revit/SystemRepository, Revit/SgtSchemaContract, ElementTagSchema. Revit/ Shared adapters: family symbols, framing parameters and wall frames. TemporaryTransactionRunner rolls back probe edits; CommittedWrite runs a write that must commit, and maps a refusal to Transaction/NotCommitted. Presentation holds the stable WPF side: the grid and preview behaviors and drag input in Tools/SGT/, and the Helix viewport behind IStructuralPreview3D. SGT code has no Helix reference. CONTRACTS One session group. SgtWindowSession.Start refuses an IRevitCallGate whose RunsInline is false, and a document whose IsModifiable is true, because a transaction is already open. It begins the group Super Girt Tool, then runs PurgeUnsupportedAsync inside it. A command uses ordinary transactions inside the group, and never starts or ends a group of its own. SgtWindowSessionTests checks the refusals. Commit only on success. WindowSessionLifecycle.FinalizeSession assimilates the group only when all of these hold: the close requests a commit, startup succeeded, no failure is recorded, and IsGroupHealthyAsync is true. Every other end rolls back: Cancel, the window's close box, a failed command, a handled UI error, and retirement of the window by its shell. WindowSessionLifecycleTests checks this. Plan admission. PlanStore.Initialize and Update change a detached copy and validate it with PlanAdmissionValidator before they replace the plan. A rejected or unchanged candidate keeps the plan and its Version. PlanStoreUpdatePolicyTests and PlanAdmissionValidatorTests check this. One segmentation. GirtSegmentBoundarySet.Split is the only girt segment computation. Plan-row segmentation, the preview, placement and the usable-span check all call it. GirtSegmentBoundarySetTests checks the rules, and PreviewPlacementParityTests the shared use. One resolved member. ResolvedMemberContractResolver builds one ResolvedMemberContract per member, and OpeningMemberContractCatalog lists the opening segments once.
