The preview modes and WallSystemWriter read these values and compute no transform of their own. PreviewPlacementParityTests compares the preview with the placed members. Write order. Profile warming places temporary instances (TemporaryTransactionRunner) to capture each section. It and placement set the cross-section rotation, then Flip, then Y and Z justification, then set the offsets to zero. Jambs add the WallRotationCompensationEvaluator angle to the rotation; the grid rows still show 0, 90, 180 or 270. FamilyInstanceMutatorTests and WallRotationCompensationEvaluatorTests check this. Storage format. SystemStorageMapper reads and writes format version 3 only. Every transport field is JsonRequired. It rejects unknown fields, numeric enum tokens and payloads over 4,000,000 characters. It migrates nothing: PurgeUnsupportedAsync removes the storage and member tags of other formats, and the tags of systems with no current storage. It keeps the members. SystemStorageMapperTests and SystemRepositoryTests check this. Ownership. SgtSchemaContract.TryGetOwnedSystemId owns an element only if it is Structural Framing and its tag has the marker SGT and a system ID. Selection, update, deletion and deconstruction use it. ContextualEditTargetEvaluatorTests checks this. Update by identity. WallSystemWriter indexes the owned members by role and tag identity. It moves each match in place, creates a member for a target without a match, and deletes owned members that no target uses. Two owned members with one identity fail with Update/DuplicateIdentity. WallSystemWriter.UpdatesTests checks this. Layers. Domain uses no App, Features, Persistence, WPF or Revit API code. Features use no App code, and Placement uses no WallAnalysis code. The portable net10.0 build has no Revit API, WPF or Presentation reference, and build/MSBuild/Portable.targets excludes .cs files under App/, Revit/, Views/ and DesignTime/. Other code that uses them does not build. Nothing checks the Domain-to-Features, Domain-to-Persistence or Placement-to-WallAnalysis rules. Raw XAML. The XAML is embedded as DBTools.ToolViews.SGT.<file>, with no x:Class and no WPF-derived type in the payload. RawXamlTierContractTests checks every payload view. FLOW NewSessionWorkflow shows a prompt banner and calls WallTargetSelectionWorkflow.PickTarget. It asks for a linked wall (LinkedWallSelectionFilter), then, after Esc, for a host foundation wall (FoundationWallSelectionFilter). ContextualEditHook reads the selected system IDs instead, through ContextualEditTargetEvaluator. SgtWindowSession.Start begins the group and purges. WindowSessionBuilder composes the window, view model and SessionAnalysisOwner. PlanBuilder.BuildNewPlanAsync sets the framing mode, then runs FamilyCalibrationStep, WallAnalysisStep, ProfileWarmStep, PlanSeedingStep and admission. For an edit, StartupAnalysisWorkflow rebuilds the plan with PlanBaselineMapper and ChangeReviewPlanBuilder, and AnalyzeEditPlanAsync analyzes a copy of it against the wall. A stored system that does not load falls back to a wall pick (FallBackToPick). Grid edits reach PlanStore through PlanSynchronizationCoordinator. Preview edits go through PreviewEditingWorkflow, which records the window's Undo steps. PreviewRefreshCoordinator refreshes in UIEdit, PlanMutation or RenderOnly mode. After an edit startup, ChangeReviewWorkflow opens Change Review when ChangeReviewEvaluator reports NeedsAttention. Confirm analyzes the reviewed plan and saves only the decision ledger (SaveLedgerAsync). Place and Update synchronize and normalize the plan, run the preflight, then call PlacementWorkflow, PlacementExecutor and WallSystemWriter. The writer places members, tags them and calls ISystemRepository.Save in one transaction. A successful write closes the window with a commit; a failed or canceled write closes it with a rollback. A refused preflight keeps the window open. FinalizeSession releases the preview and window, then assimilates or rolls back the group. The UI state saves in the background. DATA Item Value System storage One DataStorage per system, named DBTools_SGT_System_<SystemId> (GUID without hyphens), schema DBTools_SGT_SystemV2 (a schema name, not the format version). Its DataJson holds a SystemData envelope: Placed, the decision ledger and the settings. Member tag Schema DBTools_SGT with Tag (SGT), SystemId, MemberRole (girt, head, sill, jamb_left, jamb_right) and ConfigJson. Framing mode WallFramingMode.Standard for a linked wall, with the wall bottom as base. Foundation for a host foundation wall, with the wall top as base and a 20'-0" band. The JSON field is placementMode. Rules MemberRules: AutoSeedSpacing 5'-0", MinimumLength 6". UI state %APPDATA%\DBTools\Cache\SGT\ui-state.json: panel expansion, opening column widths and Bulk Edit fields. It never gates the model commit. Revit element IDs are long in the plan, storage and placement records. DIAGNOSTICS SGT log messages use prefixes such as [SGT], [SGT.Preflight] and [SGT.Place.Cutback]. A plan rejection is a SpecFailure with the text [SpecFail/<area>/<rule>] <detail> (SpecFailureCodes). A UI error shows <action>: [SGT.UI.<area>.<name>] <detail> (UserErrorCodes). DiagnosticsPreflightLogger records analysis outcomes. TESTS ./test.sh test --tool SGT # pure: portable and Windows projects ./test.sh test --tool SGT --scope local -y 2026 # -y 2027 for Revit 2027 Project Covers DBTools.SGT.Portable.Pure.Tests Domain, feature decisions and storage mapping, on net10.0 DBTools.SGT.Pure.Tests Window lifecycle, view models, flyouts, UI state and synchronization DBTools.SGT.Local.Tests Wall analysis, opening detection, model writes, storage, preview parity and the real window session The Local tests open SGT/sgt_test_model.rvt (Model paths). Without the model, they fail. SEE ALSO Hooks, Sandbox Integration, Revit Execution

developer-guide/troubleshooting.html.title: Troubleshooting | DB Tools
developer-guide/troubleshooting.html.summary: Troubleshooting This page lists common build, runtime and tool errors, and how to read the DB Tools logs. For a reported failure, read the logs in %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\ first. Build Choosing a build command Build one project or test project with plain MSBuild: dotnet build path/to/project.csproj -c Release This computes content versions, restores only the selected year and stages the project's runtime inputs. It does not validate or publish a distribution. ./build.sh BuildAll builds, validates and publishes the complete distribution for every supported year, including the Dev Mode preflight and manifest checks. BuildAll compiles no tests; use ./build.sh BuildTests or a selected-test target. See Build Pipeline. Python 3.10 or later is required Python 3.10 or later is required. Install it with: sudo apt-get install python3 On Linux and WSL, build/DotNet/sdk.sh uses Python to verify and install the pinned SDK when the private SDK root is incomplete; test.sh also uses it for test discovery. Install Python and rerun the command: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y python3 bash build/DotNet/sdk.sh On Windows, build.ps1 installs and verifies the SDK without Python. DbToolsDaemon.Protocol package missing or mismatched BuildAll requires the DbToolsDaemon.Protocol package version pinned in build/Distribution/protocol-package-lock.json, with the SHA-256 recorded there. The Validation Runner loads the package after the build tasks verify it. If the package is missing or its bytes differ from the lock, obtain the pinned package and update the lock. sourceKind is github-release for a published release, or local-candidate for an approved local candidate with its candidate-<version> tag, daemon commit, and copies of the bundle README and SHA256SUMS. Do not point the build at a daemon checkout or bypass the check. BuildAll does not need the daemon CLI or an installed Revit. The DIST suite and Revit-hosted tests use the daemon CLI. Dev Mode preflight fails ValidateDistributionCandidate runs the Dev Mode policy on each year and prints: Revit <year> Dev Mode preflight: <n> failures, <m> warnings; outcome=<x> Both years must pass. Every collectible-boundary warning (CollectibleThreadStatic, CollectibleAssemblyLoadContextType) counts as a failure. A failed policy, boundary, graph, identity or candidate-byte check needs a source fix and a new build. HandyControl output missing A missing vendor import, resource or DBTools.HandyControl output means the vendor/HandyControl submodule is not initialized. build.sh and build.ps1 initialize it automatically, which requires a Git checkout and network access: git submodule update --init --recursive vendor/HandyControl ./build.sh BuildAll The output is .artifacts/vendor/<Configuration>/handycontrol/net10.0-windows/DBTools.HandyControl.dll. Unsupported Revit year The supported desktop years are Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027; the distribution and reference metadata use the year keys 2026 and 2027. A build or candidate for any other year is rejected; there is no fallback framework. Revit backup files in test models Revit writes backup copies (*.0001.rvt, *.00001.rvt) when it saves a model. Under testing/RevitTestModels/ these files are ignored by Git. The build does not delete them; remove them by hand when you no longer need them. Runtime Tool assembly fails to load InvalidOperationException: Failed to load tool assembly 'DBTools.GM' from the declared Tools path '<path>' in ALC rooted at 'DBTools'. Related errors from ToolAssemblyResolver: Tool assembly '<name>' was not found at the declared Tools path '<path>'. Tool assembly path '<path>' declares simple name '<x>', expected '<name>'. Tool assembly '<name>' is already loaded from '<path>', but the declared Tools path is '<path>'. App loads each tool from Tools/<name>.dll beside DBTools.dll. Check that the year directory has the complete product tree (see Assembly Loading Contract) and that the manifest's assembly name matches the file. Rebuild with ./build.sh BuildAll. "Assembly already loaded" during Dev Mode reload Revit shows a popup about an assembly that is already loaded during or after BuildAll, while the dbtools-daemon Dev Mode driver watches the distribution. Causes: The driver watches the multi-year root .artifacts/dist/Release instead of one year directory. A reload starts while promotion replaces the files. DB Tools code loaded or resolved a DBTools.* assembly or type outside the driver's collectible AssemblyLoadContext (for example through an AppDomain-wide scan or Assembly.Load), so the context cannot unload. Point the driver directly at one year directory, .artifacts/dist/Release/2026 or .artifacts/dist/Release/2027, never at a copy, and publish with ./build.sh BuildAll. Promotion keeps each unchanged file as the same file (a hard link), so Windows Defender does not scan it again. A copied directory is a set of new files that Defender scans again, which can add tens of seconds to each Dev Mode inspection. Theme validation Startup validates the theme with ThemeValidator.ValidateOrThrow; a failure stops startup. In a Revit-hosted test run, read the daemon job's startup failure output instead of waiting for a dialog. Theme dictionary merge failed InvalidOperationException: Theme dictionary merge failed at '/DBTools.Presentation;V<PresentationVersion>;component/Resources/Brushes.xaml'. A resource dictionary did not load: a missing assembly reference, a broken StaticResource chain or invalid XAML. Rebuild with ./build.sh BuildAll and check that the year directory contains DBTools.Presentation.dll and DBTools.HandyControl.dll from the same build. Theme resource freeze failed InvalidOperationException: Theme resource freeze failed for key '<key>' in '<source>'. A Freezable resource (brush, geometry) cannot be frozen, usually because it has a binding or a dynamic reference. Make its values static. Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch InvalidOperationException: Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch: expected 9 dictionaries but found 8 in '<root>'. InvalidOperationException: Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch at index <i>: expected '<uri>' but found '<uri>'. Resources/Theme.xaml must merge these dictionaries in this order: HandyControl Themes/SkinDark.xaml, HandyControl Themes/Theme.xaml, then Tokens.xaml, Brushes.xaml, Converters.xaml, Controls.xaml, DataGrid.xaml, Menus.xaml and Components.xaml. See Theme System. Revit API context errors ContextUnavailableException: No UIApplication in current gate scope. InvalidOperationException: ActiveUIDocument is null. Code used the Revit API outside a valid API context, for example from a modeless window without the call gate, after the document closed, or during shutdown. Run Revit API work through IRevitCallGate.RunAsync, check that a document is open, and handle cancellation when a document closes. WPF Dispatcher errors InvalidOperationException: No WPF Dispatcher is available (Application.Current is null and no Revit window dispatcher could be resolved). InvalidOperationException: WPF Dispatcher is shutting down. UI work ran during early startup or late shutdown, when no dispatcher is available. Check for a dispatcher and for Dispatcher.HasShutdownStarted before UI work, and use BeginInvoke where the caller need not wait. Unhandled UI exception from a window command A WPF command that calls ISafeExecutor.RunAsync and lets the exception propagate into an AsyncRelayCommand raises a Dispatcher unhandled exception, which the Dev Mode driver host can also show. In window commands, use ISafeExecutor.RunWithoutThrowingAsync: it logs and notifies but does not rethrow. Use RunAsync where the caller must receive the exception. XamlParseException on a read-only binding System.Windows.Markup.XamlParseException: A TwoWay or OneWayToSource binding cannot work on the read-only property '<name>' ... Run.Text binds TwoWay by default. Binding it to a get-only property fails when the window loads. Set Mode=OneWay (or OneTime for an immutable value), or bind a TextBlock.Text instead. Contextual ribbon layout changes A contextual ribbon injector that modifies Revit's contextual tabs eagerly (for example the Multi-Select tab) or inserts at index 0 shifts the native buttons. Inject only when the selection contains matching elements, append panels and buttons with Add, and remove them when the selection no longer matches. Core's ContextualRibbonInjector follows these rules. Other startup and manifest errors Message Cause AppRuntime not initialized. Code ran before App startup completed or after shutdown Manifest '<id>' is missing required 'panel' field. (and other missing required messages) Invalid manifest.yml Tool module type '<type>' not found in assembly '<assembly>'. The manifest module type or assembly name is wrong Tools Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) TransferException carries a TransferErrorCode: Code Meaning Action DestinationTypeMissing The destination has no matching drafting view type Create the view type in the destination SourceTypeNameUnavailable The source view type name cannot be read Check that the source is a valid drafting view CreateViewFailed The destination view could not be created Check write access and view limits CopyElementsFailed The view elements could not be copied Check the elements and the target view OverridesFailed The view overrides could not be copied Some overrides cannot be transferred View Template Comparer (VTC): raw XAML resource not found System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Embedded tool XAML resource 'DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml' was not found. The VTC alert body templates are an EmbeddedResource with the logical name DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml, read with ToolWindowXaml.ReadEmbeddedResource. Check the item and its LogicalName in DBTools.VTC.csproj. The shared VTC dictionaries are in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/VTC. Logs Log files Logs are written to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\. File names use Eastern time: dbtools-<RevitYear>-<InstanceId>-<Timestamp>-<Nonce>.log dbtools-<RevitYear>-<InstanceId>-<Timestamp>-<Nonce>-manual-<ManualTimestamp>.log The second form is written after Start New Log File in the logger window. The first line of each file names the Revit year, the instance id and the Revit process id, so a log can be matched to its Revit process. Example: dbtools-2026-ABC123-20260124-143022345-a1b2c3d4.log. Startup cleans up old files: at most 50 files across all instances, at most 14 days old, and at most 100 MB in total while more than one file remains (the newest file is kept even if it alone is larger). Failures that occur before logging starts are written to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\DBTools.Fallback.log. Debug mode Debug mode lowers the minimum log level from Information to Debug, shows the logger window and flushes the log buffer every 120 ms instead of 600 ms. It is off at every startup and is not saved. It turns on when: you enable it in the Settings window or open the logger window; an Error-level entry is logged and the logger window can be shown. An error logged before the Revit main window exists opens the window once deferred startup can show it. Closing the logger window turns debug mode off. Logger window The title is DB Tools Log - Revit <Year> [<InstanceId>]. The window is a modeless utility window. The logger host applies pin mode changes centrally: a change that keeps the owner mode only updates Topmost, and a change of owner mode closes and recreates the window. Code must not change the owner of the live window directly. The window provides: the columns Source, Time, Level, Message and Duration. Source is narrow and shows the first namespace segment after DBTools and the type name, for example JoistGirderWeight · AutoUpdateTask. A name that does not fit is still and shortened in the middle, keeping the start of the tool and the end of the type name (Joist…AutoUpdateTask). While the pointer is over the row, or the row is selected, the full name scrolls as a ticker: it holds at its start, scrolls left and repeats after a gap. It returns to its start when the pointer leaves or the selection moves. With Windows animation effects off, names never scroll. Rows have no tooltips; message text without its markers: a leading [Tag] shows as a chip, and the execution phase, the elapsed time and the correlation ID leave the text. Duration shows the elapsed time of a timed entry, for example 460 ms, 5.6 s or 1 min 45 s; a details pane (the toolbar info button, a double-click on an entry, or Show Details in the context menu). Opening it scrolls the selected entry into view. It shows every value of the selected entry: time with milliseconds, level, full source, message, tag, phase, duration, correlation ID, the logged text and the exception. Copy details copies these values; the start row of a finished operation is hidden: its finish row shows the duration. A start row stays until its operation finishes, and a search shows every matching start row. Show Start Rows in the context menu shows every start row; level filters for INFO, WARN, ERROR and DEBUG, and a text search that matches the logged text and the displayed text; Copy All and Export, which save every retained entry in arrival order regardless of the filters, with the logged text unchanged. Export writes DBToolsLog_<yyyyMMdd_hhmmss><AM|PM>.txt; auto-scroll, which follows new entries. Scrolling up pauses it until you scroll back to the bottom or until a new entry arrives after 15 s idle; turning it off keeps it off; Start New Log File (in the danger menu), which starts a new file, clears the window and logs a confirmation with the same instance ID. If closing the previous file fails, the new file stays active and a warning is logged. Correlation IDs and execution phases ISafeExecutor gives every operation a GUID correlation ID and logs its phases: ["Start"] "GM Apply" starting (CorrelationId=...) ["Complete"] "GM Apply" completed in 1234ms (CorrelationId=...) The log file and exports keep this text. The logger window shows GM Apply completed with 1.2 s in Duration, and keeps the phase and correlation ID in the details pane. Phase Level Meaning Start Information The operation started Complete Information The operation finished Cancel Warning The operation was canceled Error Error The operation failed Search for the correlation ID to find every entry of one operation and its duration. Reporting a problem Include: the log file from %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\, or a logger window export; the Revit version (year and build number); the DB Tools version; the correlation ID of the failed operation; the steps to reproduce; a screenshot of any error dialog.

index.html.title: DB Tools documentation | DB Tools
index.html.summary: DB Tools documentation DB Tools is a set of tools for Autodesk Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027, mainly for structural engineering workflows. It runs on 64-bit Windows 10 or 11 and installs for the current user. Sections Section Audience Contents User guide Revit users Installation, getting started and one page per tool. Developer guide Contributors Architecture, creating a new tool and troubleshooting. API reference Contributors Reference generated from the XML documentation comments. Tools Tool Purpose Global Mapper Bulk replacement of families, types, styles and materials; duplicate detection; shared parameters. Super Girt Tool Girt, header, sill and jamb placement on walls. Combined Foundation Tags Data and positions for combined pier and footing tags. Transfer Drafting Views Copy of drafting views between a project and a library. View Template Comparer Comparison and merge of view templates. The user guide lists all tools. Requirements Item Requirement Revit Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) or Revit 2027, desktop Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit Account Standard user. The installer needs no administrator rights. Architecture DBTools.dll is the Revit entry point. It loads DBTools.Core (shared infrastructure and the tool registry), DBTools.Presentation (WPF resources and controls) and one assembly per tool from the Tools folder. The architecture overview describes the layers. Source: https://github.com/kirsch33/dbtools. Report problems on the issue tracker.

user-guide/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | DB Tools
user-guide/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started NAME getting started - the DB Tools ribbon, settings, banners and logs SYNOPSIS DB Tools > Settings DESCRIPTION This page describes the parts that all tools share. RIBBON The tab has four panels: DB Tools Common, DB Tools Structural, DB Tools Testing and DB Tools Settings. This guide names a panel by its last word, such as DB Tools > Structural. The user guide lists the tools on each panel. A tool button needs an open model. Only Settings works without one. A tool raises a settings warning when its settings are not valid, or when the model lacks something that the tool needs. Then the Settings button shows a warning icon, the DB Tools tab is highlighted, and the buttons that need the missing item are disabled. Open Settings to read and fix the warning. SETTINGS Click Settings to open DB Tools - Settings. DB Tools saves settings for each Windows user and each Revit year. Settings that you make in Revit 2026 do not apply in Revit 2027. Option in General Default Effect Enable Common Tools On Shows the DB Tools Common panel. Enable Structural Tools On Shows the DB Tools Structural panel. Enable Testing Tools On Shows the DB Tools Testing panel. Enable Services On Changes nothing. To stop Dialog Suppression, clear Enable Dialog Suppression in its pack. Enable Debug Mode Off Opens the log window and adds Debug entries to the log. It applies at once and lasts until Revit closes. A cleared panel option hides the panel only. The auto-update options of its tools still run. Common Settings, Structural Settings, Testing Settings and Services Settings hold the settings packs of the tools. Some packs have an auto-update option, such as Auto Update Joist Girder Weights. It runs the tool each time you open or switch to a view. Button Effect Validate Checks the unsaved settings and shows the warnings. It saves nothing. Save Settings Saves all changes and closes the window. Text at the bottom of the window tells when the changes apply. Reset All > Reset All Settings Resets every setting at once, after you confirm. Reset on a pack Resets that pack at once, after you confirm. If you close the window without Save Settings, DB Tools discards your changes without a prompt. BANNERS A tool shows its result in a banner at the top of its window or of the Revit window. Most banners close by themselves after 3 to 10 seconds, and an error stays longest. While the pointer is over the banners, no banner closes. A long message has a Details button, which opens the log window with the full text. With more than three banners, the last row shows +<n> more. Click it to show all banners. LOGS DB Tools writes one log file for each Revit session to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\, named dbtools-<year>-*.log. A failure from before the log starts goes to DBTools.Fallback.log in the same folder. For a problem report, send the newest log. When DB Tools logs an error, the log window opens and Debug Mode stays on until you clear it or Revit closes. In the log window, double-click an entry to see its details. Click Copy details to copy them, or Export to save all entries to a file. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do Could not load settings. The settings file may be corrupt or inaccessible. Reset Settings keeps a copy of the settings file in %APPDATA%\DBTools\ and resets the settings. The banner names the copy. Abort Addin Load closes only the settings window. Close closes only the message. SEE ALSO User guide, Installation

user-guide/index.html.title: User guide | DB Tools
user-guide/index.html.summary: User guide NAME user guide - install DB Tools and use its tools in Revit SYNOPSIS Installation, Getting started DESCRIPTION DB Tools is an add-in for Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027. The tables list its tools by ribbon panel. TOOLS Common Page Use Global Mapper Replace content in bulk, find duplicates and add shared parameters. Transfer Drafting Views Copy drafting views to a library with Export To Library, and back with Import From Library. Elevation Tags Align spot elevation tags with Align Elevation Tags, and set their symbol text with Set Elevation Symbol Text. Structural Page Use Super Girt Tool Place girts and opening framing on a wall. Combined Foundation Tags Update combined foundation tags with Update Combined Foundation Tags, and move them with Move Combined Tags. Organize Foundation Types Organize foundation types for tagging. Analytical Snap To Level Move the ends of analytical members to a level. Allow Join and Disallow Join Allow or disallow joins at both ends of framing. Update Joist Girder Weights Estimate the weight of each joist girder. Testing The Testing tools are experimental. Page Use View Template Comparer Compare and merge view template settings. Record Set Package Revit models with their linked files. Extreme Roof Framing Tool Fit columns and beams to floor and roof slopes with Extreme Roof Framing. Services Dialog Suppression has no button. It suppresses each Revit dialog whose text matches a pattern in Settings > Services Settings. SEE ALSO Developer guide

user-guide/installation.html.title: Installation | DB Tools
user-guide/installation.html.summary: Installation NAME installation - install, update and remove DB Tools SYNOPSIS DBTools-Setup-<version>.exe DBTools-Setup-<version>.exe /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES DESCRIPTION DB Tools runs in desktop Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027, on 64-bit Windows 10 or later. Setup installs it for one Windows user and needs no administrator rights. Download DBTools-Setup-<version>.exe from the releases page. INSTALLING Close Revit. Run Setup as the Windows user who uses Revit. Setup installs into the %APPDATA% folder of that user only. On Revit versions, select the Revit years. Setup selects each compatible Revit on this computer. It disables each other year: Revit 2026 - update to 2026.5 or later: update Revit, then run Setup again. Revit <year> - not detected: that Revit year is not installed. Go to the next page. If DB Tools is installed, Setup asks An existing DBTools.bundle was found. Replace it with this version? Click Yes. On Ready to install, check Product, Revit and Location. Click Install. The last page shows DB Tools is installed. Open install folder opens %APPDATA%\DBTools. Start Revit. If the DB Tools tab does not show, read the logs. UPDATING To update, run Setup of the version that you want. Setup replaces the whole bundle folder, so it deletes files that you added there. It keeps your settings and logs. DB Tools does not check for updates. UNINSTALLING Close Revit. In Windows Settings > Apps, find DB Tools and click Uninstall. The uninstaller deletes the bundle folder, and keeps your settings and logs in %APPDATA%\DBTools\. SILENT INSTALLATION Setup accepts the standard Inno Setup switches, such as /VERYSILENT and /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES. A silent install selects every compatible Revit year and replaces an installed version without a prompt. Run it in the Windows session of the Revit user. Setup writes a log during installation. Exit code Meaning 0 DB Tools is installed. 10 Setup could not activate the copied files. Another code Setup did not install, for example because Revit is running or no compatible Revit is installed. The Setup log gives the reason. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do Close Revit and run Setup again to install DB Tools. Revit runs in your Windows session. Close it. Select at least one installed Revit version. For Revit 2026, install update 2026.5 or later. No Revit year is selected. DB Tools could not be installed The last Setup page gives the reason and the path of the Setup log. It also tells whether your previous version is still installed. Close each program that uses a file in the DB Tools folders, and run Setup again. A DB Tools dialog when Revit starts, such as DB Tools theme failed to load: DB Tools could not start. Run Setup again. If the dialog shows again, send the log. FILES Path Contents %APPDATA%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins\DBTools.bundle\ The add-in. Revit loads it at start. Contents\DBTools\<version>\<year>\ holds the files for one Revit year. %APPDATA%\DBTools\ The uninstaller, your settings, the logs in Logs\ and the tool caches in Cache\ SEE ALSO Getting started, User guide

user-guide/tools/analytical-snap.html.title: Analytical Snap To Level | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/analytical-snap.html.summary: Analytical Snap To Level NAME Analytical Snap To Level - move the ends of analytical members to a level SYNOPSIS DB Tools > Structural > Analytical Snap To Level DESCRIPTION The tool moves the end points of the selected analytical members to the elevation of one level. It changes only the curve of each analytical member. The plan position (X and Y) of the end points does not change. Select the analytical members. The button is enabled when any element is selected. Click Analytical Snap To Level. In Select Target Level, select a level. Each level shows as <name> (Elev: <elevation>), with the elevation in feet. The lowest level is first. Read the Snap to Level Complete window, and click OK. REQUIREMENTS The tool skips a selected element that fails a rule, and reports the reason. Item Rule Skip reason Element An analytical member, not the physical beam or column not an analytical member Structural role Beam or Column, not another role such as Girder role not supported Curve A straight line. A curved member keeps its shape. not straight Length After the snap, the member is not shorter than Revit allows. An almost vertical beam fails this rule. would collapse The role sets which end points move: Role What moves Beam Both end points. The member becomes horizontal. Column Only the end point nearer the level. If both are equally near, the start point moves. RESULTS The completion window counts the processed and skipped elements. It shows one line for each skip reason: <reason>: <count> (element IDs <id>, <id>, and <n> more) It lists up to 10 IDs for each reason, and adds and <n> more for the rest. For not an analytical member, it shows only the count. The processed count includes members that were at the level already. Each run is one Undo step: DB Tools - Snap Analytical Elements to Level. An error undoes the whole run. A skip does not. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do No target level selected. You closed the level window without a level, or the model has no levels. Nothing changes. LIMITS All selected members snap to the one level that you select. To use more levels, run the tool once for each level. To snap to an elevation without a level, add a level there. A sloped beam loses its slope. SEE ALSO Allow Join and Disallow Join, Getting started, DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel

user-guide/tools/elevation-tags.html.title: Elevation Tags | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/elevation-tags.html.summary: Elevation Tags NAME Elevation Tags - align spot elevation text with its leader, and set symbol text SYNOPSIS DB Tools > Common > Align Elevation Tags DB Tools > Common > Set Elevation Symbol Text DESCRIPTION Align Elevation Tags moves the text of each matching spot elevation in the active view beside its leader end, at the same gap for short and long text. It works in floor, structural and ceiling plans. A spot elevation is aligned when all of these are true: A pattern in Tag Name Patterns (Regex) matches one of these names: the spot type, its family, the symbol type or the symbol family. It has a leader. The elevation base of its type is not Relative. Text Location Position of the text Above Leader, Below Leader Over the shoulder, on the side of the leader toward the point that the spot measures. A level leader puts the text below the leader. In-line with Leader Centered on the leader line, past the leader end. Align gives Above Leader and Below Leader the same position. This keeps the text off the symbol text of the DB Elevation Tag symbols. Set Elevation Symbol Text gives the selected spot elevations a symbol with other text. Enter the text, such as T.O. FTG., at Symbol text: and click Apply. The command copies the symbol family and the spot type, names each copy <original name> - <text>, and moves only the selected spots to the copy. The symbol type keeps its name. The same text again uses the same copies. The text must be on one line, without \ / : * ? " < > | { } [ ] ; ` ~. REQUIREMENTS Item Rule Symbol family For Set Elevation Symbol Text: an editable spot elevation symbol family with exactly one text element. SETTINGS Open DB Tools > Settings, expand Common Settings and find Elevation Tags. Auto Update Elevation Tags runs Align, without a banner, each time you open or switch to a supported plan view. It is on by default. Tag Name Patterns (Regex) holds up to 3 .NET regular expressions. They are not case-sensitive. The default is: ^DB Elevation Tag - (?:Concrete|Steel|Wall) Label$ Alignment Offsets edit the type that Live Preview shows, in paper inches. The arrow buttons choose the type. A positive Along Leader moves the text along the shoulder, away from the leader end. A positive Perpendicular moves it away from the leader line, or up for In-line with Leader. The next Align run uses the saved values. Live Preview draws the type with a downward and an upward leader. A dashed outline shows the text without offsets. RESULTS Align ends with a banner, such as Aligned 12 elevation tag(s). A tag that is already in place does not count. Each run that moves tags, also an automatic run, is one Undo step: DB Tools - Align spot elevations. Set Elevation Symbol Text is one Undo step: DB Tools - Set elevation symbol text. It deletes a copy that it made when the change leaves the copy unused. A failure changes nothing. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do No spot elevation tags matched Tag Name Patterns. Check Elevation Tags settings. Compare the patterns with the type and symbol names. No matching elevation tags needed changes. Spot elevations without a leader are skipped. Each matching spot is in place, has no leader, or uses the Relative base. Symbol family '<name>' contains <n> plain text elements. Exactly one is required. Edit the symbol family so that it has one text element. Elevation Tags Disabled (a settings warning) Auto-update could not start, so Align and auto-update are off. Click Clear on the warning in Settings. LIMITS Align does not change spots in linked models. The placement suits a symbol that draws its text above its origin, as the DB Elevation Tag symbols do. With another symbol, the elevation text can cover the symbol text. The offsets are stored by spot type name, for every project. A renamed type or a copy from Set Elevation Symbol Text has no saved offsets unless its new name already has an entry. A pattern that ends in $ can miss the copies, whose names end in - <text>. Align still finds a copy whose symbol type name matches. Live Preview lists only the types whose type name matches a pattern, case-sensitive. To set offsets for another type, add a pattern for its type name. EXAMPLES To also align the spot types whose names start with Acme Spot, click + Add Pattern, enter this pattern and click Save Settings: ^Acme Spot SEE ALSO Getting started, DBTools.ElevationTags

user-guide/tools/erft.html.title: Extreme Roof Framing Tool | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/erft.html.summary: Extreme Roof Framing Tool NAME Extreme Roof Framing Tool - set column and beam offsets to the underside of a floor or roof SYNOPSIS DB Tools > DB Tools Testing > Extreme Roof Framing To edit an adjustment, select its members, then click Edit ERFT on the contextual Modify tab. DESCRIPTION ERFT raises or lowers column tops and the ends of beam location lines. It moves them to the bottom surface of a target floor or roof. It changes the Top Offset of each column and the Start Level Offset and End Level Offset of each beam. It changes no levels. ERFT saves each adjustment in the model for Edit ERFT. Click Extreme Roof Framing. Select a floor or roof target. Select the columns and beams, then click Finish. Check the Columns and Beams tables, then click Apply. The bottom surface uses faces whose normals point mostly down. Member end Moves to the height of Column top The nearest point of the bottom surface. Beam end within 1/2 in. of a selected column top The adjusted top of that column. Beam end within 1/2 in. of another selected beam That beam's adjusted location line, at the same plan position. Other beam end The nearest point of the bottom surface. ERFT rounds each change to a multiple of the Tolerance: value and adds it to the current offset. OPTIONS Control Effect Pick Selects another target and calculates again. Tolerance: 1/16", 1/8", 1/4" (default), 1/2", 1" or Custom. A custom value is in inches and at least 0.01. Use a decimal point. Nearest, Up, Down The rounding direction. At 1/4", a change of -0.1 in. becomes 0 with Up and -0.25 in. with Down. Status Pending (will change), No Change (the rounded change is 0) or Error. Apply On when the tolerance is valid, a row is Pending and no row has Error. REQUIREMENTS Item Rule Column A structural column in the host model, placed at a point. Beam Straight structural framing in the host model, not a brace. Material ERFT leaves out a member whose structural material name has the word concrete, in any capitalization. Selection At least one column, or a beam with an end within 1/2 in. of a column top in the model. Target A floor or roof. RESULTS Apply is one Undo step: ERFT Apply Adjustments. It writes the offsets and marks each changed member. If one write fails, it changes nothing and shows Apply failed: with the reason. After a success, the window closes. Edit ERFT restores the target, tolerance and rounding of the adjustment. It reads the current offsets and calculates again. If the selection holds more than one adjustment, select one in Select ERFT System. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do 3D Preview is unavailable: … The preview is off for this window. Apply still works. Update the graphics driver and open ERFT again. LIMITS ERFT uses the nearest point in 3D, not the point straight above. Under a slope, a gap closes only in part. For a 12 in. gap under a 4:12 slope, the change is about 10.8 in. Each Apply from Edit ERFT closes most of the rest. Only selected members are supports. A beam end at a column that is not selected goes to the target surface. With only beams selected, ERFT checks for a column in the model, but no beam end follows it. ERFT rounds the change, not the resulting offset. Edit ERFT includes only the members that changed at the last Apply. It does not show for a member that no Apply changed. SEE ALSO Getting started, DBTools.ERFT

user-guide/tools/foundation-tags.html.title: Combined Foundation Tags | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/foundation-tags.html.summary: Combined Foundation Tags Combined Foundation Tags prepares and positions the combined pier and footing tags (family DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag). It has two commands: Update Combined Foundation Tags computes the data that the combined tag displays and writes it to shared parameters on piers and footings. Move Combined Tags moves combined tags to a corner of the footing they tag. The tool does not place tags. Place the tags with Revit's tag commands. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > the foundation tags split button. The split button also contains Organize Foundation Types. Command Effect Update Combined Foundation Tags Writes Foundation Pier Top on piers, and Associated Pier and Associated Pier Elevation on footings, in the active view. Move Combined Tags Moves each matching tag in the active view to the corner of its footing that the tag's name specifies. Both commands are enabled when a view is active and process the active view only. Both are disabled while the shared-parameter prerequisites are not met (see Prerequisites). Prerequisites The update command needs three project parameters, bound as instance parameters and identified by GUID: Parameter Type Category Group Associated Pier Text Structural Foundations Identity Data Associated Pier Elevation Length Structural Foundations Identity Data Foundation Pier Top Length Structural Columns Constraints The GUIDs are the ones in the DB shared parameter file (group DB Structural), so a project that already has these parameters from that file needs no repair. A project that has a parameter with one of these names and another GUID, such as a project set up with DB Tools releases before November 2026, reports GUID_MISMATCH until you run Install/Repair. DB Tools checks the parameters when the active model changes. If a parameter is missing, has another GUID, has the wrong data type, is bound as a type parameter, or is bound to the wrong category, or a loaded family defines one of these names with another GUID, DB Tools activates the warning Combined Foundation Tags Disabled. The warning disables Update Combined Foundation Tags, Move Combined Tags and Organize Foundation Types, and the Settings button shows the warning icon. This check shows no banner. Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags also check the parameters each time they run, for example when you run one before the check on a model change has finished. In a family document they refuse to run. When a parameter fails, the command does not run. It activates the warning and shows one message, Required shared parameters need repair, that lists each failing parameter with its status and problem: Repair runs Install/Repair, as in Settings, including the prompt about schedule fields and view filters (see Schedule fields and view filters). After a successful repair, a banner confirms it and lists what changed; run the command again. Cancel changes nothing, and the warning stays. To repair the parameters in Settings: Open DB Tools > Settings and expand Structural Settings. The Combined Foundation Tags pack lists each required parameter of the active project: its name and status, then its data type, category and group. A parameter that is not OK also shows its problem. All text wraps to the window width. Click Install/Repair under the list, or Install/Repair on the Combined Foundation Tags Disabled warning card. The pack reads the active document when it opens. Without an open project, it shows No project open in place of the list; when a family is the active document, it shows A family is active. Install/Repair is then unavailable. The Settings window blocks Revit while it is open: close it, open or switch to the project, and open Settings again. Install/Repair needs an active project. It loads the definitions from the embedded shared parameter file, binds them to the required categories as instance parameters, and clears the warning. It keeps any other categories bound to these parameters and their values, and whether values can vary between group instances. If a parameter that already has the required GUID is bound as a type parameter (WRONG_BINDING_TYPE), Install/Repair changes it to an instance parameter and copies the value of each type to every instance of that type. If it is not bound to its required category (WRONG_CATEGORY), Install/Repair adds the category and keeps every value, including different values in instances of one group. For a parameter with another GUID (GUID_MISMATCH), Install/Repair replaces the parameter with the company definition and keeps: every category the old parameter was bound to, plus the required category, as instance categories; the old parameter group, and whether values can vary between group instances; every value: an element value stays on the same element, and the value of a type parameter is copied to every instance of that type. The company definition replaces the old parameter's visibility, description, user-modifiable and hide-when-no-value settings. The status message and the banner name each replaced parameter, the values kept, and each setting that changed. Install/Repair changes nothing and keeps the warning when it cannot keep every value: the old parameter has another data type, for example Area where Length is required; the parameter with the required GUID has another data type (WRONG_DATA_TYPE); Install/Repair cannot change the data type of a shared parameter, so delete that parameter in Manage > Project Parameters, which deletes its values, and run Install/Repair again; a value cannot be written to its element, for example because Revit blocks the change; a rebar container overrides the old parameter; Associated Pier Elevation or Foundation Pier Top (Length) has values on members of a group that is placed more than once. Revit changes such a value only in group edit mode, and it does not let a Length parameter vary between group instances, so DB Tools cannot write it. Values of Associated Pier (Text) in such groups are kept; a type parameter has a value on a type that has no instances; a parameter with the required name and another GUID holds values next to the parameter that has the required GUID (DUPLICATE_NAME); more than one parameter has the required name and none has the required GUID. The message names the parameter and the reason, and lists each value that could not be kept with its element ID. The DB Tools log lists every one. Correct the cause, for example delete the extra parameter in Manage > Project Parameters or purge the unused type, and run Install/Repair again. A duplicate of a parameter that already has the required GUID (DUPLICATE_NAME) is deleted only when no element or type has a value for it; the status message names each deleted duplicate. A global parameter with one of these names is not a project parameter; Install/Repair leaves it alone. These rules are tested with text and length values, extra categories, type parameters and grouped elements. Elements in design options and elements owned by another user in a workshared model are not tested; if Revit blocks a change there, Install/Repair changes nothing. Status values include MISSING, GUID_MISMATCH, FAMILY_GUID_MISMATCH, DUPLICATE_NAME, WRONG_DATA_TYPE, UNBOUND, WRONG_BINDING_TYPE and WRONG_CATEGORY. Families with another GUID A loaded family keeps its own copy of a shared parameter: a family parameter, or a label that shows the parameter. When a family uses one of these names with another GUID, its labels and formulas keep looking for that GUID. Revit also removes a deleted shared parameter from the labels of the families that use it, so a tag then shows nothing. Install/Repair therefore changes the families first and deletes the parameter with the other GUID only when no family uses it any more. When a project has a parameter with one of these names and another GUID, Install/Repair opens each family of the project to check it; in a project with many families this takes a while. For each family parameter with the name and another GUID, it: replaces the parameter in the family with the one from the DB shared parameter file, as an instance or type parameter as before, in the same group; keeps every formula, dimension label and label that uses the parameter, and every value of each family type; reloads the family into the project, then gives every element and type its value back and checks each one. When the company parameter is already bound, the status is FAMILY_GUID_MISMATCH and names the families whose types or elements show the parameter. A label that shows the parameter directly does not show in the status; Install/Repair finds it. Install/Repair changes the families in the project only. The family files in your library still use the other GUID; when you load such a file again, the problem comes back. Replace the parameter in the file too. Install/Repair changes nothing, keeps the warning, and names the family when: a label uses the parameter directly, as added through Edit Label > Add Parameter in a tag or title block family. DB Tools cannot change a label. In Revit 2027 the message has one line per label: its detail group, the position of the parameter in the label, and its prefix, suffix, sample text, spaces before, line break before and non-breaking spaces, so you can add the company parameter with the same settings. Revit 2026 cannot tell which label it is. Open the family, select the label (in a detail group, use Edit Group first), click Edit Label, replace the parameter with the one from the DB shared parameter file, and load the family into the project again; a nested family uses the parameter, or the family is a shared family nested in another family; the family defines the parameter as a type parameter in Structural Foundations or Structural Columns, where the project binds it as an instance parameter; the family defines it with another data type; an element has one value for the family parameter and another for the project parameter; the family is in-place or cannot be edited, and it defines the parameter, or DB Tools cannot tell whether it does. When its elements show the parameter and the project parameter could explain that, DB Tools checks, without a change, whether the elements still show it without the project parameter; a value cannot be written back after the reload, for example because a formula computes it or the element is in a group placed more than once. Invalid parameter bindings When an add-in undoes a change to Values can vary by group instance of an existing parameter, Revit can leave the parameter bindings of the model in an invalid state until the model is reopened. DB Tools does not leave this state, but it cannot read the parameters while it lasts. It then shows one message and changes nothing: Revit's parameter bindings for this model are in an invalid state; save, close and reopen the model, then try again. Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags show it as a warning banner and do not run. Settings shows it under Status not available in place of the parameter list, and Install/Repair shows it as its result. The check on a model change and the automatic update activate the warning Combined Foundation Tags Disabled. Save, close and reopen the model. DB Tools checks the parameters again when the reopened model becomes active. Schedule fields and view filters When Install/Repair deletes a parameter (a replaced parameter or an empty duplicate), Revit also removes every schedule field that uses it and, from any view filter that uses it, the rules that go with it. This includes a field in an embedded schedule and a combined parameter field that includes the parameter. Revit removes a combined parameter field whole. Install/Repair cannot keep these fields or add them again. You must add the company parameter to those schedules by hand. A change of binding (WRONG_BINDING_TYPE or WRONG_CATEGORY) keeps the schedule fields. Revit removes each rule set of an affected view filter that has a rule on the deleted parameter, with every rule in that set. The filter keeps its categories and its other rule sets, so it can select other elements than before. A filter with no rules left applies to all elements of its categories. Install/Repair cannot keep or restore the removed rules. Before you continue, record whether each filter uses AND or OR and whether any rule is inverted. The rule list does not show this logic. After the repair, add every listed rule to each filter by hand, including rules that use other parameters. The list shows only the rules that Revit removes. The parameter list shows a warning marker, for example "Used in 2 schedules" or "Used in 1 view filter", below each parameter that Install/Repair would delete while a schedule or view filter uses it. Below the marker, each line names a schedule and the field heading, or a view filter, rule parameter and rule. Install/Repair cannot see the formula of a calculated field, so a calculated field that uses the parameter is not listed; check calculated fields after the repair. When the repair would remove schedule fields or view filter rules, Install/Repair (the pack button, the warning card button, or Repair in a command's message) asks before Revit deletes them. The prompt lists each schedule, field and parameter, and each view filter, rule parameter, rule and deleted parameter. It tells you to record each filter's logic before you continue: Cancel changes nothing. The parameters, values, bindings, schedules and view filters stay as they are, and the warning stays. Continue runs the repair. The status message and banner list each schedule field and every rule from each affected view filter that Revit removed. If the project changed while the prompt was open and the list is now different, Install/Repair changes nothing and asks again with the new list. A value created by family migration may still fail a later preservation check; if it does, Install/Repair reports the refusal and rolls back the repair. After you continue, open each listed schedule and add the company parameter again, with its formatting, sorting, grouping, filters and conditional formatting. Open each listed view filter and add every listed rule with the parameter named for that rule. Use the AND/OR logic and inverted rules that you recorded before the repair. Update Combined Foundation Tags Usage Open a plan view that shows the piers and footings. Run Update Combined Foundation Tags. Read the banner. With Auto-Update Enabled on (the default), the update also runs each time you activate a floor plan or ceiling plan. Automatic runs show no result banner. What it does The command considers the family instances visible in the active view. A family instance is a pier when its family name matches a pier pattern. It is a footing when its family name matches a footing pattern (see Settings). For each pier, it computes Foundation Pier Top = the Top Offset parameter (0 if absent) plus the elevation of the level in the Top Level parameter, and writes it to the pier. For each footing, it finds the pier nearest in plan (X and Y of the location points) and within 2 ft. It writes the pier's Type Mark to Associated Pier and the pier's Foundation Pier Top to Associated Pier Elevation. A footing with no pier within 2 ft gets an empty Associated Pier. For a member of a group placed more than once, the updater compares each parameter before writing it. This includes nested groups whose enclosing group is placed more than once. Equal values need no write and do not count as skipped. A changed parameter is written if it varies between group instances, such as Associated Pier when that setting is enabled. A changed parameter that does not vary is skipped. Other parameters and elements still update in the same run. A group placed once still works. Revit changes non-varying values in repeated groups only in group edit mode. Length parameters cannot vary between group instances, and the Revit API cannot enter group edit mode. The updater keeps the parameter's existing variance setting. A footing can still use a skipped pier's Type Mark and computed top. If the pier's top cannot be computed, the footing uses its stored Foundation Pier Top, for grouped and ungrouped piers alike. A value is written only when it differs. Lengths are compared after rounding to two decimals. Revit cannot clear a length value. A footing with no pier in range keeps its previous Associated Pier Elevation and counts as skipped on every run until a pier is within 2 ft. Result The update, with its selection sets, is one undo entry. If a Revit write fails unexpectedly, the whole update is rolled back and the error is shown. A failure while creating the selection sets keeps the parameter writes and is reported. The banner reads Updated N element(s); M failed/skipped. or No elements modified. An element is counted as skipped when a pier lacks a valid Top Level, a footing or pier has no location point, a parameter is missing or read-only, or a length cannot be cleared. An element also counts as skipped when a changed parameter does not vary between instances of its repeated group. It enters the Skipped selection set and can also enter Modified if another parameter changes. The log records up to ten detailed failures, then reports the total. When this occurs, the banner adds: N skipped: in groups placed more than once (Revit allows these values only in group edit mode). Outcome Banner At least one element modified Stays open. Has Select Modified, and Select Skipped when some elements were skipped. Nothing modified, some skipped Warning that closes after 8 seconds. No buttons. Nothing modified or skipped Info that closes after 5 seconds. When every value is already current, the updater creates no selection sets and changes nothing. The manual result is an Info message, and automatic updates show no result banner. The buttons select the elements of the run that just finished. They work only while the model that ran the update is active. Each run also creates selection sets named DB Tools - FoundationTags - Modified Elements (<timestamp>) and DB Tools - FoundationTags - Skipped Elements (<timestamp>) when the respective list is not empty. The timestamp is in Eastern time. A second run in the same second adds a suffix such as (2). The model keeps the 5 most recently created sets with the prefix DB Tools - FoundationTags - . Skipping members of groups placed more than once does not stop later automatic updates. Automatic runs show no result banner. If an automatic update fails, DB Tools shows the error and stops automatic updates for that model until you close and reopen it. After Save As, or the first save of a new model, it tries once more. The commands remain available. Move Combined Tags Usage Open a plan view with combined tags. Run Move Combined Tags. What it does The command examines the independent tags in the active view. It moves a tag when: the tag tags a Structural Foundations element (in the model or in a linked model); the tag's family or type name matches a tag family pattern; and the tag's name is a corner name. The corner name is the name of the tag, or the name of its type when the tag has no name: Top Right, Top Left, Bottom Right or Bottom Left (case-insensitive). The command computes the footing's bounding rectangle from its geometry in the footing's own X and Y axes. It selects the corner by the view's orientation, so Top Right is the corner at the top right of the view even in a rotated view. It sets the tag head position to that corner. The Z value of the tag head is unchanged. Linked footings are transformed into the host model's coordinates. The tag's leader is not changed. Result The banner reads Moved N; skipped M of K candidate tags. A candidate is skipped when the corner name is not valid, the tagged element is not a family instance with a location point, or it has no geometry. When no candidate exists, the banner says why: Message Cause No tags were found in the active view. No independent tags in the view. No tags in the active view are currently tagging structural foundation elements. The view's tags tag other categories. No tags matched the configured Tag Family Patterns. Check Combined Foundation Tags settings. Sample rejected tag families/types: <list> Tags tag foundations, but no tag family pattern matches. The move is one undo entry. If an unexpected Revit geometry or write error occurs, the whole move is canceled and no tag stays moved. Settings Open DB Tools > Settings and select the Combined Foundation Tags pack. Setting Default Used by Auto-Update Enabled On Update (runs on floor plan and ceiling plan activation) Tag Family Patterns ^DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag(?: No Elevations)?$ Move Pier Family Patterns ^Foundation Pier(?: - Round)?$ Update Footing Family Patterns ^(?:Footing\|Pile Cap)-Rectangular$ Update Each pattern list holds up to 3 regular expressions. Matching is case-insensitive. An empty list uses the default. An invalid expression is skipped and logged. When no valid pier or footing pattern exists, the update does nothing. When no valid tag pattern exists, the move does nothing. Limitations Both commands work on the active view only. Only family instances that are visible in the active view are updated. The nearest-pier search is 2D and has a fixed 2 ft radius. Piers and footings are recognized by family name only. Families with other names need a matching pattern. The corner a tag moves to is taken from its name. A tag with another name is skipped. Install/Repair cannot change a label that uses a required parameter with another GUID directly, or the family files in your library. See Families with another GUID.

user-guide/tools/framing-joins.html.title: Allow Join and Disallow Join | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/framing-joins.html.summary: Allow Join and Disallow Join NAME Allow Join, Disallow Join - allow or disallow joins at both ends of framing SYNOPSIS DB Tools > Structural > Allow Join or Disallow Join DESCRIPTION The two commands share one split button. Allow Join allows joins at both ends of each selected Structural Framing element, such as a beam. Disallow Join disallows joins at both ends. Select the framing. The commands are enabled when the selection holds at least one Structural Framing element. On the split button, click Allow Join or Disallow Join. Read the banner. RESULTS A run changes only the Structural Framing elements in the selection. It ignores all other elements, such as structural columns, and does not report them. The banner shows Allowed joins on <n> element(s). or Disallowed joins on <n> element(s). The count <n> includes elements that had that join state already. Each run is one Undo step: DB Tools - Allow Join Selected or DB Tools - Disallow Join Selected. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do Failed to apply allow join operation for element <id>. Revit refused the change for that element. The run stops and changes nothing. The message says disallow for Disallow Join. Find the element with Manage > Select by ID. LIMITS A command always sets both ends of each element. It cannot set one end only. SEE ALSO Analytical Snap To Level, Getting started, DBTools.FramingJoins

user-guide/tools/gm.html.title: Global Mapper | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/gm.html.summary: Global Mapper Global Mapper (GM) replaces project content in bulk. You map a source (a family, a type, a line style, an object style, a material or a parameter) to a target, review the plan, and apply every mapping in one operation. GM also finds likely duplicates, ranks replacement candidates by name and property similarity, and adds shared parameters to families and categories. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Common > Global Mapper. GM opens as a modeless window and needs an open, active project. It works on the active document only. Linked files are not changed. Tab Purpose Duplicates Finds likely duplicate elements and lets you choose which one to keep. Families Maps families and their types, parameters, object styles and materials to other families. Line Styles Replaces line styles. Object Styles Replaces Detail Items object styles. Materials Replaces materials. Shared Parameters Adds shared parameters to families and categories, or maps existing parameters to them. The Shared Parameters tab needs a Revit shared parameter file with at least one group. Without one, GM disables the tab and explains why. Startup waits for all category and parameter-group reads to finish. If a read fails while another is canceled, GM reports the failure. Startup clears the loading state after the reads finish. Usage Open a tab. Choose the source rows to change and the target for each. A target can be chosen by hand or by the similarity ranking. Check Apply on each mapping to include in this run. Click Review Plan. GM opens Commit Review as a modal window and shows the plan. The model is not changed until you click Apply there. Click Apply. Then choose Keep + Continue, Keep + Close GM or Roll back (see Commit Review). Save the project before a bulk change. Header controls These controls apply to the current tab. Control Effect Search: Filters rows by name. Threshold: Slider from 0 to 100%. Sets the minimum similarity for automatic target selection. Sort mode (Similarity / A-Z) Orders target lists by similarity, with colored scores, or alphabetically with no scores. One setting covers the top-level and nested target lists. Hide Unused Hides elements with no instances in the project. Hide Unscanned Hides unscanned rows. Shown on the Families and Shared Parameters tabs only. Applied Only Shows rows with Apply on, including rows linked from other tabs. Not shown on Duplicates, which has its own status filter. Inspector Pane, Preview Panel, Views Panel, SP Authoring Pane Show or hide those panes. Clear... menu Clear Saved Mappings, Clear Saved UI State, Clear Deep Scan Cache (see Saved state). Mapping Conflicts Opens the conflict list. Shown when conflicts exist. Auto-Resolve All resolves them in the order: Duplicates, Tab Defaults, Family Overrides, Manual. The status line at the bottom left shows the loading state, the number of visible rows and the number of applied and conflicting rows of the current tab. A grid shows Loading... while data loads and a No ... message when a loaded result is empty. Similarity and threshold GM scores each target against its source. Scores use the same theme roles in every pane: 90–100 Success, 70–89 Secondary, 50–69 Warning, and 0–49 Muted. Options without a score use Body. At a threshold, an unchanged row selects the highest-scoring target at or above it. If no target qualifies, the row stays empty. A manual choice is never changed by the threshold. Opening a list and closing it without picking another entry is not a manual choice. <Do Not Map> is an explicit choice. On the Duplicates tab, the threshold controls which keep-target candidates appear for each source row. Duplicates tab The tab scans automatically when you open it. It groups elements that look like duplicates by name and property similarity. Styles and materials are matched on their previews. GM does not report two styles or materials as duplicates when it cannot read their previews. Line-style detection covers the whole line-style catalog, including styles with no family usage. Detect refreshes the catalog and the Usage rows and keeps your keep targets. Usage indexing decides which keep targets every restylable curve of a source can accept. While indexing runs, rows show line-style targets pending Usage indexing. A saved keep target stays visible, and Review Plan validates the targets after indexing. Steps Scope the rows. Category limits family rows and follows the category selected elsewhere in GM. Kind filters sources: All, Families, Materials, Line Styles, Object Styles or Shared Params. The status bar filters groups by All, Open, Resolved, Excluded or Conflicts. Group nodes show resolved counts, for example Families (133) · 45 resolved. For each source row, choose the Keep Target. A target must be in the same domain and category as the source. Check Apply for the rows that are ready to commit. Click Accept Applied to stage the rows that are ready. Click Review Plan. Columns Column Description Apply Commit flag for this session. It is off when the tab opens and is never restored from saved state. Source The element to replace, with its Kind, Suggestions and Highest Score. Keep Target The one element that remains. Save Off makes the choice apply to this run only. On saves the keep target for later sessions. Status Ready, Accepted, Mapped, or blank. A row is Ready when Apply is on, the keep target is not the source itself, the row is not excluded, and it has no validation or conflict flag. Choosing the source itself as the keep target marks the row as the keeper and turns Apply off. Accept Applied stages the rows that are Ready, not every row with Apply on. The inspector pane shows candidate details and a Metadata section with the Source ID and instance count. Its Accept split button saves the selection. The drop-down Accept Once keeps it for this session only. For a family row, Edit Type Mapping... in the context menu sets which source types map to which keep types. Shared-parameter duplicate rows can drive the selections on the Shared Parameters tab (Map From and Apply). Keep targets, the one-time-save choice, ignored candidates and exclusions are restored with the saved state. Exclusion badges (Saved, Session, Saved (Overridden)) show the exclusion time in a tooltip when it is known. A chain badge on a candidate shows that its source is already mapped. The tooltip reads Accepted as duplicate → <target>. when the candidate is accepted, or Mapped on the <tab> → <target>. when another tab maps the source. Accepting a candidate whose source another tab maps to a different target raises a Duplicate vs Manual conflict. Conflicts A blocking conflict prevents Review Plan. An advisory conflict (a restored saved choice that is not applied) shows in the conflict list only. The conflict button appears when any conflict exists. If one source is accepted to more than one target, GM raises a duplicate multi-target conflict and offers one-click cleanup. Choosing Keep Manual for a duplicate-versus-manual conflict clears the duplicate row's keep and apply state, so the same conflict does not return. Families tab The tab maps families in the selected category to replacement families. A family can be replaced only by a family of the same category. Columns Column Description Expand (+) Shows the row details. Quantity Instances of the family in the project. Apply Includes the mapping. Source The family. Target The replacement family. Choose the category first, then the target. Select the target with the dropdown; entries show their similarity score. Row details Expand a row to map its parts. The detail tabs are Types, Object Styles, Materials and Parameters. Object Styles and Materials are disabled when empty. The nested target lists use the same sort mode and threshold as the parent list. When you change the parent target, nested lists refill and keep the rows you changed by hand. Types: map each source type to a target type, or select <Do Not Map>. To create a type in the target family, check Create on the type row and enter New Type Name. Created types appear after the refresh that follows a commit. Parameters: map parameter names, with example values. Instance and type parameters are separate mappings, labeled (Instance) and (Type). A parameter maps only to a target of the same scope. GM copies parameter values only through these mappings, and they run with the type replacements. A red ! badge marks a conflict, such as a duplicate target parameter or a missing type-write policy. Resolve it before Review Plan. The Parameters tab shows Parameter scanning is unavailable; parameter mapping is disabled. when scanning is unavailable, and No mappable parameters detected for this family. when it finds none. Expanded rows restored from saved state refresh their Object Styles and Materials usage automatically once usage data is loaded. While a target list is open, the mouse wheel scrolls that list, not the grid behind it. Type-scope writes: if a type-scope mapping writes into a target type that already has instances, GM blocks the commit until you choose Keep target type values (skip type-scope copies) or Overwrite target type values (copy them). GM takes the decision from the model state before the replacement batch starts. Moving the target's instances away earlier in the batch does not cancel Keep target type values. When overwriting is allowed, each mapping copies the original source values, even if an earlier mapping changed that source type. Object Styles and Materials: usage found by walking one placed instance. Rows from a deep scan carry a DS badge. An instance cycler, with previous and next buttons and a zoom button, moves to the sampled instance, even when it is in another view. Badges Badge Meaning OS, MAT, OS+MAT The family Apply state is linked from the Object Styles or Materials tab. LK (OS/MAT) Marks the nested rows that currently drive that link. DS Row data came from a deep scan. A tooltip shows partial-scan warnings. A linked Apply marks the family row, but family-owned operations (type swaps, parameter maps, type creation) run only when you checked that family row yourself. A saved target that is no longer among the options is flagged as incompatible. Choose the target again. Line Styles tab The tab replaces one line style with another. Column Description Apply Includes the mapping. Source The current line style. Target The replacement. Qty The curves in this document that a commit can restyle from this style. Preview A swatch of the style. GM captures each source's curves before it applies any line-style mapping, so a swap A to B and B to A exchanges the two populations, and a chain A to B to C leaves A's curves on B and B's curves on C. The mappings commit one after another inside the single undo step of the apply. A failed mapping rolls back the whole apply. GM restyles a grouped curve only when its group, and every enclosing group, has exactly one placed instance of its group type. Curves in groups with more than one instance are not counted and not replaced, because Revit requires Edit Group mode for them. GM does not enter that mode and does not ungroup elements. Ordinary curves with the same style are counted normally. A target has to be usable by every restylable curve of the source. A saved target that is not usable stays in the saved intent, shows a warning and is left out of the plan until you choose a valid target or Do Not Map. On the Line Styles, Object Styles and Materials tabs, an unavailable saved or chosen target stays visible as a disabled entry with a reason. A refresh keeps it; choose another target to replace it. Object Styles tab The tab replaces object styles of Detail Items subcategories (styles that are not line styles). Selecting a style lists the families that use it. A preview pane shows the style. Checking Apply links the affected families on the Families tab. Unchecking it removes the link. A family keeps its Apply if you checked it or another source links it. A chain badge beside the source shows that another tab, an accepted duplicate or a saved mapping file set the mapping. Its tooltip names the origin, for example From the Duplicates tab. Edit to override. Choosing another target overrides the mapping and removes the badge. The Line Styles and Materials tabs show the same badge. At commit, GM opens each affected family document and ensures the target style exists in it, creating the style when it is missing. It copies the core style appearance from the project target, rewrites the references to the source style, and reloads the family into the project. Before commit, GM leaves out a top-level mapping whose source style has no family usage and no deep-scanned family reference. A mapping found only by a deep scan is kept and appears in Commit Review. A nested mapping whose owner family no longer shows the source in the usage or deep-scan data is left out with a warning. Materials tab The tab replaces materials. Column Description Apply Includes the mapping. Source The material to replace. Target The replacement. Color Preview A swatch of the material color. Families Count Families that use the material. Families affected by a mapping are linked on the Families tab with the badge MAT or OS+MAT. In Families Using This Material, the Apply indicator shows the active link, so a linked family stays marked when a filter hides it from the Families list. At commit, GM updates material parameters in the project and in the affected family documents. When the target material is missing in a family document, GM creates it, copies its core properties and rewrites the references. It then reloads the family. A mapping whose source or target cannot be resolved in the project is ignored before commit and shown as a warning. Revit does not support formulas for parameters of the Material data type. GM migrates writable material defaults for each family type. It leaves formula-determined parameters outside the replacement. A replacement material takes over the appearance and the physical and thermal properties of the new material everywhere the old one was used. Shared Parameters tab The tab adds shared parameters to families and categories, maps existing parameters to shared parameters, and repairs a shared parameter that has the company name but another GUID. The header has a By family / By parameter switch to the left of SP Group. SP Group applies to both views. The tab opens in By family each time. GM does not save the choice. View Use it to By family Work on one family: add parameters, set Map From or a Formula, look at sampled values and instances. By parameter Work on one company parameter across many families: fill it or add it in many families at once, or repair a wrong GUID. The first visit to the tab loads the shared parameter groups and the categories, with a loading overlay once. Later expanding and collapsing, searching, and conflict updates do not show the overlay. Categories The tree lists each category that holds a loadable family in the project, annotation categories included. In-place families are not loadable, so they are not listed. Category labels show counts such as Mechanical Equipment (12). An empty category shows (0) and is dimmed. By default, the tree shows only the categories that hold a family with work to do, and the selected category. A family has work to do when one of these is true: It carries a parameter with the name of a definition in SP Group and another GUID.
