The last use scan in By parameter lists a label, an unread label or a nested family in it that you must fix by hand. A definition of SP Group is missing from the family, and a family parameter scores at or above Threshold as its Map From source. A family whose parameter discovery is incomplete does not count for this reason. A mapping of the family has Apply on and Map From with no source, or the mapping has a conflict. The category tool tip counts the reasons, for example 2 families to map · 1 wrong GUID. The selected category shows No work to do when it has none. The tree computes the list again when the SP Group, the threshold, a mapping or a scan result changes. The selected category stays in the list until you select another one. Check Show all categories above the tree to show every category. The check box is off when the tab opens. In By parameter, the family table lists the families of the categories that the tree shows, so the check box applies to both views. By family The left panel shows the category tree, then families, then types, then up to five sampled instances of each type, labeled for example Instance #1 (id:123456). The SP Authoring pane on the right shows a card for each shared parameter of the selected type. Close hides the pane. Select a group in SP Group. Expand a category and a family, and select a type. The panel shows the existing parameters with sampled values, and the shared parameters of the group. For each parameter to add, check Apply. Choose Embed In Family or leave it clear, and choose Instance Parameter or Type Parameter for Binding. Optionally fill the new parameter from an existing one: set Source to Map From and choose the parameter in From, or set it to Formula, enter it in Fmla and click Set. Click Review Plan. A Map From card shows ← <name> with the source name. The source card shows the FROM badge. Each card has the link Every use of this parameter →. It opens By parameter with that definition selected. When the project holds a definition of SP Group with a GUID that differs from the company file, the SP Authoring pane shows a warning above the cards: This project has "<name>" with a GUID that differs from the company file. This family carries "<name>" with a GUID that differs from the company file. when GM knows that the selected family carries it. The link Review every use → opens By parameter in repair mode for that name. Embed In Family Effect Clear Adds the parameter to the category as a project parameter. If the parameter already has a binding, GM adds the category to it and keeps its group. See Binding rules. Checked Adds the parameter inside the family document, so it travels with the family. Plan validation checks that each selected type still belongs to its family and category. It rejects a mismatched or stale selection with an error before apply. Map From writes the value that the Examples column shows: Between two parameters of the same type (Length to Length, Text to Text, Yes/No to Yes/No), the stored value is copied exactly. Into a Text parameter, GM writes the source as shown, with the document's units (300 mm, Yes, or the name of a phase or level). Into a Length, Area or other measured parameter, GM reads the source as Revit reads typed input, in the document's units. In a millimeter project, 12 is 12 mm. Text read into a Number or Integer parameter uses the decimal separator of your Windows number format and no thousands separators. With a decimal point, 1.5 is 1.5, and 1,5 or 1,500 is not written. With a decimal comma, 1,5 is 1.5, and 1.5 or 1.500 is not written. An Integer parameter takes only whole numbers, so 2.5 is not written. A value that cannot be read this way is not written. Examples are a Yes/No into a Number, 300 mm into an Integer, or a level or phase name into another element parameter. Commit Review lists the operation as Failed, with the value, the parameter and the reason, and writes none of its values. The Formula preview reads values by the same rules, including a measured value in the unit it shows. When a value cannot be read as a number, the preview shows that it is unavailable and names the parameter. The preview cannot evaluate functions such as if; it shows that it is unavailable and names the function. The instance navigator, beside SP Group, steps through the sampled instances of the selected type with the previous and next buttons, and selects that instance in the tree. Zoom shows the current instance in Revit, even when it is not in the active view. With Auto-zoom checked, each step also zooms to the new instance. The instance navigator, Auto-zoom and Zoom show in By family only. By parameter The left side, 1 · Pick a parameter, lists the definitions of SP Group. Each item shows one status line: Company · <n> families have this name: <n> counts the families of the shown categories whose parameter names include the definition name. It counts names, not GUIDs. A warning icon and Two GUIDs in this project: the project holds a shared parameter with that name and another GUID. This status comes from a scan of the whole project, so it shows even when the tree hides the family. Select a definition to show its uses on the right. A definition with Two GUIDs in this project opens the repair table. Every other definition opens the family table. Every use of this parameter → in By family always opens the family table. Below the table, Other uses found: lists the uses of the company GUID, for example Project binding: Structural Foundations · instance. It shows Labels: not scanned until a full use scan has run. Fill or add one parameter in many families The family table has the title Every use of <name> and the hint Tick the families to fill or re-point. It lists each family of the shown categories that has at least one type. A family that already has a parameter with the definition name is not listed. Column Content Apply Checked adds the definition to every type of the family. Family <family> · <n> placed. No match · choose shows when no family parameter scores at or above Threshold. By family selections differ shows when the types of the family have different mappings. Fill from (suggested) — (no value), then the family's parameters, sorted by score, for example FLOW_RATE (92%). GM selects the best parameter when it scores at or above Threshold, else — (no value). When the ticked types of a family all map from one source, the row shows that source and adds it to the list if needed. — (no value) means no Map From: GM adds the parameter with no value. Go to Open in By family selects the family and its first type in By family. It checks Show all categories when the tree hides the family's category. To fill one company field across many families: Select a group in SP Group, then click By parameter. Select the definition in 1 · Pick a parameter. Choose Embed In Family and Binding (Instance or Type) above the table. They apply to every ticked family, with the same meaning as on the By family card. Binding starts at Type. For each family, read the source in Fill from (suggested). Choose another source where the suggestion is wrong or the row shows No match · choose. Check Apply on each family to fill. Click Review Plan. To add a company parameter to many families with no value, do the same steps, and choose — (no value) in Fill from (suggested) on each family. A tick in By parameter writes the same mappings that By family writes, one for each type of the family. A change in one view shows in the other view, and both views use one plan. Repair a parameter with another GUID A parameter has a wrong GUID when it has the name of a company definition but another GUID. Revit treats the two as different parameters. GM moves each use of the old GUID to the company definition, keeps every value, or refuses. When you select a definition with Two GUIDs in this project, GM scans the project and opens every editable loadable family, under a progress overlay (Scanning shared parameter uses...). The overlay has Cancel. When you cancel the first scan of a definition, or it fails, the table shows Scan the families first. GM keeps a finished result until a Scan again finishes, you keep an apply, or you close GM. The repair table has the title Every use of the old GUID, the hint Tick the uses to move. and Re-point to <name> (company GUID). Its columns are Move, Use, Where, Reason and Go to. Use Move Move project binding Tick it to move the project parameter, its binding, its values, its schedule fields and its view filter rules. It can be ticked only when every other use is ready (see the steps below). Reason names what keeps it closed. Move family parameter One row for each family. Tick it to move the family parameter, with its formulas, dimension labels and associated parameters. Labels · fix by hand Not ticked. Where reads <family>: <n> labels in groups <names>. Reason says what to change. Family use · fix by hand Not ticked. A nested family or an unread label that you fix by hand. Copy stored values Follows Move project binding. You cannot change it. Move schedule uses Follows Move project binding. You cannot change it. View filters Follows Move project binding. You cannot change it. A row that GM cannot move safely shows the reason and has no tick. Open in By family on a family or label row selects that family in By family. Scan again, next to Re-point to, runs the full scan again for the selected definition, for example after you fix a family by hand. A tick stays when the new scan lists the row again and the row can still be ticked. GM clears every other tick. If the scan fails or you click Cancel, the table keeps the earlier result. The repair runs in two phases, because deleting the old project parameter also removes it from the labels of loaded families: Phase 1 moves the ticked family parameters. The old project parameter, its binding, schedule fields, filter rules and values stay. GM refuses phase 1 alone while a schedule field or a filter rule uses the old GUID, because the moved families would no longer fill it. Move the project binding in the same apply instead. When labels also remain, so the project binding cannot move yet, take the field out of the schedule or the rule out of the filter, repair, and then add them back with the company parameter. Phase 2 moves the project binding. It runs only when Move project binding is ticked, every family parameter is ticked, and no use is left to fix by hand or blocked. To repair a parameter: Select the definition with Two GUIDs in this project, or click Review every use → in By family. Wait for the scan. If the table shows Scan the families first., the scan did not finish or Revit did not open every editable family. Close any family that is open in the Family Editor, then click Scan families. Tick Move family parameter on each family that can move. Read each Labels · fix by hand and Family use · fix by hand row. These uses keep Move project binding closed. Tick Move project binding if it is open. Click Review Plan, then Apply in Commit Review. When labels remain, apply phase 1 first. Then fix the labels by hand: Click Open in By family on the label row, or open the family in the Family Editor. Edit each listed label. In a detail group, edit the group first. Replace the parameter with the parameter of the same name and the company GUID, and keep its formatting. Load the family into the project again, and close it in the Family Editor. Click Scan again. Move project binding opens when no hand-fix use remains. Revit 2026 does not let DB Tools read annotation labels. In Revit 2026, an annotation family that contains the old GUID directly shows a Family use · fix by hand row, with Family '<family>' contains unread label uses of '<name>'. The row stays while the family contains the old GUID, even after you fix every label. Fix the labels, then use Purge Unused in the Family Editor to remove the unused parameter, and load the family again. A repair must be the only change in a plan. When other mappings are pending, Review Plan shows Apply the repair on its own: clear the other mappings, or apply them first. and Apply is disabled. In Commit Review, the repair shows in the Shared Parameters section as Old GUID uses → <name> (company GUID), in the stage Shared Parameters (Repair). At Apply, GM scans again. If the project changed after Review Plan, the repair fails with The project changed after Review Plan. Review the plan again. and changes nothing. A failure or Cancel in either phase rolls back the whole attempt, phase 1 included. When hand-fix uses remain after a successful repair, Commit Review shows Completed with Warnings, with one Manual shared parameter repair remains: <text> warning for each use. Keep + Continue and Keep + Close GM clear the repair ticks and the use scan results. GM does not save repair ticks. Binding rules These rules apply to both views when GM binds a shared parameter to a category. Project state GM does The project does not hold the parameter Binds it. The project holds the parameter with no binding (families define it) Instance binding: records the values that loaded families hold, binds, and writes the values back. Type binding: refuses with Binding "<name>" as a type parameter could change values that loaded families hold. Bind it as an instance parameter. An instance binding exists Adds the category and keeps every value and the setting that lets values vary between group instances. A type binding exists Refuses with GM cannot add a category to the type binding of "<name>" and prove that every value stays. Add the category in Manage > Project Parameters. The binding kind would change between instance and type Refuses. GM does not add a second GUID for one name. When the project, or the target family for Embed In Family, already has the name with another GUID, Review Plan lists "<name>" already exists in this project with another GUID. Repair it in By parameter first. and Apply is disabled. GM checks again at apply, before it changes the project or the family. A family loaded between review and apply therefore fails the operation, and GM rolls the attempt back. GM also refuses when a project or family parameter with the name is not shared. Deep scan Some family details, such as embedded parameters and nested families, need a deep scan. A deep scan opens the family document. It is always started by you; GM does not scan when you expand a row. A deep scan is needed to: unlock the expanded details of a family with no instances (Scan required); read embedded definitions, such as nested family graphs, that a placed instance does not expose. For a family with instances, the Object Styles and Materials details come from walking one placed instance, so a deep scan is usually not needed. That walk records whether a source appears directly in the root family or only inside nested family content, and planning reuses that. Action Effect Scan Family (in the expanded details) Always runs a fresh deep scan. A complete result replaces the cache entry. An incomplete result removes the previous reusable entry. Deep Scan Unscanned (top-bar icon, Families tab) Scans all unscanned families with no instances in the current category, after a confirmation, with a progress overlay. Clear Deep Scan Cache Deletes the cached results and refreshes the display before it reports success. Results are cached across sessions. At startup GM restores cached results for eligible families with no instances. The restore is strict: if the cache entry does not resolve in the current document (for example a missing or ambiguous style or material), GM logs a warning and leaves the family unscanned. No banner appears. If you clear the cache while the restore runs, the cleared families stay unscanned until you scan them again. If Revit reports an error while GM reads a family parameter, GM keeps the names it read as diagnostics and marks parameter discovery incomplete. Those names are not offered as mapping choices and are not used for duplicate scoring. GM also removes the older reusable cache entry for that family. A separate successful read of the host can still fill the mapping choices. Otherwise, scan again after you fix the reported problem. If GM cannot fully resolve nested-family or material usage during a scan, it keeps the extracted details and warnings visible as a partial result, and does not cache or restore the family as complete. Scan again after you fix the reported references. A malformed or incomplete cache entry is deleted and needs a new scan. The cache is disposable and is not migrated between formats. Saved state GM saves your mappings and window state for each project, by its file path. Each unsaved document has its own state, so unsaved documents with the same title do not share state. On reopen, saved targets are restored as suggestions. Apply is left off, so nothing is enabled for commit. Menu item (Clear...) Effect Clear Saved Mappings Removes the mapping and duplicate selections for this document. The mappings do not return from an older saved file or from an open GM window. Clear Saved UI State Removes the tab, search, filter and scroll state. The next GM window for the document starts with default state. An open window does not write its older state back when it closes. Clear Deep Scan Cache Removes deep-scan data and the DS badges. Each Clear... item asks for confirmation, and Cancel clears nothing. A completed clear shows a success banner, for example Cleared saved mappings for this document. A failed clear shows an error banner titled with the action, for example GM Clear Saved Mappings, and no success banner. If GM cannot write the saved mappings, it logs the failure and shows an error banner, and your mappings may not persist. If the saved-mappings file has a format that this GM version cannot read, GM shows a banner and continues without restoring it. A saved target, or a saved Shared Parameters Map From source, that no longer exists is flagged as incompatible and must be created again. A style target must belong to the scope of its source (Line Styles or Object Styles). Each of the Materials, Line Styles and Object Styles tabs lists only its own kind of element. Result Commit Review Review Plan opens Commit Review. Revit is blocked while it is open. The window shows: the planned operations, by section (Plan Overview, Planned Operations, Host Replacements, Family Changes, Nested Families, Shared Parameters, Validation Issues); sections that do not apply are hidden; after apply, Commit Results, Stage Summary (succeeded, failed and skipped counts per stage, with affected references, family and timing context) and Family Breakdown; an Operation Results table with a status for each operation (Pending, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped), its operation id, stage and timing. Failed operations are summarized per mapping rule, with the source and target display names rather than element ids. The status bar shows the apply phase before the commit and the Applied, Skipped and Failed counts after it. Right-click a report table for Copy Selected or Copy All. Copy Report copies the whole report. Failed in the rules summary counts failed mapping rules. One rule can run across many families. Use the Families line (Planned / Attempted / Failed) and the Failed Operations row, which adds up the per-family failures. Apply and keep Apply runs the plan as one operation. The changes stay provisional while Commit Review shows the results. The commit continues after a failed operation: failures are recorded and the remaining operations run. The overlay Cancel button requests cancellation at once. After the run, GM verifies that no references to a source remain. Outcome What you can do Every operation succeeded and verification found no remaining source Choose Keep + Continue, Keep + Close GM or Roll back. An operation failed, verification found a remaining source, or the apply was canceled GM rolls the attempt back. Nothing is kept. Inspect the errors and choose Retry Apply to run the reviewed plan against the current model. Succeeded with nonfatal warnings Labeled Completed with Warnings. The Operation Warnings section lists each distinct instance, parameter and reason. Review it before you keep the changes. Keep remains available when verification succeeds. Keep + Continue records the mappings and returns to GM. GM refreshes the mapped data in place and restores the expanded row context. Types created with Create appear in the refreshed rows. Deep Scan results stay for families the commit did not change. Scan a changed family again to restore its details. Keep + Close GM records the mappings and closes GM. Roll back restores the model and creates no undo entry. A kept apply is one undo entry named Global Mapper: Apply. Press Ctrl+Z to revert it. Do not leave Commit Review open after Apply. Choose Keep or Roll back first. Closing the window with the X: during apply, requests cancellation and cleanup, then closes. If the cleanup fails, the window stays open and shows the error; after apply, asks whether to keep or roll back, with Roll back as the default. After any apply, GM re-reads the affected rows and counts from the model, whether the apply was kept or rolled back. A banner reports the outcome: A successful apply shows a green banner with the Applied, Failed and Skipped counts. If the apply has operation warnings, the banner is a warning banner that ends with Operation warnings: <n>. A failed apply shows a red banner that starts with the reason, for example Apply was rolled back: 1 operation(s) failed. No changes were kept. or Apply failed; no changes were kept. Commit Review stays open. A canceled apply shows Apply was canceled. No changes were kept. If an apply seems to stall near 90%, Revit is still processing one operation. Click Cancel once and wait. GM cancels and cleans up when that operation ends. If it does not recover, report it with the newest DB Tools log. How replacement batches behave Line styles, host materials, family materials, family object styles, types, host symbols and nested-family replacements use each mapping's original source population. A swap A to B and B to A exchanges the populations. A chain A to B and B to C leaves the original A population on B and the original B population on C. References moved by an earlier mapping do not become a later mapping's source. A shared nested family can appear under several selected roots. GM combines its applicable mappings and changes each original reference once. Later family reloads keep the result. Equivalent duplicate mappings get a merged notice. Conflicting targets for the same family source need your attention. A source that is absent from a traversed family is zero work, not a failed mapping. When a family reload cannot complete, every family operation that ran in that traversal is shown as failed, including equivalent shared-family aliases. The report keeps the affected count for writes completed before the failure and shows the reason. GM rolls the whole apply back, and you can choose Retry Apply. A failed operation can report writes that succeeded before it failed. Those counts are diagnostics, and the rollback discards the writes. If one half of a swap fails, the successful half could leave both populations on one target. For that reason GM rolls back the whole apply. Unchanged shared children stay on the project version during another family's reload. Shared children that the current traversal changed are reloaded from the edited family document. The family-document counts in Commit Review include the examined root and nested family documents, including documents where a source has no references. A parent-only material mapping leaves a shared child's material defaults unchanged. Map the child itself, or include it in the traversal, to change those defaults. Messages GM reports results and problems in banners with the title Global Mapper. Message Meaning Apply completed. Applied: <n>, Failed: <n>, Skipped: <n>. Family documents attempted: <n>, family document failures: <n>. The apply finished. The banner adds Operation warnings: <n>. when operations reported warnings, and Verification warning: <text> when the reference check found a problem. Apply was rolled back: <n> operation(s) failed. No changes were kept. One or more operations failed. Inspect the errors in Commit Review and choose Retry Apply. Apply was rolled back: <reason> No changes were kept. The check after the apply found a remaining source reference. Apply failed; no changes were kept. The apply stopped with an error. Commit Review stays open. Apply was canceled. No changes were kept. You canceled the apply. Keep is unavailable: the last apply kept no changes. Retry Apply or close Commit Review. Keep was chosen after an apply that was rolled back. No conflicts to resolve. Auto-Resolve All found no conflicts. No auto-resolvable conflicts were found. The remaining conflicts need a manual choice. Queued creation of new type: '<name>'. You can rename before commit in Commit Review. A Create row was added on the Types detail tab. No unscanned (0-instance) families are eligible for deep scan. Deep Scan Unscanned has no family to scan in the current category. Deep scan cache cleared. Clear Deep Scan Cache finished. Cleared saved mappings for this document. Clear Saved Mappings finished. Cleared saved UI state. Next open will use defaults. Clear Saved UI State finished. No placed instances found to navigate to. The instance cycler has no instance to show. Saved mapping source parameter '<name>' is not available. Re-create the mapping. A saved Shared Parameters Map From source no longer exists. Configure a Revit shared parameter file that has at least one group to use this tab. The Shared Parameters tab is disabled. Set a shared parameter file in Revit. Apply the repair on its own: clear the other mappings, or apply them first. A plan holds a repair and other mappings. Commit Review shows Repair must be applied on its own, and Apply is disabled. "<name>" already exists in this project with another GUID. Repair it in By parameter first. A bind or embed would add a second GUID for the name. Repair the parameter first. At plan time, Commit Review shows Shared parameter GUID conflicts prevent Apply. The project changed after Review Plan. Review the plan again. The repair scan at apply found a change since the review. Nothing changed. Binding "<name>" as a type parameter could change values that loaded families hold. Bind it as an instance parameter. Loaded families define the parameter and the project does not bind it. GM cannot add a category to the type binding of "<name>" and prove that every value stays. Add the category in Manage > Project Parameters. The parameter has a type binding. Manual shared parameter repair remains: <text> An operation warning after a repair. Fix the named use by hand. Inline texts: Deep scan to unlock details for families without instances (row tooltip): the family has no instances and no deep scan. Run Scan Family. Parameter scanning is unavailable; parameter mapping is disabled. and No mappable parameters detected for this family. (Parameters detail tab). line-style targets pending Usage indexing (Duplicates row): wait until indexing ends. Scan the families first. (By parameter repair table): the scan did not finish, or Revit did not open every editable family. Click Scan families. No families in the shown categories. (By parameter family table): no family of the shown categories can take the parameter. Check Show all categories. When an action fails unexpectedly, GM shows an error banner titled with the action, for example GM Duplicate Type Mapping, GM Deep Scan or GM Clear Saved Mappings, followed by the error text. The action changes nothing. Retry it, and read the DB Tools log if it fails again. If Review Plan is disabled, no mapping is applied, or a blocking conflict exists. If the target list is empty, the category has no other family. If some instances were not replaced, open the family and check that every type is mapped. Limitations GM changes the active document only. A family can only be replaced by a family of the same category. Line style and object style scopes are limited as described above: curves in multi-instance groups are not restyled, and the Object Styles tab covers Detail Items subcategories only. Commit time grows with the number of elements and families. A few dozen changes finish at once; thousands can take minutes. The progress overlay shows the state. The Revit API cannot change an annotation label. GM lists each label that uses an old GUID, and you fix it by hand. Revit 2026 does not let DB Tools read annotation labels. An annotation family that contains an old GUID keeps the binding move closed until the family no longer contains it. A repair changes the families loaded in the project, not the family files on disk. A family loaded again from an old file brings the old GUID back. A repair moves uses only to the company definition with the same name. To move values between two names, use Map From. GM does not repair these cases. The row shows the reason and has no tick: The project already binds the company GUID. More than one other GUID with the name has a project parameter. A combined parameter schedule field, a schedule with a calculated field (Revit counts a percentage field as one), or a schedule filter value that GM cannot carry. A view filter rule or evaluator that GM cannot carry and verify. A non-editable nested family that DB Tools cannot inspect, in a family that uses the old GUID directly (not as a family parameter). GM moves a family parameter even when its family has a non-editable nested family. If a hidden use keeps the old GUID after the reload, GM refuses the move and rolls the attempt back. A schedule field that shows totals, a minimum or a maximum that the company parameter's field cannot show refuses the binding move at apply. By parameter has no Formula source. Write formulas in By family.

user-guide/tools/joist-girder-weight.htm.title: Update Joist Girder Weights | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/joist-girder-weight.htm.summary: Update Joist Girder Weights NAME Update Joist Girder Weights - estimate the weight of each joist girder and write it to Wt SYNOPSIS DB Tools > Structural > Update Joist Girder Weights DESCRIPTION The tool estimates the self-weight of each joist girder in the model, in pounds per foot (lb/ft). It writes the estimate to the girder's Wt parameter and changes nothing else. A joist girder is a Structural Framing element whose family name matches Family/Type Name Pattern. By default, these are the families G Joist Girder, BG Joist Girder, VG Joist Girder and Vulcraft Joist Girder. The estimate uses four values of the girder: Length, Depth, Number of Joists and the point load. The point load is the load, in kips, at each panel point where a joist bears on the girder. The tool works on the whole model. It skips a girder with a missing or invalid value. REQUIREMENTS For each value, the tool tries each listed name on the girder, then on its type, and uses the first value found. Value Parameters Rule Number of Joists Number of Joists, SpaceNum, Number of Equal Spaces Must be more than 1. Enter the number of equal spaces, not of joists. Length Cut Length, Length Must be more than 0. Depth Depth Must be more than 0. Point load Parameters that match the load patterns See Loads. Weight Wt An editable Number parameter. The tool writes lb/ft here. Text values for the first three must be plain numbers. Length and Depth are in feet. A parameter of type Length works in any display units. In a Number or text parameter, enter 48 in. as 4. Loads The point load is the total load, or else the dead load plus the live load. The load patterns in SETTINGS find each kind by parameter name. The tool skips the girder if two parameters of one kind have values, if a load is negative, or if no usable load exists. A Force parameter is converted to kips. Other numbers are kips. Text can add a unit: k, kip, kips, lb, lbs, lbf, pound, pounds or kN. SETTINGS Open DB Tools > Settings, expand Structural Settings and find Joist Girder Weights. Auto Update Joist Girder Weights runs the tool, without a banner, each time you open or switch to a view. It is on by default. It can slow view changes in a large model. To see what it skips, run the tool from the ribbon. The four patterns are .NET regular expressions. By default, the load patterns match DL, LL, and names that contain Dead Load, Live Load, Point Load or Total Load. The defaults are: Family/Type Name Pattern ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$ Dead Load Pattern (?:^DL$|Dead\s*Load) Live Load Pattern (?:^LL$|Live\s*Load) Total Load Pattern (?:Point\s*Load|Total\s*Load) RESULTS A run from the ribbon ends with a banner like this: Candidates: 12 Updated: 10 Skipped: 2 Sample skipped element(s): - Element 412345: Depth must be > 0. - Element 412377: Number of joists must be > 1. Candidates is the number of joist girders found. The banner lists up to 5 skipped girders, with the first problem of each. Find each girder with Manage > Select by ID, fix it, and run the tool again. Each run that changes values is one Undo step: Auto Update Joist Girder Weights. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do Required writable Double parameter 'Wt' not found. Add Wt as an editable Number parameter. Missing required input for 'Point Load'. … No load parameter has a value. Fill in a load, or match the load patterns to your names. Ambiguous <kind> Load inputs: … Two parameters of one kind, such as Dead Load and DL, have values. Clear one. Joist Girder Weights Disabled (a warning in Settings) A saved pattern is not valid, so the tool is off. Correct the pattern and click Save Settings. Auto-update failed; disabled for this document session. Auto-update stays off until you reopen the model. LIMITS The weight is an estimate from a fixed formula, not from SJI or manufacturer tables. A blank Number total load counts as 0 and replaces the dead and live loads, so Wt becomes 0 with no warning. Fill in or delete it. Make Wt an instance parameter. A type parameter gives all girders of that type one value. A Wt with units, such as Length, shows a wrong value. EXAMPLES To also use the family Acme Girder, set Family/Type Name Pattern to this value and click Save Settings: ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$|^Acme Girder$ SEE ALSO Getting started, DBTools.JoistGirderWeight

user-guide/tools/organize-foundation.htm.title: Organize Foundation Types | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/organize-foundation.htm.summary: Organize Foundation Types Organize Foundation Types renames pier, footing and pile cap types by their dimensions, assigns sequential type marks, and merges types that have identical dimensions. It changes types. It does not move placed instances. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > the foundation tags split button (with Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags). The command processes the whole model. It is disabled while the Combined Foundation Tags Disabled warning is active (see Combined Foundation Tags). Usage Save the model. Run Organize Foundation Types. Answer Do you want to overwrite existing type marks? Read the Organize Foundation Types result dialog. Answer Effect Yes Regenerates the type mark of every processed type. No Keeps existing type marks. Types with an empty type mark receive a new one. Processed types The tool processes types of these families (exact names, case-sensitive): Family Category Dimension parameters Mark prefix Foundation Pier Structural Columns b, h P Foundation Pier - Round Structural Columns d RP Footing-Rectangular Structural Foundations Width, Length, Foundation Thickness F Pile Cap-Rectangular Structural Foundations Width, Length, Foundation Thickness CAP Types of other families are not processed. Naming and marks Each type is renamed as <dimensions> (<mark>). Dimensions are formatted in feet and fractional inches. Family Name format Example Foundation Pier <b>x<h> (<mark>) 2'-6"x2'-6" (P-1) Foundation Pier - Round <d> DIA. (<mark>) 2'-0" DIA. (RP-1) Footing-Rectangular <width>x<length>x<thickness> (<mark>) 3'-0"x3'-0"x1'-0" (F-3.0) Pile Cap-Rectangular <width>x<length>x<thickness> (<mark>) 4'-0"x4'-0"x2'-0" (CAP-4.0) Types are processed in ascending order of size, and marks are assigned in that order: piers: section area b x h; round piers: diameter; footings and pile caps: width, then length, then thickness. Pier and round pier marks are P-1, P-2, ... and RP-1, RP-2, .... Footing and pile cap marks are <prefix>-<w>.<n>, where <w> is the width in whole feet (rounded down) and <n> counts from 0 within that width: F-3.0, F-3.1, CAP-4.0. Merging Types of one family with equal dimension values are duplicates. The tool keeps the first in the sort order, changes every instance of the other types to the kept type, and deletes the other types. Equality is exact on the stored values, so types that differ by a small amount are not merged. Instances stay where they are. Result The run is one undo entry. The result dialog shows the number of types renamed, duplicates merged and types skipped: Successfully organized pier and footing types. - N types renamed - N duplicates merged - N types skipped When types are skipped, the first line reads Organized pier and footing types with skipped types. and the dialog adds up to 5 lines <type id>: <reason>. A type is skipped when Revit rejects its change, for example when the new name already exists. The remaining types are still processed. If a merged type cannot be deleted, the command fails and changes nothing. Press Ctrl+Z to undo the whole run. Limitations With No, the tool does not compare new marks with preserved marks that come later in the sort order, so two types can end with the same mark. Use Yes for a consistent set. The tool changes only the type name and the Type Mark parameter, and the type of merged instances. The type mark is written only when the Type Mark parameter is a writable text parameter. Linked models are not processed. Types that Revit rejects are skipped, not retried.

user-guide/tools/recordset.html.title: Record Set | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/recordset.html.summary: Record Set NAME Record Set - copy Revit host models and their linked files into one package folder SYNOPSIS DB Tools > Testing > Record Set DESCRIPTION Record Set copies host RVT files and their file-based links into a target folder. Then it changes the links in the copied hosts to point to the copies. It copies the files as saved on disk, and changes no source file. Click Target Folder... and choose the target folder. Click Add Revit File... and choose host RVT files. With hosts in the list, the button is Add host. In Host Models, set Discipline and Building for each host. Choose < Add new… > to type a name. Read the Preview tree and the Preview Messages. Right-click a DWG in the tree to set its CAD handling. Click Execute. Execute is available when the preview is up to date, the footer shows Root Allowed, and no message has the severity Block. OPTIONS The Options menu above the preview: Item Effect Manage Disciplines..., Manage Buildings... Add, rename or delete names. A rename or a delete also applies to the hosts and links. Auto-discover CAD Xrefs Find the Xrefs of each DWG, also nested ones, with AutoCAD Core Console. Copy each Xref file into the folder of the DWG copy. Allow CAD repath With discovery, point each Xref in the DWG copies at its copy, with a relative path such as .\Grid.dwg. Both CAD options start on only when Core Console is found. Without discovery, Record Set copies the folders xrefs, xref, refs, ref, external, dwg and cad that are beside the DWG to the same place beside the DWG copy. Names and options last until the window closes. The context menu of a DWG link in the tree: Item Effect CAD: Keep Xrefs The default. Copy the DWG and its Xrefs as the Options menu sets. CAD: Bind All Bind every Xref into the DWG copy, with Core Console. It drops the Xrefs added with Add Xref... from the plan. Bind Type > Bind or Insert For CAD: Bind All, Bind sets AutoCAD BINDTYPE 0 and Insert sets 1. Add Xref... Add a DWG Xref by hand. It is copied beside the DWG copy. REQUIREMENTS Item Rule Target folder Must be in \\fileserver\Projects, a root built into the tool. Otherwise Root shows Blocked. Free space At Execute, the target drive must keep 10 GiB free after the copy. AutoCAD Core Console Needed for discovery, repath and Bind All. Record Set uses the ACCORECONSOLE environment variable, then PATH, then the newest AutoCAD or DWG TrueView. The footer shows the path in ACAD. RESULTS <target>\<building>\<discipline>\<host>.rvt <target>\<building>\<discipline>\Linked Files\<link> a link of one host <target>\Common Linked Files\<link> a link of two or more hosts The default building - and an empty discipline add no folder. A link is common when its full path appears two or more times, even in one host. When two different source files would get one target path, the second gets <name> (2).<ext>, and so on. Execute copies the files, does the CAD work, and then changes the links in the host copies. A copy replaces an existing file in the target and keeps the source timestamps. After the run, an alert shows Status: ok and the manifest path. A failed run shows no alert, logs the error and opens the logger window. Record Set adds no Undo step. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do Policy denied host file: <name>, and the other Policy denied … messages The file is not copied. The tool excludes .dwl, .dwl2, .tmp, .bak, .lnk and .exe files, and names that match *backup*.rvt, *.old or ~$*. Xref <name> in <dwg> not found: <stored path> The file is not at its stored path or in the DWG folder. The DWG copy keeps the stored path. CAD Xref discovery failed for <name>: <error>. Using fallback. Record Set copies the Xref folders as without discovery, and changes no Xref path. Bind All blocked for <dwg>: … A Block. Every direct and nested Xref must exist and must not be excluded. Fix the Xref, or choose CAD: Keep Xrefs. Total size <bytes> exceeds limit., Total plan item count <n> exceeds limit. A Block. The plan is over 80 GiB or 10,000 items. Put fewer hosts in each package. FILES <target>\.recordset.lock exists while a run is active <target>\.recordset_sentinel marks a Record Set target <target>\_recordset_manifests\<run>.json the run ID, counts and status (ok or failed) LIMITS A failed run does not undo its work. Read the log and the manifest before you run again. If a run stops without removing .recordset.lock, the next run at that target fails. Delete the lock only when no Execute runs on that target. Execute cannot be canceled. Record Set does not copy the links of linked models. Without discovery, or without Allow CAD repath, the DWG copies keep their stored Xref paths. An absolute path still points to the source. Links with a path relative to a Revit library location are not copied or changed. SEE ALSO Getting started, DBTools.RecordSet

user-guide/tools/sgt.html.title: Super Girt Tool | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/sgt.html.summary: Super Girt Tool NAME Super Girt Tool - place girts, headers, sills and jambs on one wall SYNOPSIS DB Tools > Structural > Super Girt Tool To change a placed system, select one of its members, then click Modify | Structural Framing > Super Girt > Edit SGT Wall. DESCRIPTION Super Girt Tool (SGT) frames one straight wall with horizontal girts. At each opening, it can add a header, a sill and two jambs. It stores the configuration with the members for later edits. Click Super Girt Tool and pick a wall in a linked model. For a foundation wall of the host model, press Esc at that prompt; SGT then asks for a host wall. SGT analyzes the wall and opens its window. It adds girt rows at the base and every 5'-0" above it. Change the rows and openings. The preview shows the result. Click Place. SGT places the members and closes the window. Elevations are heights above the base: the bottom of a linked wall, or the top of a foundation wall. On a foundation wall, SGT frames a fixed band 20'-0" high above the foundation, and ignores the openings of that wall. OPTIONS Type a length as decimal feet (7.5), feet and inches (7'-6 1/2") or inches (18"). A number without a mark is in feet. Layer The wall layer that the members align to. The default is the most-exterior structural layer. If none exists, SGT chooses the thickest non-finish layer, or the thickest layer when all are finishes. Ties favor the exterior layer. Offset The distance from that layer, across the wall. A positive value moves the members toward the exterior. Girts Each row is one girt at one Elevation, with a Girt Type. When you choose a type of another family, SGT replaces Rotation, Y Justification, Z Justification and Flip with the defaults of that family. To add a row, type an elevation next to Add Girt and click it. Openings On a linked wall, SGT detects doors, windows and wall openings. Add Opening adds one by hand. Center Along is the distance from the wall start to the opening center. The Left Jamb, Right Jamb, Header and Sill boxes turn each member on or off. A girt is split at each opening that it crosses. Click the chevron of a split row to edit each segment. Double-click a row to open Bulk Edit for that row and the other selected rows. Preview The preview has an Elevation, a Section and a 3D mode. Elevation shows the wall from the exterior, so the wall start is at the right. Left Jamb and Right Jamb are left and right in this view. In Elevation, drag a member's end handle to a grid line, an opening edge, a wall edge or another member. A drag that ends elsewhere changes nothing. Double-click an end handle to type the gap at that end. The Undo and Redo buttons of the window apply only to these edits. REQUIREMENTS Item Rule Wall A straight wall in a loaded link, or a host wall whose type has the function Foundation. Girt types Structural Framing types of editable families: C and MC channels, Z shapes, angles and HSS. Opening types Channels and HSS only. Girt end gaps A girt with a gap needs the Start Extension and End Extension parameters. SGT knows a shape by the Structural Section Shape, Section Shape or Shape parameter, or by names such as C10X15.3, C Shapes or HSS. It skips a family or type whose name contains joist, girder or truss. SGT prefers C Shapes : C10X15.3 as the default girt type. If that type is not eligible, SGT selects another eligible type. RESULTS Place creates and tags the members. SGT writes the end gaps of each girt to its Start Extension and End Extension, as negative values. For an edited system, Update moves the existing members, creates the missing ones and deletes the extra ones. Update Summary then lists each change as Moved, Recreated or Deleted. Delete System deletes the members and the configuration. Cancel or closing the window rolls back the session. Change Review Change Review opens when you edit a system whose wall or openings changed in the model. Review Changes opens it at any time. Decision Effect Accept Use the changed geometry from the model. Keep Keep the geometry of the last placement, or the values that you typed. Ignore Leave the framing as placed. Change Review asks again next time. Confirm saves the decisions and changes no framing; click Update afterward. Relink moves the system to another wall. Deconstruct removes the SGT data and keeps the members as plain framing. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do [SpecFail/Calibration/NoEligibleFamilies] No eligible structural framing families found … No loaded family meets the REQUIREMENTS. Load one, such as C Shapes. Profile warmup failed for <n> family types; … SGT cannot read the section of these types, so you cannot select them. [SpecFail/Writer/ExtensionParamMissing] Start/End Extension parameters are required for endpoint gaps. A girt with a gap has no extension parameters. Use another type, or set the gap to 0. <action>: [<code>] <detail> An action failed. The detail gives the reason. LIMITS An opening splits each girt that crosses it, even with all four members off. To run a girt across, drag the girt's handle at one edge of the opening to the other edge. SGT joins the two pieces into one girt. SGT leaves out a girt piece shorter than 6", with no message. Update overwrites any Start Extension or End Extension value that you type on an SGT girt. If you move or resize a detected opening, its Source becomes Manual, and SGT stops following the opening in the link. A second Super Girt Tool run on a wall places a second system. To change a system, use Edit SGT Wall. A copy of an SGT member keeps its SGT tag, so Delete System deletes it too. If Place or Update fails, the window closes and all changes of the session are lost. SEE ALSO Getting started, DBTools.SGT

user-guide/tools/tdv.html.title: Transfer Drafting Views | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/tdv.html.summary: Transfer Drafting Views NAME Transfer Drafting Views - copy drafting views between the model and a library file SYNOPSIS DB Tools > DB Tools Common > Import From Library DB Tools > DB Tools Common > Export To Library DESCRIPTION Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) works with a library: a Revit model (.rvt) that holds standard drafting views. An import copies views from a library (the source) into the active model (the destination). An export copies views from the active model into a library. Run a command and select a library. TDV opens it in the background. In the Transfer Drafting Views window, check the views to copy. Fix each name conflict, then click Transfer Selected. Each click is one transfer. Click Accept and Transfer More or Close Tool in the result. OPTIONS Control Effect View Type: Shows only the source views of one type. Search views Shows the views whose name contains the text, or its letters in the same order. Import? or Export? Includes the row in the transfer. View Name The destination name. Click it to change it. Replace Replaces the destination drafting view with the same name. View Type The destination view type. Retain Original uses the type name of the source view. A checked row has a conflict in these cases: Its name is blank. Another checked row has the same name. The destination has a drafting view with that name, and Replace is off. The check ignores case and leading or trailing spaces. SETTINGS Open DB Tools > Settings, expand Common Settings and find Library Files. Add Fallback Path adds a file that TDV uses when the main path is not valid. A path is valid when the file exists, ends in .rvt, and was saved in the Revit version that runs. TDV opens no other file, so it never upgrades a library. A cross marks an invalid path. When Revit starts, when Settings opens and when you click Save Settings, TDV checks the saved paths. One entry with no valid path turns on the warning Library Paths Invalid, which turns off both commands for all libraries. Fix or remove the entry, then click Save Settings. Validate Libraries shows the result but does not change the commands. RESULTS For each checked view, TDV makes a drafting view. With Replace, it deletes all elements of the existing view and gives that view the selected type. It copies the scale, the VIEW_DESCRIPTION parameter, the elements and their graphic overrides. It skips the categories Title Blocks, Viewports, Views, Schedules and Guide Grids. If a view fails, TDV undoes only that view and continues. Per-View Issues in the result shows its code. Cancel on the progress bar undoes the whole transfer. Each transfer of an import is one Undo step: Transfer Drafting Views. TDV then closes the library without saving. After an export, TDV saves the library if the last transfer added or replaced a view. A workshared library synchronizes with central and relinquishes all elements. Then TDV closes the library and activates your model again. MESSAGES Message Meaning and what to do DestinationTypeMissing The named type is not in the destination, or Retain Original could not make it. CopyElementsFailed Revit could not copy an element. TDV copies nothing from that view. LIMITS In an export window, only the last transfer decides the save. If it added and replaced nothing, TDV closes the library without saving, and the earlier transfers are lost. A copied element whose type name exists in the destination uses the destination type. If the destination has no type with the Retain Original name, TDV duplicates the alphabetically first destination drafting view type and gives it that name. The type keeps the properties of the duplicated type. SEE ALSO Getting started, DBTools.TDV

user-guide/tools/vtc.html.title: View Template Comparer | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/vtc.html.summary: View Template Comparer View Template Comparer (VTC) compares two view templates in the open project, side by side. For each differing setting you choose which template's value to keep. VTC then writes the result to one of the templates or to a new merged template. It can also save templates to a library and load them back. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Testing > View Template Comparer. The Testing panel is shown when Enable Testing Tools is on in the settings (the default). If the project has no view templates, the command shows No view templates found in the document. Usage Select the Left and Right templates. The Swap button exchanges them. Click a value cell in the Settings Comparison tree to choose which side wins for that row. The Inspector has Use Left, Use Right and a clear button for the selected row. For a category row, use Edit Left or Edit Right (in the Inspector, from the row, or from the context menu Edit Override...) to stage a local graphic-override edit. A staged edit is marked Edited. Review the selected rows and eligible staged edits in the Preview tab. Click Process and choose the target. Comparison tree The tree has these top-level groups: Template Parameters, Model Categories, Annotation Categories, Analytical Model Categories, Imported Categories, Filters, Filter Overrides, Revit Links, Worksets and Design Options. Control Effect Search box Filters rows by name. Filter Limits the rows by configuration (see below). Select Left / Select Right Selects all differing rows shown by the current search and filter, taking the value from that side. Wipe Clears all selections and conflict state. Filters are kept. Reset Resets the search, the view filter and the conflict filter. Expand/collapse button Expands or collapses all groups. Show: All, Conflicts, Success After Process, shows all rows, only rows that failed to apply, or only rows that applied. Context menu Select from Left (with children), Select from Right (with children), Clear selection (with children), Edit Override..., and for Revit links Open Revit Link Settings... and Copy Revit Link Settings To.... A category row or a Filter Overrides row is configured in a template when that template hides it or overrides any of its graphics. A Template Parameters row is configured when the template includes the parameter. The Filter modes are: Configured (default): rows configured in either template. Configured in Left and Configured in Right: rows configured in that template. Rows that are not category, filter-override or template-parameter rows are always shown. Select Left and Select Right select every differing row that the filter and search show. Under Configured in Left, Select Left can therefore select a row that both templates hide when only Right overrides its graphics. Processing that row to the right template keeps it hidden and clears those overrides. Process Process applies the selected rows and the eligible staged edits in one batch. A staged edit is eligible when its row has a selected side and that side is the edited side, or when its row is not in the current comparison. An edit on a visible row with no selected side, or with the other side selected, is not applied. The dialog asks Apply changes to: Option Effect Overwrite <Left name> Writes the selected values into the Left template. Overwrite <Right name> Writes the selected values into the Right template. Create Merged Template Creates a new template named in Template Name:. The name is required. A merged template starts as a copy of the Left template, so settings VTC does not compare, such as the view scale, keep the Left values. Use Swap to choose the other base. For a row that has a selected side, the target takes that side's value. When the selected side lacks the setting (it is absent there), the row in the target is reset to its default, instead of keeping the base value. This applies to categories, worksets and Revit link settings. A setting that cannot be applied is reported as a conflict, and the others are applied. Any other failure undoes the whole batch. Overwriting a template is one undo entry. Create Merged Template is one undo entry named Create Merged View Template. If it fails, no template remains, so you can retry with the same name. Imported categories Imported categories (DWG, DXF and other imports) appear under their own Imported Categories group. They use the same compare, edit, preview and process flow as other categories. Revit links Revit link settings appear under Revit Links, grouped by link. Type-level and instance-level link targets are listed separately. VTC lists only the settings that the running Revit version lets add-ins both read and write: Visibility Mode, Linked View, Filters, Nested Links, Object Styles, Color Fill, View Range, Phase, Phase Filter, Detail Level, Discipline. VTC matches links between the two templates by link name. If two links have the same name, VTC stops with an error. Action Effect Open Revit Link Settings... Opens Native Revit Link Settings for one link target. The window always lists all supported settings of that target, even if you opened it from one row. Apply to Template writes the selected settings; it is one undo entry. Copy Revit Link Settings To... Copies the supported settings to other link targets. Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter are matched by name in the target linked model. If the name is unavailable because the linked document is unloaded, the raw id is reused only when source and target reference the same linked model. The copy is one undo entry. A target that cannot accept the settings is reported and the others are copied. Any other failure leaves every target unchanged. Loading a saved template from the library also remaps Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter by name in the target linked model. If the saved name is not found there, the setting fails with a not-found error. If the snapshot holds no name (the linked document was unloaded), the stored id is reused. When only one template contains the link row, VTC uses that template. When both do and you have not selected a side, VTC asks which template to use. Library The Library tab saves template snapshots to disk and applies them back to a template. Save Template > Left Template, Right Template or Merged Template. An optional name field sets the saved name. When blank, the source template name is used. Load applies the selected saved template to the side chosen in Load to:. It first asks for confirmation, because it overwrites the template's settings in Revit. A delete button removes the selected saved template, and a refresh button reloads the list. Snapshots are stored under %APPDATA%\DBTools\Cache\VTC\. VTC creates the folder on the first save. Saved names ignore case and surrounding spaces. Saving under an existing name asks Replace saved template 'X'?; Cancel saves nothing. If VTC cannot check the name, or another Revit session saves that name during your save, the save fails and nothing is overwritten. A snapshot that is incomplete or malformed fails to load with a storage error. VTC does not repair or migrate it. If a save or delete succeeds but the list cannot refresh, VTC shows a warning that names the template. A save or delete that fails shows an error. Result Process, Apply to Template and Copy Revit Link Settings To... each make one undo entry. VTC reports each result in an alert titled View Template Comparer. Rows that failed to apply are conflicts; after Process, Show: Conflicts lists them. Messages Message Meaning No view templates found in the document. The project has no view templates. VTC does not open. Select two templates to compare first. Left or Right is not selected. Select at least one setting or make a local override edit before processing. Process has nothing to apply. Created merged template '<name>'. <n> operations completed. Create Merged Template finished with no conflict. Applied changes to '<name>'. <n> operations completed. Overwrite finished with no conflict. ... <n> operations succeeded and <n> conflicts were reported. Some rows failed to apply. Use Show: Conflicts. ... No operations succeeded and <n> conflicts were reported. No row was applied. Pending edits cleared because the template pairing changed. Changing Left or Right discarded staged edits. Pending edits cleared because the comparison was rebuilt. Refreshing the comparison discarded staged edits. Pending edits cleared during selection wipe. Wipe discarded staged edits. No category override data is available on the <Left/Right> side for this row. The row cannot be edited on that side. This Revit link exists on both Left and Right. Choose which template should <action>. Choose the template for a link command. Select a specific Revit link row or setting to open. Open Revit Link Settings... needs a link row. No supported Revit link settings were found for this node. The row has no supported link setting. No other Revit link targets are available to copy settings to. Copy Revit Link Settings To... has no target. Applied <n> Revit link settings to <name>. Apply to Template finished. A warning adds the number of settings that could not be applied. Copied Revit link settings from '<source>' to <n> target(s). The copy finished. A warning lists the failed targets. Revit link key '<key>' is ambiguous. Link names must resolve uniquely per target kind and setting. Two links have the same name. Rename one of them. Saved template '<name>' to cache., Saved merged template '<name>' to cache. The library save finished. Replace saved template '<name>'? A saved template has this name. Replace overwrites it. Apply saved template '<saved>' to '<template>'? This will overwrite the current template settings in Revit. Confirm Load. Applied '<saved>' to <template>. Load finished. Deleted saved template '<name>'. The delete finished. Failed to save template: <reason>, Failed to load template: <reason>, Failed to delete template '<name>': <reason> The library action failed and changed nothing. ... but the displayed saved-template list could not refresh. The save or delete succeeded; click the refresh button. Limitations VTC compares templates in the open project. It does not compare templates across projects, except through the library. Link settings that Revit does not let add-ins read and write are not shown. Create Merged Template copies the Left template, so use Swap to base the merge on the other template.
